Status: DRAFT r2 (revised after Codex grounded review r1, PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS). Stable sections from Codex overnight research (read, not re-derived) + eg1-model-provenance + Fluid-1 teardown. License section corrected per Codex web verification r1.

## 0. TL;DR
Fix EG-1's three measured English weaknesses — under-activation of genuine lists (esp. two-item/scoped), leftover spoken-command residue, without breaking its currently-strong restraint — by adding ~1,000 public-source-grounded, balanced English training pairs to the existing set and retraining the SAME base (Qwen3-4B) on the SAME shipped prompt via the documented QLoRA recipe. Grade the quantized artifact on the frozen English sets. Ship as a weights-only EG-1 update if it clears the predeclared bar.

## 1. Problem
Users report EG-1 is weak at exactly what makes cloud polishers popular: turning spoken lists into clean bullets and formatting email/notes structure. Codex's overnight scan makes training-data starvation the leading testable hypothesis: list examples are scarce, two-item lists are nearly absent, and prompt-only tuning caused regressions. Retrain #1 tests that hypothesis. It does not yet prove that the Qwen3-4B base has no relevant ceiling.

## 2. Goals & non-goals
### 2.1 Goals
- Raise genuine-list activation (esp. two-item + scoped-implicit) measurably (defined in §11).
- Remove leftover spoken formatting commands.
- Hold restraint (do not convert ordinary prose to lists) — currently ~100%.
- Keep core English polish non-inferior (lower bound > -2pp).
- Keep the same base + same shipped prompt + same download size (~2.7GB) → clean weights-only hot-swap.

### 2.2 Non-goals
- Multilingual (retrain #2, on top of this).
- Base-model switch (Gemma etc. benched unless this plateaus).
- Prompt-contract change (behavior in weights; promptTemplateID unchanged).
- Building the full public-speech benchmark lab (rejected over-engineering).

## 2.5 Grounding brief (evidence, read not re-derived)
**Weakness diagnosis (Codex overnight, OVERNIGHT-LOG DATA-004 / EVAL-005/006/007):**
- 259/5,656 training outputs are lists; item skew: 2-item=**3**, 3=179, 4=25, 5=30, 6=2, 7=19, 8=1.
- 80 `LF-*` + 80 `LFT-*` rows leaked from the old benchmark into training → old 94-95% headline is contaminated (82% family overlap), NOT held-out quality.
- Current EG-1 + shipped prompt: positive-list activation 72/100, 71/100 strict; two-item activation 11/20. UNDER-activates.
- Restraint currently strong: 100/100 restraint, 98/100 strict on the 100-trap set.
- Prompt-only "list-v2" boosts activation (86/100) but damages meaning, loses scope, leaves command headers, REGRESSES restraint → behavior must be trained into weights at prompt parity.

**Training pipeline (eg1-model-provenance, #1265):** Base Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507; QLoRA (Unsloth, r16/a32, lr 5e-5, 2 epochs, response-only loss) on the RTX 4090 ($0); merge → GGUF → Q5_K_M → judge the QUANTIZED artifact. Training prompt MUST equal shipped prompt (drift = ±18pp). Weights-only update keeps promptTemplateID → hot-swap.

**Ceiling context (Fluid-1 teardown):** competitor ~100k real dictations; realistic internal target 20-50k; per-behavior we are near-zero on lists → high buffer, cheap first win.

**Single-authority / negative claims:** eval harness `scripts/eval/` is the ONLY polish eval harness (never fork); new data + scorers extend in place. All new training pairs must be family-disjoint from the frozen eval sets (exact + token + char-ngram + embedding screen) — reuse the existing scanner.

## 3. Design
### 3.1 Approach
Add ~1,000 balanced English pairs (dropping the ~160 leaked `LF-*`/`LFT-*` rows so we don't re-contaminate the eval), retrain per the documented recipe under the CURRENT shipped prompt, quantize, grade on frozen sets.

New English 1,000 stratification (TRAINING-DATA-DESIGN-V2, adopted):
- 400 positive lists — item counts 2/3/5/7 balanced; list types (explicit bullets, explicit numbering, scoped-implicit, bare-label, correction/format-command) balanced; domains (work, personal, technical, medical, legal) balanced; lengths balanced.
- 400 matched prose-restraint — each paired to a positive family, same domain/length/difficulty; types: incidental enumerations, narrative sequences, compound nouns ("laptop charger"), quoted content, alternatives/contrasts, shared modifiers, two-item policy-boundary prose.
- 200 core polish — filler removal, self-correction, punctuation, entity/number/date preservation, minimal edit.
Persona slice (Finding 3): ≥100 of the 1,000 must be email-shaped and ≥100 note-shaped, under the same list/restraint balance and preservation rules.

### 3.2 Data sourcing — license rule (Codex web-verified r1; round #1 GREEN-with-conditions only)
Pin the exact source release/revision, download URL, file hashes, and license snapshot before ingestion. A source-level allowlist controls acceptance; a dataset name alone is not proof. Two paradigms: **(A) Degrade** real structured GOLD → synthesize messy spoken input; **(B) Minimal-clean** real spoken transcript INPUT → minimally-edited output that STAYS prose.

- **OASST1/OASST2 — GREEN with notice:** Apache-2.0. Carry license + applicable NOTICE attribution in the training-source notice bundle and model card. Filter quotations, code, PII, suspected third-party text. (GOLD — lists/emails/steps + prose negatives.)
- **AMI — GREEN for covered material only:** use transcription + only annotations explicitly CC-BY-4.0. Carry creator/source attribution, license link, modification notice. (INPUT — restraint pillar: narrative/incidental/compound.)
- **VoxPopuli — GREEN with restrictions:** use only VoxPopuli DATA/transcripts; NOT its CC-BY-NC code/pretrained models/separately-licensed LM data. Carry European Parliament source attribution + complete source URL (obligation, not request). (INPUT — spoken lists, cleanup.)
- **Common Voice CV11–CV16 — GREEN with access conditions:** pin the precise release, accept its terms, never attempt speaker identification, strip speaker IDs/demographics, do not redistribute the raw corpus. (INPUT — single-sentence prose negatives.)
- **FLEURS — LICENSE-GREEN BUT TRAINING-EXCLUDED:** reserve ALL FLEURS rows for the future public-speech EVAL lane so that benchmark stays disjoint. Not a training source.
- **GovInfo — PER-DOCUMENT YELLOW:** accept only material verified as authored by a federal employee within official duties, containing no third-party/contractor/transferred-copyright/covered-faculty/state-local/separately-licensed material. Record originating agency + verification basis per document. (GOLD — agendas/checklists, used sparingly with per-doc clearance.)

**Deferred/excluded:** AESLC/Enron requires actual rights clearance (founder approval alone insufficient — third-party email copyright + privacy). Stack Exchange excluded (CC-BY-SA attribution/share-alike + current AUP bars automated ML collection; note: license is by contribution date, there is no July-2024 cutoff). WikiHow excluded (CC-BY-NC-SA, non-commercial). TED-LIUM excluded (BY-NC-ND).

**Slice → source map (round #1, ~1,000 pairs):**
| Slice | Count | Paradigm | Input | Gold |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| "Make a list" | 400 | A degrade | synthesized spoken | OASST bullet/numbered answers + per-doc-cleared GovInfo |
| "Keep as prose" (matched restraint) | 400 | B + some A | AMI + VoxPopuli transcripts + OASST prose answers | minimally-cleaned prose |
| General cleanup | 200 | B | Common Voice / VoxPopuli | punctuation + caps normalized |

**W4 design guard:** the 400 restraint cases must be *matched* to the 400 list cases on surface trigger words ("and","then",commas,"first/second") so the model learns the boundary, not a keyword. AMI is the highest-value negative source.

### 3.3 Generation + acceptance
**Source realism rule:** call this corpus "public-source-grounded," not "real-dictation-grounded." OASST = chat-style clean text; AMI = mostly scenario-based meeting speech; Common Voice/VoxPopuli = read/formal speech. Before acceptance, manually audit a stratified sample of ≥100 generated pairs for ASR-reachable input, realistic dictation phrasing, minimal edits, semantic fidelity, source-style artifacts. Reject + regenerate any stratum with >5% material failures.

**Pair acceptance contract:** every accepted row records source name, exact release/revision, source document ID, source URL, source-text hash, license snapshot hash, generation-model ID, generation-prompt hash, and stratum. Acceptance requires: source-document dedup; PII/secret screening; removal of quotations, code, lyrics, embedded third-party material unless separately cleared; exact preservation of entities, numbers, dates, negation, scope, attribution, obligations; no newly generated medical/legal advice; no teacher commentary or formatting-command residue in the gold output. Both input and output sides screened. English needs NO native-human roster (multilingual concern; overnight custody machinery out of scope).

### 3.4 Prompt parity — SETTLED (founder 2026-07-16)
Train + infer against the CURRENT shipped prompt. Behavior in weights; promptTemplateID unchanged; clean hot-swap. (Rejected: adopting list-v2 as a new prompt contract — the overnight A/B showed prompt-only changes damage restraint + add residue + force a code-lane prompt-family change.)

## 11. Testing / eval — predeclared go/no-go bar (SOLE decision authority)
Run the exact shipped prompt, chat template, llama.cpp runtime flags, and quantized Q5_K_M artifact. Record prompt hash, GGUF hash, runtime build, flags.

**Primary endpoint:** on the existing 75-case positive-list A/B set, candidate strict wins minus losses ≥ 8 and two-sided exact McNemar p < 0.05.

**Mandatory safety gates:**
1. Two-item activation improves over the current 11/20, with NO candidate-only item/scope/entity/number/timing/negation/attribution/obligation loss.
2. Zero candidate-only restraint false lists; total false lists ≤ baseline; restraint strict ≥ 98/100.
3. Blind semantic review: zero candidate-only S3/S4 failures; no increase in S2+ failures.
4. Core-polish non-inferiority: lower bound of the paired 95% bootstrap CI for candidate−baseline > -2pp on the FROZEN core-polish set.
5. Frozen email/note persona slice: no candidate-only S3/S4 damage; no structural regression.

**Seeds:** train 1265, 1266, 1267. Seed 1265 is the predeclared shipping candidate; 1266/1267 test robustness and may not be used to cherry-pick a winner. All three must clear the safety gates. Only seed 1265 is opened on the final release set, once.

**Development vs release evidence (Finding 5):** the existing 75+75 / positive-100 / restraint-100 / two-item sets remain DEVELOPMENT + regression gates (already inspected during diagnosis). Before training starts, freeze ONE small final English RELEASE set from UNUSED source documents/families using the existing generator, scorer, and blind semantic-review flow — no new custody system. Do not inspect candidate outputs on it until the recipe + shipping seed are fixed. It must include lists, matched restraint, core cleanup, and email/note dictation.

Live UAT at swap: dictate real spoken lists through the app; confirm bullet output + no damage + latency < budget.

## 12. Blast radius, telemetry, and rollback
The artifact change introduces no transcript or list-content telemetry. Existing non-content telemetry must be segmented by model revision and watched for polish completion, local-polish-not-ready, inference failure, timeout, latency, download/admission failure, and user rollback/removal signals.

Rollback keeps the current artifact revision immutable and available. If the new revision fails, ship an emergency TRUSTED manifest/app update pointing to the prior shard set and hashes (manifests are bundled trust roots — rollback is not a bare manifest repoint). Never overwrite model objects in place or reuse paths with changed bytes. The delivery kill switch stops byte mutation; it is not a model-version rollback. (Matches hot-swap contract: eg1-operations.md:28, model-delivery.md:13.)

## 13. Ship criteria
Section 11 is the single go/no-go authority. Ship only when its primary endpoint, every safety gate, three-seed robustness rule, exact-runtime check, and final release-set check pass. If any gate fails, do not ship. Adjust one declared data variable, run one smoke, then one full three-seed recipe. Do not create a second scorer, benchmark authority, or parallel decision table.

If a safety layer still blocks a specific merge, surface the exact command for the founder to run once instead of silently waiting.
21. **Proactive over reactive — pave the good road, don't wall the bad one (founder rule 2026-07-02).** When preventing a class of mistake, default to making the correct pattern the effortless, discoverable, copy-paste default so the wrong thing is never authored in the first place; do NOT reach first for a blocking gate/hook/check that stops the work after the energy is already spent. A blocking guardrail is reactive by definition — it interrupts at the finish line and slows shipping — so it is at most a quiet last-ditch net behind the proactive layer, never the primary mechanism. When asked to "add a guard/hook/lint/gate," first ask what would make the mistake impossible-to-write or unnecessary, and lead with that. Applies to all projects; the specific tooling that implements it stays project-local, the principle is global. First instance: the test-timing default — guide [knowledge/dev/test-timing.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/test-timing.md) + the `~/.claude/scripts/test-timing-scan.py` authoring hook (nudges, never a CI wall).

## Scripts & Fast Paths

High-frequency commands. Depth in the linked file.

**Pull a secret / API key — GCP Secret Manager.** Prereq: `gcloud --configuration=business auth login --update-adc` (as hello@enviouslabs.co). Inside Claude (`$CLAUDECODE=1`) bare `get-key NAME` is REFUSED — use:
- `~/.claude/bin/get-key --list` — available keys
- `~/.claude/bin/get-key --check NAME` — verify access, exit 0/1, no print
- `~/.claude/bin/get-key fingerprint NAME` — SHA-256, safe to log
- `~/.claude/bin/get-key launch NAME ENV_VAR -- cmd…` — bridge value to a process, no stdout leak
→ [secrets-management.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/secrets-management.md)

**Cloud credits — AWS Bedrock ($1,120, exp 2028-04) / Azure OpenAI ($5K, exp 2027-01).** Route here before direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Keys via `get-key launch`:
- AWS: `aws-bedrock-access-key-id` + `aws-bedrock-secret-access-key`, region `us-east-1`, model IDs `us.anthropic.*`
- Azure: `azure-openai-endpoint` + `azure-openai-key`; `az` CLI needs `--tenant dcf062e4-4887-4190-b873-579cea214f6c`
→ [cloud-llm-credits.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/cloud-llm-credits.md)

**Council — GPT + Gemini second opinion.** Always background; one call fires both providers; reuse the `--session` name across rounds (never `-v2`). Absolute paths required. Use for **strategic questions only (1-2 rounds)** — pure reasoning, no repo access. Then ground the strategy against real code with Codex.
- `Bash run_in_background:true ~/.claude/bin/get-key launch gemini-api-key GEMINI_API_KEY -- ~/.claude/bin/get-key launch openai-api-key OPENAI_API_KEY -- ~/.local/bin/council ask --reasoning medium --session <kebab-topic-YYYY-MM-DD> "PROMPT"`
→ [llm-council.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/llm-council.md)

**Codex — GPT-5.x grounding against real code.** Unlike council (pure reasoning), Codex reads the actual codebase, runs commands, and validates strategy against what's really there. Read [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md) before the first Codex call in a task, including a resume. Flow: council converges on a strategy → hand Codex the plan → it checks feasibility against real files (require file:line citations) → implement. **Default path: run `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec` directly via `Bash run_in_background:true`** (fallback `codex-5.3-spark` if usage-capped — never bare `codex`, never hand-edit `~/.codex/config.toml`'s model default: [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md) RULE: two-named-scripts-not-one-mutable-default) — leaner than the subagent, the output file is yours to read for live progress, and the harness re-invokes you on exit either way (same notification). Reserve the `codex:rescue` subagent for interactive multi-round rescue where you want an agent to iterate with Codex for you. EnviousWispr uses the shell path exclusively. Effort is pinned by the script (sol → medium), prompt via stdin:
- `Bash run_in_background:true` → `cat <prompt-file> | ~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check > <out> 2>&1`
- Multi-round: capture `thread_id` from line 1, then `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec resume <UUID> "delta"` (never fresh `exec` for round 2+). If overriding sandbox, the exec-level flag goes before the subcommand: `exec --sandbox read-only resume <UUID> "delta"`. NEVER shell `&` / `</dev/null`.
→ [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md)

**Browser / DevTools — chrome-devtools-mcp.** Session startup: Cmd+Q Chrome fully → reopen → verify `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` toggle ON → start Claude. Recovery on `about:blank`: `pkill -9 -f "chrome-devtools-mcp"`.

   192	## Failures and how to do differently
   193	
   194	- Symptom: a review loop drifts toward abstract council opinions and away from the real defect set. Cause: non-grounded review is treated like evidence. Fix: reopen the real files and let file/line grounded review drive plan changes. [Task 3]
   195	- Symptom: the 5b fix starts growing into message, analytics, or dead-mic-versus-quiet-room inference work. Cause: the plan stops being about the concrete zero-sound receipt. Fix: keep the scope on the plain silence fact, the existing capture-session identity, and zero-signal-source retirement only. [Task 2]
   196	- Symptom: multilingual confidence gets overstated from one headline score or a geography proxy. Cause: the harness is English-heavy and production language fields are blank. Fix: build per-language baselines and exact-runtime tests before retraining or shipping claims. [Task 4]
   197	- Symptom: a privacy scrub or corpus refresh makes the EG-1 branch look wildly different from what actually changed. Cause: private-bundle history or renamed provenance paths contaminate the audit. Fix: compare semantic fields before assuming corpus drift, keep private snapshots ignored, and rebuild the public branch cleanly on current `origin/main` when scrub history damages ancestry. [Task 4]
   198	- Symptom: overnight/autopilot research loses experiment history after compaction. Cause: tests and numbers live only in chat. Fix: keep docs/scripts/log artifacts with the exact metrics and commands tried. [Task 4]
   199	- Symptom: a large overnight EG-1 push burns usage/time but still feels like "little visible product progress." Cause: the lane spread across benchmark invalidation, safety proofs, model scouting, and infrastructure before producing a ranked shipping candidate. Fix: present the chronology plainly, separate trust-building work from actual model-improvement work, and stop pretending the artifact volume equals product progress. [Task 4]

    10	## FACT: eg1-headline-what-it-is
    11	| Question | Answer |
    12	|---|---|
    13	| Full fine-tune or LoRA? | **QLoRA** (LoRA on the 4-bit-quantized base) — NOT a full-parameter retrain. |
    14	| Adapter shipped separately? | **No.** The LoRA adapter is **merged back into the base weights**, then converted and quantized; there is no runtime "base + adapter." Physical packaging + the current shard identity are owned by [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity (EG-1 ships as 8 componentSet GGUF shards, #1417 — not one file). |
    15	| Base model | **Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507** (Alibaba, Apache-2.0, the non-thinking variant). |
    16	| Built from scratch? | No. It is a fine-tuned **derivative** of Qwen3-4B — this is why the README says "fine-tuned derivative of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0)" and the EG-1 license applies to the *fine-tuned weights*, not the base. |
    17	| Plain-English framing for Saurabh | "We took Alibaba's Qwen 4B, taught it our dictation-cleanup behavior with a QLoRA fine-tune, and baked the result into one custom model. It's ours, but it stands on an open base." |

    33	| Division of labor | TRAIN on the PC, EVAL on the Mac (llama.cpp/Ollama + judge harness), ship the merged GGUF back over Tailscale. |

    37	## FACT: eg1-build-pipeline
    38	The end-to-end pipeline (mirror of Fluid-1's exact approach — competitor-proven):
    39	```
    40	QLoRA train (4090)  →  merge adapter into base  →  GGUF convert  →  Q5_K_M quantize  →  judge the QUANTIZED artifact
    41	```
    42	- **Judge the quantized artifact, never the fp16 checkpoint.** The shipped quality number must be measured on exactly the GGUF users run. (Q5_K_M was chosen over Q4_K_M: Q4 scored 86.5% vs Q5 88.8% on the hard-340 at bake-off; the feared Qwen-Q4 collapse did not materialize, but Q5's ~2pp edge + fewer criticals won.)
    43	- Shipped quant: **Q5_K_M, ~2.7–2.9 GB total**. Current sharded artifact identity + exact per-shard SHAs: [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity.
    44	
    45	## FACT: eg1-training-data
    46	Two data generations; **v2 is what shipped** (`train_sft_v2.jsonl`, **5,656 pairs**). Format is flat `{id, source, input(raw) → output(cleaned)}` JSONL.
    47	- **v1 (3,036 pairs):** SFT built from 1,549 Type-B-approved rows after excluding the hard-340 IDs/texts, plus founder dictations. The exclusion protected the hard-340 exact cases, not the full 1,890 working set. The 900-case overflow set stayed exact-text sealed but was derived from the same provenance families.
    48	- **v2 = v1 + 1,924 teacher-distilled real dictations** (teacher = gemini-2.5-flash + the v6 cloud prompt; hallucination-filtered, noop-capped) **+ 696 targeted convention drills.**
    49	- **Leakage correction (2026-07-15):** shipping v2 has exact ID and normalized-input overlap with **1,549/1,890** full Type B rows; conservative normalization finds 1,551. Provenance-family components expose 1,866/1,890 approved rows and 899/900 overflow rows. The old zero-overlap statement conflated the protected hard-340/exact-overflow checks with the broader working set. The old 1,890 and overflow scores are historical development/robustness evidence, not held-out quality estimates. Owner receipt: `docs/experiments/eg1-multilingual/OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md` TYPE-B-001.
    50	- **Prompt = training contract:** the model was trained AND ships with ONE fixed short system prompt + `<TRANSCRIPT>…</TRANSCRIPT>` wrapper (`scripts/eval/prompts/eg1-polish-prompt-v1.txt`, pinned by a golden-string test in `EGOnePromptBuilder`). Training prompt MUST equal inference prompt — prompt-shape drift cost ±18pp on the untuned base. This is why EG-1 gets its own `.egOneFixed` prompt family and ignores per-mode prompt rules (behavior is in the weights).
    51	
    52	## FACT: eg1-quality-and-bias-gate
    53	Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. (Numbers here are the #1265 acceptance run; note the separate marketing-vs-settings discrepancy tracked in `eg1-operations.md` FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines — 94.4/94.7 internal vs 93.7 public, same model, different run.)
    54	- **Hard-340 subset:** 94.7%, **0 critical fails** (beat the gpt-4o + v6 cloud champion same-batch: 93.5%, 2 crit).
    55	- **Full 1,890:** 94.4% (traps 97.3%, false-positive 2.4%).
    56	- **Historical one-time bias gate:** exact-text-sealed 900-overflow scored 88.0% vs untuned-base anchor 61.2%; Type-C mixed slice 94.5%; 100 train-excluded real dictations ~95%. This does not prove held-out generalization because the 2026-07-15 provenance audit found 899/900 overflow rows in training-exposed Type B families.
    57	
    58	## FACT: eg1-language-coverage-provenance
    59	- **Trained overwhelmingly on English.** The v2 corpus is English-oriented `raw → cleaned` dictation data, but it is not literally ASCII-only. The historical quality numbers above are English.
    60	- **Base is multilingual** (Qwen3-4B handles ~100+ languages) and the fixed prompt says "keep the same language … never translate," so EG-1 will *accept* and attempt to polish non-English — but that rides on base-model ability, un-benchmarked per-language. Lower-resourced languages will be rougher.
    61	- **Multilingual training pairs are an explicit v3 lever** (epic #1190 follow-ups), not shipped in EG-1 v1/v2.
    62	- Do not conflate with transcription: the ASR engines (Parakeet = English + 24 European; WhisperKit = 99) are a separate stage feeding EG-1 (`architecture.md`).
    63	
    64	## RULE: eg1-retrain-recipe-for-eg2
    65	Rule: To build EG-2 (or EG-1 v3), reuse this exact pipeline — QLoRA (Unsloth, 4090) → merge → GGUF → quantize → judge the quantized artifact against the SEALED holdout — and keep the training prompt byte-identical to the shipped prompt. A PROMPT change means a new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case (see `eg1-operations.md` RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract); a weights-only update keeps the template id.
    66	Why: prompt-shape drift alone swings quality ±18pp; judging fp16 instead of the quantized GGUF ships a number users never see.
    67	How to apply: expand data on the v2 recipe (synthetic + teacher-distilled real dictations + targeted drills), preserve zero-overlap with the eval, re-run the one-time bias gate on any new data generation, and route any prompt-family change through a code-lane PR. Distribution (R2 upload, manifest bump) is `eg1-operations.md`.
    68	Ref: #1265 method-of-record; #1190 epic.

    64	## 1. Problem
    65	Users report EG-1 is weak at exactly what makes cloud polishers popular: turning spoken lists into clean bullets and formatting email/notes structure. Codex's overnight structural scan proved the cause is a starved training diet, not a base-model ceiling.
    66	
    67	## 2. Goals & non-goals
    68	### 2.1 Goals
    69	- Raise genuine-list activation (esp. two-item + scoped-implicit) measurably.
    70	- Remove leftover spoken formatting commands ("make a bullet list of…").
    71	- Hold restraint (do not convert ordinary prose to lists) — currently ~100%.
    72	- Keep core English polish non-inferior (no worse than -2pp).
    73	- Keep the same base + same shipped prompt + same download size (~2.7GB) → clean weights-only hot-swap.
    74

    76	- Multilingual (that is retrain #2, on top of this).

    81	## 2.5 Grounding brief (evidence, read not re-derived)
    82	**Weakness diagnosis (Codex overnight, OVERNIGHT-LOG DATA-004 / EVAL-005/006/007):**
    83	- 259/5,656 training outputs are lists; item-count skew: 2-item=**3**, 3-item=179, 4=25, 5=30, 6=2, 7=19, 8=1.
    84	- 80 `LF-*` + 80 `LFT-*` rows leaked from the old benchmark into training → old 94-95% headline is contaminated (82% train/eval family overlap), NOT held-out quality.
    85	- Current EG-1 + shipped prompt: positive-list activation 72/100 (behavior), 71/100 strict; two-item activation 11/20. UNDER-activates.
    86	- Restraint currently strong: 100/100 restraint, 98/100 strict on the 100-trap set.
    87	- Prompt-only "list-v2" boosts activation (86/100) but damages meaning (split "picked up dinner"), loses scope on 5 explicit-list cases, leaves spoken-command headers, and REGRESSES restraint. → behavior must be trained into weights at prompt parity, not prompted.

    90	- Base Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507; QLoRA (Unsloth, r16/a32, lr 5e-5, 2 epochs, response-only loss) on the RTX 4090 (AlienSV, $0); merge → GGUF → Q5_K_M → judge the QUANTIZED artifact.

    95	- Held-out English dev eval sets: 75 positive-list + 75 restraint (`eg1_english_list_pilot75_v2_bundle`, leakage-clean, gitignored), plus two-item 20-case and positive-100/restraint-100 materialized prompt sets.
    96	- Intact v2 training data (5,656 pairs).

   100	### Grounding: single-authority / negative claims
   101	- Eval harness: `scripts/eval/` is the ONLY polish eval harness (never fork). New data + scorers extend it in place.
   102	- Leakage: all new training pairs must be family-disjoint from the held-out eval sets (exact + token + n-gram + embedding screen) — reuse the overnight leakage screen, not a new one.
   103	
   104	## 3. Design
   105	### 3.1 Approach
   106	Add ~1,000 new balanced English pairs to the 5,656 (dropping the ~160 leaked `LF-*`/`LFT-*` rows so we don't re-contaminate the eval), retrain per the documented recipe under the CURRENT shipped prompt, quantize, grade on held-out sets.
   107	
   108	New English 1,000 stratification (from TRAINING-DATA-DESIGN-V2, adopted):
   109	- 400 positive lists — item counts 2/3/5/7 balanced; list types (explicit bullets, explicit numbering, scoped-implicit, bare-label, correction/format-command) balanced; domains (work, personal, technical, medical, legal) balanced; lengths balanced.
   110	- 400 matched prose-restraint — each paired to a positive family, same domain/length/difficulty; restraint types: incidental enumerations, narrative action sequences, compound nouns ("laptop charger"), quoted content, alternatives/contrasts, shared modifiers, two-item policy-boundary prose.
   111	- 200 core polish — filler removal, self-correction, punctuation, entity/number/date preservation, minimal edit.
   112	
   113	### 3.2 Data sourcing — license-verified (round #1 is GREEN-license ONLY)
   114	Real content grounds one side of every pair; the other side is synthesized. Two paradigms:
   115	- **(A) Degrade:** real clean structured text = GOLD output → synthesize the messy spoken input (flatten bullets to run-on speech, inject disfluencies + spoken commands).
   116	- **(B) Minimal-clean:** real spoken transcript = INPUT → minimally-edited output that STAYS prose.
   117	
   118	**Round #1 sources — all GREEN (permit commercial ML + derivative-model distribution):**
   119	| Source | License (verified) | Side / role | Weakness |
   120	|---|---|---|---|
   121	| OpenAssistant oasst1/oasst2 | Apache-2.0 | GOLD — real bullet/numbered answers, drafted emails, matched prose answers | W1,W2,W3,W4 (primary gold pillar) |
   122	| AMI Meeting Corpus | CC-BY-4.0 | INPUT — spontaneous meeting speech; incidental enumerations, "first…then" narratives, compound nouns | W4 (primary restraint pillar), W2 |
   123	| VoxPopuli (en) | CC0-1.0 | INPUT — formal spoken monologue, some spoken lists | W1, W4, cleanup |
   124	| Common Voice CV11–CV16 | CC0 (older releases direct-download) | INPUT — clean single-sentence prose | W4, cleanup |
   125	| FLEURS (en) | CC-BY-4.0 | INPUT — read sentences | cleanup, W4 |
   126	| US federal gov docs (GovInfo/Federal Register) | Public domain (17 U.S.C. §105) | GOLD — agendas, minutes, checklists, plain-language procedures | W1, W2 |
   127	
   128	**Attribution to carry on the model card:** AMI, FLEURS (CC-BY-4.0) require attribution; VoxPopuli (CC0) requests acknowledging the European Parliament; OASST (Apache-2.0) and Common Voice (CC0) need none. Screen GovInfo docs for embedded third-party copyrighted excerpts.
   129	
   130	**DEFERRED / founder call (NOT in round #1):**
   131	- **Enron / AESLC emails** — YELLOW: FERC public record, no clean license grant. Would add real corporate-email density for W2, but round #1 covers W2 adequately via OASST drafted-email answers + GovInfo memos. Excluded from round #1; founder can approve as a round-#2 add.
   132	- **Stack Exchange** — YELLOW: pre-July-2024 dumps only (CC-BY-SA, share-alike + attribution); 2024+ dumps forbid commercial/LLM use. Low value here; skip round #1.
   133	
   134	**RED — excluded, do not re-investigate:** WikiHow (CC-BY-NC-SA, non-commercial), TED-LIUM (NC-ND), Spotify podcasts (research-only), post-2024 Stack Exchange.
   135	
   136	**Slice → source map (round #1, ~1,000 pairs):**
   137	| Slice | Count | Paradigm | Input | Gold |
   138	|---|---:|---|---|---|
   139	| "Make a list" | 400 | A degrade | synthesized spoken | OASST bullet/numbered answers + GovInfo agendas/checklists |
   140	| "Keep as prose" (matched restraint) | 400 | B + some A | AMI + VoxPopuli real transcripts (incidental/narrative/compound) + OASST prose answers | minimally-cleaned prose |
   141	| General cleanup | 200 | B | Common Voice / VoxPopuli | punctuation + caps normalized |
   142	
   143	**W4 design guard:** the 400 restraint cases must be *matched* to the 400 list cases on surface trigger words ("and", "then", commas, "first/second") so the model learns the list boundary, not a keyword. AMI is the highest-value negative source (natural "laptop, charger, and cables" compounds + "first we…then we…" narratives that must stay prose).
   144	
   145	### 3.3 Generation method
   146	Real content grounds one side; a strong teacher model (different author/critic models, per design) synthesizes the paired side into ASR-style raw input / minimally-edited gold output. Automated quality + leakage screen before acceptance. English needs NO native-human roster (that was a multilingual concern — the overnight custody/registry machinery is out of scope here).
   147	
   148	### 3.4 Prompt parity — SETTLED (founder 2026-07-16)
   149	Train + infer against the CURRENT shipped prompt. Behavior lives in weights; promptTemplateID unchanged; clean hot-swap. (Rejected: adopting list-v2 as a new prompt contract — the overnight A/B showed prompt-only changes damage restraint and add residue, and it would force a code-lane prompt-family change.)
   150

   176	## 11. Testing / eval — the go/no-go bar
   177	Grade the QUANTIZED artifact on the held-out English sets, report four axes (Codex-defined):
   178	1. Positive-list activation ↑ (esp. two-item + scoped) vs current EG-1.
   179	2. False-list restraint held (no worse than current 98/100 strict).
   180	3. Meaning damage: ZERO new S3/S4 (scope/entity/number/timing) damage.
   181	4. Core English polish non-inferior (≥ -2pp).
   182	Paired per-case strict outcomes + exact McNemar + bootstrap CI. Three training seeds before any ship claim (report each, don't average away a bad run).
   183	Live UAT at swap: dictate real spoken lists through the app, confirm bullet output + no damage + latency < budget.
   184	
   185	## 12. Blast radius & rollback
   186	Weights-only artifact swap; rollback = repoint manifest to the current EG-1 shard set. No code path change. Same download size class.

   188	## 13. Ship criteria
   189	All four eval axes pass on the quantized artifact across 3 seeds → build the ship PR (manifest/version bump + Live UAT). If restraint breaks or activation doesn't move, DO NOT ship: adjust the data balance and re-run (one smoke + one full dev run per recipe, per stop rules).

   235	## Rules
   236	
   237	Global. Every project. Project CLAUDE.md must not restate — extend or scope only.
   238	
   239	1. **Validate, don't guess.** Run the command, read the file, test the path. No assumptions stated as facts. Production-grade from day one.
   240	2. **Empirical debugging.** Hypothesis → falsifiable test → run → fix. No sweeping changes based on theory.
   241	3. **chrome-devtools-mcp first.** Default driver for any browser work. → [browser-automation.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/browser/browser-automation.md)
   242	4. **DRY.** Every fact lives in one place. Reference, don't restate.
   243	5. **Council when unsure.** Canonical invocation → [llm-council.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/llm-council.md).
   244	6. **No em-dashes or en-dashes in human-facing content.** Marketing, in-app strings, email, Discord, release notes. Use periods, commas, colons, semicolons, parens, or restructure.
   245	7. **Edit in place, never delete-and-recreate.** File ID is a primary key. Deleting breaks share links, permissions, comments, history.
   246	8. **Never ask if done.** Keep working. Saurabh decides when to stop.
   247	9. **Session wind-down.** Local session-log + Discord post via canonical script. Promote persistent infra to CLAUDE.md/knowledge before logging. → [session-wind-down.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/session/session-wind-down.md)
   248	10. **Write for machine reading.** Every token taxes every future session. Optimize for grep retrieval. → [writing-style.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/writing-style.md)
   249	11. **Match existing style; diff every edit.** If diff is larger than the change, stop and investigate.
   250	12. **Discord webhooks: use canonical script; read webhook contract first.** → [discord-webhooks.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/session/discord-webhooks.md)
   251	13. **Plan before non-trivial code.** Don't jump to code on non-trivial work — plan it and get an explicit "go" first; each project's own workflow rules govern how rigorous (council, gates, validation). "Auto mode" after approval grants the full build/test/review loop without check-ins, but never a new design decision — if the design must change, stop and re-approve.
   252	14. **Complete or doesn't ship.** Migrations and refactors ship complete: old code removed and new code wired in the same change, no forwarding shims or "clean up later" follow-ups. Too big to ship complete means split the scope smaller, not the completion.
   253	15. **No unauthorized cloud spend.** Verify with Saurabh before any cloud spend. If a plan requires spend, document the amount and his approval in the written plan to avoid mid-execution blockers.
   254	16. **Don't fake-narrate async work.** Report a terminal status as done; say you're "watching" / "I'll report back" only when a real watcher (ScheduleWakeup, Monitor, non-terminal background task) exists; before promising a result, confirm the watcher notifies on both success and failure. → classification table [async-watchers.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/async-watchers.md)
   255	17. **Grep the knowledge base before researching.** Before researching, reverse-engineering, or building a solution from scratch, grep `~/.claude/knowledge/` and the project's `.claude/knowledge/` — it's very likely already documented. Never answer from training data when a knowledge file covers the topic.
   256	18. **Review to an explicit all-clear before "done."** Self-audit every non-trivial artifact (code, plan, migration) to clean, then run it through the last reviewer (Codex for code/plans) and iterate to an EXPLICIT approval on a confirming re-run — merely folding the previous round's findings is NOT approval. Nothing is done, shipped, deployed, merged, or pushed until that gate passes; a green build or passing live test is necessary but never a substitute for the review sign-off.
   257	19. **No AI attribution in git.** Never add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer to commit messages or a "Generated with Claude Code" line to PR bodies. This OVERRIDES the Claude Code harness default that re-injects those instructions every session (founder decision 2026-07-01). Applies to all projects. Commit/PR content only — unrelated to code comments, which follow surrounding style.

Do not park work "awaiting founder merge" or treat merging as needing fresh approval: the review gate IS the approval; merging is mechanical. If a safety layer still blocks a specific merge, surface the exact command for the founder to run once instead of silently waiting.
   259	21. **Proactive over reactive — pave the good road, don't wall the bad one (founder rule 2026-07-02).** When preventing a class of mistake, default to making the correct pattern the effortless, discoverable, copy-paste default so the wrong thing is never authored in the first place; do NOT reach first for a blocking gate/hook/check that stops the work after the energy is already spent. A blocking guardrail is reactive by definition — it interrupts at the finish line and slows shipping — so it is at most a quiet last-ditch net behind the proactive layer, never the primary mechanism. When asked to "add a guard/hook/lint/gate," first ask what would make the mistake impossible-to-write or unnecessary, and lead with that. Applies to all projects; the specific tooling that implements it stays project-local, the principle is global. First instance: the test-timing default — guide [knowledge/dev/test-timing.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/test-timing.md) + the `~/.claude/scripts/test-timing-scan.py` authoring hook (nudges, never a CI wall).

   499	## Codex Issue Preflight
   500	
   501	Before claiming or implementing any GitHub issue, Codex must run a short preflight and write down the result in its working notes or issue comment if useful:
   502	
   503	1. Refresh the exact issue with comments: `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,state,labels,comments` (on a non-TTY pipe, bare `--comments` prints only the comments and prints nothing when the issue has zero comments — deliberate gh behavior since v1.4.0, not a regression; use JSON to return the body and comments together).
   504	2. Check current open PRs: `gh pr list --state open --limit 40 --json number,title,headRefName,url`.
   505	3. Check whether the work already landed on `main`: search recent commits and grep the named files.
   506	4. Decide the issue shape before editing:
   507	   - direct code PR
   508	   - tracker cleanup / child issue creation
   509	   - already complete and ready to close
   510	   - research experiment only
   511	5. Only add `in-progress` after the issue still clearly needs Codex work.
   512	
   513	For experiment issues, use a hard stop rule: one smoke run, one full benchmark, then stop unless the result improves the target metric without meaningful regressions. Do not hand-tune repeatedly in the same PR lane after the benchmark says the shape is weak.
   514	
   515	When a PR is opened and Codex is no longer actively editing that issue, remove the `in-progress` label or leave a clear issue comment saying it is waiting on PR review.

   517	## Codex Review Defaults
   518	
   519	For Codex review work, match Claude Code's Codex setup — two named, model-pinned scripts, never the bare `codex` binary and never a hand-edited `~/.codex/config.toml` default (`~/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md` RULE: two-named-scripts-not-one-mutable-default):
   520	
   521	```bash
   522	~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol review --base origin/main
   523	```
   524	
   525	Fallback if `codex-5.6-sol` errors with a usage-limit message: `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.3-spark review --base origin/main` (pins high effort). Both scripts already pin their own reasoning effort — do not add a competing `-c model_reasoning_effort=...`.
   526	
   527	The canonical EW flow commits the work first, then reviews the committed diff (`workflow-process.md` RULE: local-codex-iteration-before-push). A PreToolUse gate (`.claude/scripts/check-selfreview-before-codex.sh`) blocks `codex review` until the HEAD commit message carries the single-authority self-audit (`Self-audit-grep:` / `Self-audit-owner:`). For an ad-hoc uncommitted review (`--uncommitted`) the self-audit is not yet in a commit, so either commit first (preferred) or bypass with `SKIP_SELFAUDIT=1` (audit-logged).
   528	
   529	If `codex-5.6-sol` errors on the model itself (not a usage-limit message), treat that as a CLI/version mismatch and report it plainly — do not silently fall back to Spark for a non-capacity reason.
   530	
   531	**Every finding you report ships its fix.** Give the exact replacement text — real code in the file's language, or verbatim prose for a doc — not a description of the change. If you genuinely cannot write it, mark the finding `DIAGNOSIS-ONLY` and say why in one line. The author adjudicates: adopts, modifies (and tells you what changed), or rejects with evidence. A finding without proposed text is incomplete.
   532	
   533	**If your current task is reviewing a git diff, read `docs/codex-diff-review.md` first.** It is short, and it is the protocol. Do not apply it while writing code, answering a question, or reviewing a plan — the default there is the smallest correct change, not consolidation.
   534	
   535	A scoped `codex review` (`--base` / `--uncommitted` / `--commit`) cannot accept a custom prompt; the target is an enum and the prompt is one of its variants. This file is the only channel that reaches the diff reviewer, which is why the pointer lives here.
   536	
   537	For grounded reviews, the canonical Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 review contract lives in `.claude/rules/workflow-process.md` (§5 and the grounded-review mechanics). Model + reasoning effort are pinned by `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol` / `codex-5.3-spark`, not by this repo's `.codex/config.toml` (that file only sets `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` — it has no model/effort keys; do not assume it can override the two-script default).

   547	gh issue close <N> --comment "reason" # Complete work
   548	```
   549	
   550	## Non-Interactive Shell Commands
   551	
   552	**ALWAYS use non-interactive flags** with file operations to avoid hanging on confirmation prompts.
   553	
   554	Shell commands like `cp`, `mv`, and `rm` may be aliased to include `-i` (interactive) mode on some systems, causing the agent to hang indefinitely waiting for y/n input.
   555	
   556	**Use these forms instead:**
   557	```bash
   558	# Force overwrite without prompting
   559	cp -f source dest           # NOT: cp source dest
   560	mv -f source dest           # NOT: mv source dest
   561	rm -f file                  # NOT: rm file
   562	
   563	# For recursive operations
   564	rm -rf directory            # NOT: rm -r directory
   565	cp -rf source dest          # NOT: cp -r source dest
   566	```
   567	
   568	**Other commands that may prompt:**
   569	- `scp` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` for non-interactive
   570	- `ssh` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` to fail instead of prompting
   571	- `apt-get` - use `-y` flag
   572	- `brew` - use `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` env var

   591	5. **Submit work**: push the branch and open a PR when the task needs review.
   592	6. **Complete**: close the issue only when the requested work is truly done, or leave a clear issue comment if Claude Code / Saurabh still need to review or merge.

   595	
   596	- Use GitHub Issues for ALL persistent task tracking
   597	- Always assign priority and type labels to new issues

   600	- TaskCreate/TaskList are for intra-session steps only

   603	
   604	**When ending an implementation work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Local work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.
   605	
   606	**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**
   607

   609	2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
   610	3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, or comment on in-progress items with exact next steps
   611	4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   612	   ```bash
   613	   git pull --rebase
   614	   git push
   615	   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   616	   ```
   617	5. **Open or update PR when appropriate** - Submit the PR, but do not merge it unless Saurabh explicitly asked for that merge
   618	6. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
   619	7. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
   620	8. **Hand off** - Provide context for Saurabh, Claude Code, or the next session
   621	
   622	**CRITICAL RULES:**
   623	- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
   624	- NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
   625	- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
   626	- If push fails, resolve and retry until it succeeds

   663	## Compatibility (know this cold)
   664	
   665	**Runs on macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, Apple Silicon only (M1+). No Intel.**
   666	
   667	- **Core dictation** (record, transcribe, paste) works on the entire supported range. It never requires macOS 26.
   668	- **The built-in Apple Intelligence polish option requires macOS 26+.** It calls Apple's FoundationModels framework (`SystemLanguageModel`), which only exists on macOS 26. This is NOT the same thing as "Apple Intelligence the consumer feature," which shipped in macOS 15.1: third-party apps had no way to invoke the on-device model until FoundationModels arrived in 26. Do not "correct" our macOS-26 lines to 15.1.
   669	- **Below macOS 26**, Apple Intelligence polish is unavailable and the text falls back to raw SILENTLY. `frameworkUnavailable` IS in the silent-skip set (the `isSilentPolishSkip` switch in `Sources/EnviousWisprPipeline/TextProcessingRunner.swift`, alongside `.unsupportedInputLanguage` / `.outputLanguageDrift`), so a genuine pre-26 user gets raw text with no "polish failed" pill (fixed; #1080 closed 2026-06). The user can pick Ollama (on-device) or bring an OpenAI / Gemini key. Cloud polish and Ollama work on the full range.
   670	- **Proof:** the code is compile- and run-time gated to macOS 26 (`AppleIntelligenceConnector.swift`); telemetry confirms 100% of genuine Apple Intelligence polish users run macOS 26.x (90d). Engineering detail: `.claude/knowledge/llm-contract.md`.

   672	## How this project works
   673	
   674	Saurabh is founder; Claude is CTO and sole implementer. Every update is exec-level, plain English, one question at a time. No class/file names, paths, or engineering acronyms in chat — they belong in tool calls and commits.

   676	## Principles
   677	
   678	- **Heart & Limbs.** Critical path (audio, ASR, paste) must never fail. Features (Custom Words, LLM polish, filler removal) are limbs: enhance with timeouts and fallback. If a limb fails, the user gets raw text.
   679	- **Full functionality at maximum speed.** Sub-second pipeline latency target. 60-minute graceful cap (#1060), but designed for dictation, not long-form recording.
   680	- **Production-grade from day one.** No band-aid fixes, no shortcuts that trade today's speed for tomorrow's debt.

   833	# Gotchas & Non-Obvious Patterns
   834	## FACT: pathway-loaded-gotchas
   835	| Scope | File |
   836	|---|---|
   837	| Swift compiler patterns (FluidAudio qualification, `@preconcurrency`, CFString literals, `nonisolated(unsafe)`) | `.claude/rules/swift-patterns.md` |
   838	| Audio / streaming / AVAudioEngine / VAD / overlay | [`gotchas-audio.md`](gotchas-audio.md) |
   839	| Release / signing / notarization / CI / Sparkle | [`gotchas-release.md`](gotchas-release.md) |
   840	| LLM polish contract invariants | [`llm-contract.md`](llm-contract.md) |
   841	| WhisperKit-specific traps | [`whisperkit-research.md`](whisperkit-research.md) § Non-Obvious Traps |
   842	| Incident response runbooks | [`incident-response.md`](incident-response.md) |
   843	## RULE: carbon-hotkey-after-nsapp-run
   844	Rule: Register Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey` only from `applicationDidFinishLaunching` or later, never before.
   845	Why: Earlier registration returns `noErr` (success) but events are silently never delivered.
   846	Ref: `AppLifecycleCoordinator.runDidFinishLaunching()` → `DictationRuntime.startHotkeyServiceIfEnabled()` → `HotkeyController.startIfEnabled()`.
   847	## RULE: cgevent-needs-axtrust
   848	Rule: CGEvent-based paste needs Accessibility trust to deliver. The shipped path (`PasteService.dispatchCmdV()`) posts Cmd+V via a `.combinedSessionState` source through `.cgAnnotatedSessionEventTap`; `pasteToActiveApp()` reads `AXIsProcessTrusted()` for telemetry, NOT as a per-call gate — the app-level mandatory-Accessibility onboarding (#735/#736) is what guarantees delivery.
   849	Why: On macOS 14+, posted events silently never deliver without Accessibility, regardless of tap level.
   850	Ref: `PasteService.pasteToActiveApp()` / `PasteService.dispatchCmdV()`.
   851	## RULE: modifier-only-needs-accessibility
   852	Rule: Any modifier-only hotkey default MUST be paired with Accessibility-mandatory onboarding (#735); chord defaults via Carbon do not need this.
   853	Why: Global flags-changed monitors silently fail outside the app without Accessibility; Carbon chord paths do not.
   854	Ref: PR #736.
   855	## RULE: permission-status-prompt-only
   856	Rule: Treat `permission.status=granted` for Accessibility with care; `dictation.completed` is the cleanest proxy for "ended up granted".
   857	Why: TWO emit paths now — `requestAccessibilityAccess()` (`PermissionsService.swift`) on explicit prompt, AND `refreshAccessibilityStatus()` (`PermissionsService.swift`, granted in `refreshAccessibilityStatus()`) with `context:"changed"` when the background poll detects a System-Settings grant. So `permission.status=granted` is no longer purely explicit-prompt-only, and Settings grants are no longer invisible.
   858	Ref: 2026-05-15 #733 funnel analysis.
   859	## RULE: activate-ignoring-other-apps-dead
   860	Rule: Use `PasteService.forceActivateApp(pid:)` (sets `"AXFrontmost"` as CFString via AX API) for Tier 2 paste-back activation; do not use `.activateIgnoringOtherApps`.
   861	Why: macOS 14+ ignores the `activateIgnoringOtherApps` flag for LSUIElement apps, breaking paste-back entirely.
   862	Ref: `PasteService.forceActivateApp(pid:)`.
   863	## RULE: audio-constants-from-architecture
   864	Rule: Use `architecture.md` Audio Constants for the canonical capture format, tap sizing, VAD chunking, and pre-roll policy; call `SilenceDetector.reset()` (resets stream state to `.initial()`) before every new session.
   865	Why: Stale VAD state corrupts the next recording.
   866	Ref: [architecture.md](architecture.md) Audio Constants (canonical values); runtime VAD thresholds + filtering + state machine behavior live in [pipeline-mechanics.md](pipeline-mechanics.md) `vad-config-and-filtering`.
   867	## RULE: keychain-two-backends
   868	Rule: Release builds use Apple Keychain (`com.enviouswispr.app.api-keys` service); DEBUG/dev/unrecognized bundles use `~/.enviouswispr-keys/` (0700 dir, 0600 files); never UserDefaults, never log keys, never delete files in `~/.enviouswispr-keys/` (rotate by overwriting).
   869	Why: Wrong storage leaks keys; deletion breaks app and MCP connectors that share the directory.
   870	Ref: `KeychainManager`.
   871	## RULE: ollama-silent-failure
   872	Rule: Before debugging polish code, check Ollama binary existence, then reachability at `http://localhost:11434`, then model availability.
   873	Why: When `ollama serve` is down, polish silently fails under the strict readiness timeout.
   874	Ref: `OllamaSetupService`.
   875	## RULE: tccutil-bundle-id-scope
   876	Rule: Always scope `tccutil reset` to a bundle ID — `com.enviouswispr.app` for prod, `com.enviouswispr.app.dev` for dev; never blanket-reset Accessibility.
   877	Why: Bare `tccutil reset Accessibility` wipes permissions for ALL apps system-wide, breaking window managers, automation tools, screen readers.
   878	How to apply: If TCC stops persisting, verify cert (`security find-identity -v -p codesigning | grep "EnviousWispr Dev"`) and bundle ID (`plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw "build/EnviousWispr Local.app/Contents/Info.plist"`); on dev+prod conflict, quit both, reset both bundle IDs, reboot, re-grant production first then drag dev `.app` into System Settings.
   879	Ref: [distribution.md](distribution.md) § Dev Certificate.
   880	## RULE: uat-runner-background-only
   881	Rule: Run `python3 Tests/RuntimeUAT/uat_runner.py run` with `run_in_background: true`; retrieve via `TaskOutput`.
   882	Why: Foreground UAT silently fails (listing via `uat_runner.py list` is fine in foreground).
   883	Ref: `Tests/RuntimeUAT/uat_runner.py`.
   884	## RULE: asr-backend-unload-before-swap
   885	Rule: Only one ASR backend is active at a time; always unload the active backend → swap → warm the new backend (`ASRManager.switchBackend(to:)` unloads+swaps, then `EngineCoordinator.startWarm(for:)` / `ensureEngineWarm(reason: .engineSwap)` warms it).
   886	Why: Two active backends corrupt lifecycle ownership.
   887	Ref: `ASRManager.switchBackend(to:)`; `EngineCoordinator.startWarm(for:)`.
   888	## RULE: ui-state-via-named-homes
   889	Rule: Route UI-facing pipeline state via `LiveRecordingState.pipelineState` / `LiveRecordingState.currentTranscript`, post-recording error via `LastRecordingResult.polishError`, and reset via `DictationRuntime.resetActivePipeline()`; never reach into a concrete pipeline's `.state` / `.lastPolishError` / `.reset()`.
   890	Why: Direct pipeline access bypasses WhisperKit when it is the active backend.
   891	Ref: 2026-03-22 audit Q2/Q20.
   892	## RULE: accessibility-monitoring
   893	Rule: `PermissionsService.startMonitoring()` polls Accessibility using `TimingConstants.accessibilityPollIntervalSec` (`Constants.swift`) and calls `refreshAccessibilityStatus()` to catch runtime revocation; `resetAccessibilityWarningDismissal()` re-arms the warning banner. Note: `AppLifecycleCoordinator.runDidBecomeActive()` does NOT refresh on activate — the background poll is the live mechanism.
   894	Why: Users can revoke Accessibility at runtime.
   895	Ref: `PermissionsService.startMonitoring()` (`PermissionsService.swift`).
   896	## RULE: nsscreen-guard-first
   897	Rule: Guard `NSScreen.screens.first` with `guard let` or `??`; never force-index `NSScreen.screens[0]`.
   898	Why: Display sleep/wake, monitor disconnect/reconnect, and window-server transitions return an empty `NSScreen.screens` array — `[0]` crashes with index-out-of-bounds.
   899	Ref: `NSScreen.screens`.
   900	## RULE: no-cp-into-worktree
   901	Rule: Apply deltas to a worktree via `git diff -- <file>` + `git apply`; never `cp` files from the root checkout into a worktree.
   902	Why: Root may contain unstaged changes from prior sessions; copying silently includes them in the worktree branch commit.
   903	Ref: PR #109 CI failure.
   904	## RULE: foundationmodels-build-gate
   905	Rule: The required PR gate `build-check` must depend on a `macos-26` lane (`latest-stable` Xcode) that compile-probes FoundationModels; post-#906 that lane is `build-release` in `pr-check.yml` (standalone probe, `build-check` aggregates both lanes). `main-post-merge.yml` has an SDK-version guard (`macOS SDK 26.0+ required`) + Release build, but NOT a standalone `#if canImport(FoundationModels)` compile probe.
   906	Why: `#if canImport(FoundationModels)` is compile-time — missing SDK silently strips AI code and ships unexplained polish failure; after the #906 split `build-check` is an aggregator, so the probe lives on the release lane, not the gate job itself.
   907	Ref: PR #712 (2026-05-09); #906 (2026-05-29).
   908	## RULE: xcode-test-entrypoint
   909	Rule: Run logic tests through `scripts/xcode-test.sh`, never raw `swift test`. The wrapper drives `xcodebuild test` against the generated Tuist project (`-project EnviousWispr.xcodeproj -scheme EnviousWispr -configuration Debug`, arm64) with a "Test run with N test" executed-count guard; `--release` opts into the full release-config test RUN locally (mirrors `main-post-merge.yml`, Release config, `ENABLE_TESTABILITY=YES`) — useful for reproduction, though the PR `build-check` gate itself now compiles (not runs) both Release test targets on its own (#1539). Still wrap `#if DEBUG`-gated symbols (`TelemetryService.testEventHook`, `CapturedTelemetryEvent`) in `#if DEBUG` in the test file.
   910	Why: Raw `swift test` no longer proves the shipped app/XPC/resource topology; release-lane runs catch `#if DEBUG`-symbol compile errors.
   911	Enforced (nudge, not a block): `.claude/scripts/check-swift-build-gate.sh` (PreToolUse Bash) fires on raw `swift test` or `swift build -c release` and points here; conventions.md RULE: xcode-build-engine-cli owns the enforcement detail.
   912	Ref: #913 PR7; [ci-pipeline.md](ci-pipeline.md). (was: never-raw-swift-test, PR #610.)
   913	## RULE: xcode-test-script-path-must-match-worktree
   914	Rule: Invoke `scripts/xcode-test.sh` using the SAME worktree's own path you're testing (relative `scripts/xcode-test.sh` from inside that worktree, or that worktree's absolute path) — never the root checkout's absolute path from inside a feature worktree.
   915	Why: The script derives `PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"` from its OWN invocation path (`$0`), not `cwd` (`scripts/xcode-test.sh:19`). Invoking root's absolute script path from a worktree silently `cd`s into and tests ROOT's checkout instead — full "TEST SUCCEEDED" output, plausible test count, zero of your new tests actually run, no error of any kind.
   916	How to apply: From a worktree, run `./scripts/xcode-test.sh` (relative) or the worktree's own absolute path; if unsure which ran, `grep -c "<your new test name>" <log>` — a genuine 0 with "TEST SUCCEEDED" means it tested the wrong checkout, not that your test was skipped.
   917	Ref: #1392/#1393 (2026-07-11); distinct from tools-and-apps.md RULE: claude-scripts-absolute-path-from-worktrees (that one covers gitignored `.claude/scripts/` returning a silent no-op; this one covers tracked `scripts/` silently testing the wrong checkout).
   918	## RULE: xcode-rebuild-relaunch
   919	Rule: After any change needing runtime validation, run `/wispr-rebuild-and-relaunch` (→ `scripts/build-dev-app.sh`: quit ALL running dev instances by `EnviousWispr Local.app` executable path → Tuist generate → xcodebuild the `EnviousWispr-Dev` scheme → self-signed → copy to `build/EnviousWispr Local.app` → relaunch → verify by worktree path); `/wispr-run-smoke-test` is compile-only.
   920	Why: Users validate the bundled `build/EnviousWispr Local.app`, not a raw `swift build` binary. Only one dev EW runs at a time (founder 2026-07-01). Dev and prod share the `EnviousWispr` executable name, so cleanup is scoped to `EnviousWispr Local.app` paths — never `pkill -x EnviousWispr`, never a bundle-ID quit (the `.dev` id is shared across worktrees).
   921	Ref: #913 PR4/PR7. (was: stale-binary-rebuild-relaunch, PR #109.)
   922	## RULE: xcode-build-after-commit-for-push-gate
   923	Rule: When a ship-path (`Sources/`/`Tests/`/`Package.swift`/`Project.swift`/`Tuist.swift`) commit must pass the push-freshness gate (`.claude/scripts/check-push-discipline.sh`: newest of `build/EnviousWispr Local.app/Contents/MacOS/EnviousWispr` and `.derivedData/Dev/Build/Products/Dev/EnviousWispr Local.app/Contents/MacOS/EnviousWispr` executable mtime ≥ HEAD commit epoch), run `scripts/build-dev-app.sh` AFTER committing — building first then committing leaves the executable older than the commit and the gate blocks the push.
   924	Why: The gate keys freshness to the Xcode dev-build outputs (PR4), not a SwiftPM `.build` binary. Never `SKIP_PUSH_CHECKS=1` to dodge it (banned guardrail bypass).
   925	How to apply: `git commit --amend` (the standard post-Codex-review fix) bumps the committer epoch past your last build and re-blocks the push. A plain rebuild does NOT fix it when no Swift source changed: the content-aware build system skips the relink so the artifact mtime stays stale, and `touch`ing a source with unchanged content does NOT force a recompile. Force a genuine relink by `rm -rf` the built `.app` (BOTH the DerivedData product `.derivedData/Dev/Build/Products/Dev/EnviousWispr Local.app` AND the `build/` copy), then re-run `scripts/build-dev-app.sh` (object files stay cached → fast relink, not a full recompile). When checking freshness by hand, stat the bundle EXECUTABLE (`Contents/MacOS/EnviousWispr`), not the `.app` dir — the dir mtime stays stale across incremental builds and will fool you.
   926	Ref: 2026-05-30 PR #908; #913 PR4/PR7; 2026-06-07 PR #1016 (amend/relink trap re-confirmed). (was: build-after-commit-for-push-gate; spm-never-rm-build-dir deleted — `.build` is no longer the canonical build dir.)

   929	# Engineering Conventions
   930	Production-breaking rules live in [gotchas.md](gotchas.md); workflow policy lives in [`.claude/rules/workflow-process.md`](../rules/workflow-process.md).
   931	## RULE: xcode-build-engine-cli
   932	Rule: Build EnviousWispr with Xcode's build engine driven from the CLI via the committed Tuist manifests (`Project.swift` / `Tuist.swift`). Do not commit the generated `.xcodeproj` / `.xcworkspace`, and do not treat raw `swift build` / `swift test` as the build or test path for the app, XPC services, release archive, or repo test gate.
   933	Why: The SwiftPM-only path could not place Core ML / SwiftPM resources where the generated `Bundle.module` accessor resolves them in a signed `.app` (#913). Xcode owns app + 2 XPC + test + resource assembly; Tuist keeps it reproducible and CLI-only with no committed project files. (`swift build` of the package products still compiles as an informal quick sanity check, but it is not the canonical build and never produces the shippable bundle.)
   934	How to apply: Dev bundle → `scripts/build-dev-app.sh` (Tuist generate → xcodebuild `EnviousWispr-Dev`/`Dev` config → `build/EnviousWispr Local.app`); logic tests → `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; release DMG → `scripts/build-release-dmg.sh <version>`. Kill old dev processes by `EnviousWispr Local.app` executable path (ALL dev instances — one dev EW at a time, founder 2026-07-01), never `pkill -x EnviousWispr` (dev and prod share the `EnviousWispr` executable name). Enforced (nudge, not a block): `.claude/scripts/check-swift-build-gate.sh` (PreToolUse Bash) fires on raw `swift test` or `swift build -c release`/`--configuration release` and points at the real script; plain `swift build` (debug, with or without `--target`) stays silent as the allowed sanity check. The real wall is downstream: `check-push-discipline.sh` keys push freshness to the Xcode-engine artifact's mtime, so a raw swift build/test can never silently satisfy Definition of Done even if the nudge is ignored.
   935	Ref: [xcode-build-tooling.md](xcode-build-tooling.md); [gotchas.md](gotchas.md) RULE: xcode-test-entrypoint; 2026-07-11 (this session caught itself using `swift build -c release` as the release gate, no hook existed).
   936	## FACT: commit-style
   937	Conventional commits: `type(scope): message`, squash-merged. Types: `feat` / `fix` / `refactor` / `docs` / `chore` / `test` / `perf`. Scopes: `asr` / `audio` / `ui` / `llm` / `pipeline` / `settings` / `hotkey` / `vad` / `build` / `user` / `release`. Example: `feat(hotkey): chord default for fresh installs`.
   938	## RULE: di-narrow-homes
   939	Rule: Inject the narrow `@Environment` home a view needs (e.g. `LiveRecordingState`); never add a broad cross-domain state object and read it as `<object>.<domain>...`.
   940	Why: That god-object pattern is what made AppState the deletion target of epic #763.
   941	How to apply: Settings changes route through `PipelineSettingsSync.handleSettingChanged()`; AppState is freeze-test blocked from reintroduction; full decision tree in [state-ownership.md](state-ownership.md).
   942	Ref: epic #763.
   943	## RULE: settings-persistence
   944	Rule: Persist non-sensitive settings via `UserDefaults.standard` with `didSet`; persist API keys via `KeychainManager` (Apple Keychain for release `com.enviouswispr.app`, file storage at `~/.enviouswispr-keys/` for DEBUG/dev/unrecognized bundles, failing closed).
   945	Why: Failing closed means UAT and beta builds never touch the production Keychain.
   946	Ref: [gotchas.md](gotchas.md) RULE: keychain-two-backends.
   947	## FACT: view-patterns
   948	- Settings tab body: `SettingsContentView { ... }` (branded ScrollView wrapper in `SettingsComponents.swift`; replaced `Form { }.formStyle(.grouped)`).
   949	- Main window: one unified window — `UnifiedWindowView` (`SettingsView.swift`), a `NavigationStack` + custom `HStack` whose sidebar is a `ScrollView` of button rows (NOT a `NavigationSplitView`/`List` — that was replaced for macOS-26 sizing; the sidebar renders as `AXButton`s, uat-testing.md #1296) driven by the `SettingsSection` enum (History + every settings tab); onboarding is a separate `Window(id: "onboarding")`.

   955	Why: It is the SoT; ad-hoc choices drift the brand.

   963	## RULE: logging-convention
   964	Rule: Use `AppLogger.shared` actor (always `await` at call site) via `log(_:level:category:)`; never log secrets.
   965	Why: Single actor avoids duplicate sink setup; secrets in logs leak in CI artifacts.
   966	How to apply: Levels `.verbose` / `.debug` / `.info`; categories `"Pipeline"` / `"LLM"` / `"Audio"` / `"PipelineTiming"`; the ENTIRE log pipeline (OSLog + file sink) is `#if DEBUG`-only — release builds are dead code, no output; in DEBUG, OSLog receives every call and the file sink at `~/Library/Logs/EnviousWispr/app.log` (5×10MB rotation) is active only when debug mode is enabled; `CORRECTION_DEBUG` category traces RAW ASR → WordCorrector → Filler Removal → LLM Polish per utterance.
   967	Ref: PR #85.

   969	Rule: Never call `safeReply(error as NSError)` in `ASRServiceHandler` (the sole remaining XPC service handler after #1543 collapsed audio capture in-process); always pass error paths through `XPCErrorSanitizer.sanitizeForXPC(error)` with the `// XPC error sanitization boundary.` anchor comment.
   970	Why: Unsanitized NSError userInfo can SIGABRT the helper during XPC encode.
   971	How to apply: `scripts/check-xpc-error-hygiene.sh` enforces this in CI.
   972	Ref: issue #297.

   977	Why: Ship-path `.claude/` links break on GitHub, fresh clones, and cloud worker prompts.
