   982	# GitHub — Everyday Essentials (auto-loaded subset)
   983	Daily-work subset: finding issues, running PRs, and the git-safety systems that stop wrong commands. Full reference (branch protection detail, CI internals, releases, dependabot, codeowners, runner migration, SPM cache): [github.md](github.md) — read on demand before release / CI / workflow work.
   984	
   985	## FACT: lane-first-question
   986	The first question for any edit: tracked in git, or gitignored? Verify in 5s — `git check-ignore -v <path>`: nothing returned = tracked = full GitHub process; a match = gitignored = direct edit, no PR possible (that is the `Docs/dev-tooling` lane, not a "Local" lane — no such lane exists).
   987	
   988	Lane names, globs, obligations, artifacts: `phase3-validation.md` FACT: lane-obligations (sole owner). When Codex is still required on gitignored work: `workflow-process.md` FACT: lane-classification. Neither is restated here.
   989	
   990	## FACT: finding-issues
   991	Read an issue WITH its comments — always `--json`, never bare `--comments`. On a non-TTY pipe `--comments` prints ONLY the comments (it drops the body and metadata) and prints nothing at all when the issue has zero comments, so it can read as an empty success. This is deliberate `gh` behavior since v1.4.0 (cli/cli#2462), not a bug and not a 2.92.0 regression — a cli/cli maintainer confirmed this on issue #13452 (the one we filed). The `--json` form returns body + comments together regardless of TTY:
   992	`gh issue view <N> --json title,body,state,labels,comments`
   993	| Action | Command |
   994	|---|---|
   995	| List open work | `gh issue list --state open` |
   996	| List active | `gh issue list --label "in-progress"` |
   997	| List epics | `gh issue list --label "epic" --state open` |
   998	| Issues in epic | `gh issue list --milestone "Smart Polish v2"` |
   999	| Claim | `gh issue edit <N> --add-label "in-progress"` |
  1000	| Comment | `gh issue comment <N> --body "..."` |
  1001	| Close | `gh issue close <N> --comment "Reason: what was done, PR #, validation status"` |
  1002	| Create | `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..." --label "P2-medium,feature" --milestone "Epic Name"` |
  1003	
  1004	Every issue needs a priority label (P0-critical … P4-backlog) and a type label (epic/feature/bug/task/research). Children of an epic get the epic's milestone; standalone issues get none. GitHub Issues are the persistent tracker; TaskCreate/TaskList are intra-session only.
  1005	
  1006	## RULE: pr-workflow
  1007	Rule: Feature branch from `origin/main` (worktree if concurrent sessions); implement + commit (conventional commits); push; open PR; clear the cloud-review gate; THEN arm `--auto`; watch to terminal state; verify main green.
  1008	How to apply: Do NOT arm the merge at open. First clear the cloud-review gate (full mechanics: github.md RULE: codex-cloud-review-gate) — post `@codex review`, run `poll-codex-review.sh <pr> <head_sha>` in `run_in_background: true`, evaluate findings, fix anything real in-PR. THEN `gh pr merge <pr> --squash --auto --delete-branch`; watch via absolute path `/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/scripts/poll-pr.sh <pr>` in `run_in_background: true` (`.claude/` gitignored — relative path silently no-ops from worktrees). Push with `git -C <worktree-path> push ...`. If main post-merge fails, the most recently merged code-PR session owns the repair.
  1009	Ref: PR #596; cloud-review gate 2026-06-22.
  1010	
  1011	## RULE: phase-pr-closes-keyword
  1012	Rule: A PR shipping ONE phase of a multi-phase issue uses `Part of #N` / `Updates #N`, never `Closes #N Phase 1`.
  1013	Why: GitHub closes greedily on bare `Closes #N` and ignores trailing qualifiers, erasing the audit trail for remaining phases.
  1014	How to apply: Only the final phase's PR uses `Closes #N`. If auto-closed by mistake: `gh issue reopen <N>` + status comment.
  1015	Ref: #847.
  1016	
  1017	## FACT: branch-protection
  1018	`build-check` is the ONLY required check on every PR; it aggregates `build-debug` and `build-release` (debug + release build + test-target compile; the FoundationModels compile probe runs on `build-release`, not on the aggregator job itself). `polish-quality-gate` advisory. Strict/up-to-date is OFF, so a moved main needs no rebase. Force-pushes and branch deletion blocked. All human changes to `main` go through PRs; only the release bot pushes directly.
  1019	
  1020	## FACT: pr-merge-delete-branch-worktree-noise
  1021	`gh pr merge <pr> --squash --auto --delete-branch` run from a FEATURE WORKTREE prints `failed to run git: fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree at <root>` — this is BENIGN, NOT a failed merge. The merge AND the remote-branch delete succeed; only gh's LOCAL post-merge branch-delete fails (it tries to switch the local checkout to `main`, which the root worktree holds). Verify with `gh pr view <pr> --json state` (expect `MERGED`); the later `git push origin --delete <branch>` returns `remote ref does not exist` (already gone). Do NOT retry the merge or assume failure. Ref: #1200 (2026-06-23).
  1022	
  1023	## FACT: push-discipline-hook-two-dot-diff-false-positive
  1024	`check-push-discipline.sh`'s build-freshness check computes `CHANGED_FILES` via a TWO-DOT diff (`git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF"..HEAD`), not the merge-base-aware three-dot form (`BASE_REF...HEAD`). If your worktree branched off an OLDER `origin/main` commit and `main` has since advanced with unrelated Swift changes, the two-dot diff attributes THOSE files to your branch too — the hook then denies the push with "touches ship-path files... run scripts/build-dev-app.sh," even when your actual diff (`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`, three-dot) never touched `Sources/`/`Tests/`/`Package.swift` at all. This is the SAME two-dot-vs-three-dot bug class the CI classifier (`scripts/ci/classify-changes.sh`) was already fixed for (`ci-pipeline.md` FACT: detect-code-changes-extracted-to-script) — the push-discipline hook was not.
  1025	Why matters: branch-protection's "Strict/up-to-date is OFF, so a moved main needs no rebase" (FACT: branch-protection above) is true for GitHub's own merge requirements, but does NOT mean your LOCAL push is immune to this local hook's false positive — a stale worktree base can still block your push on phantom Swift changes.
  1026	How to apply: Before troubleshooting a "no local dev build found" denial on a diff you're confident is Swift-free, run `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` (three-dot) yourself to check for real ship-path files. If it's clean but the hook still denies, `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main` in the worktree (re-run tests after, a rebase replays commits) — this makes `BASE_REF` and your branch's actual base converge, which fixes the two-dot diff's symptom without touching the hook. Do not reach for `SKIP_PUSH_CHECKS=1` as the first move; the rebase is the real fix and is good git hygiene regardless.
  1027	Ref: #1433 (2026-07-09), PR #1437 — a Worker-lane-only diff got denied because main had advanced with unrelated `PasteCascadeExecutor.swift` changes since the worktree was created.
  1028	
  1029	## RULE: git-safety-systems
  1030	Rule: Enforce `.claude/rules/session-behavior.md` RULE: root-stays-on-main, which solely owns root placement and worktree policy.
  1031	How to apply: `command-safety.sh` denies checkout/switch resolving to root; `check-protected-paths.sh` denies ship-path edits in root while on main; `check-commit-gate.sh` blocks commit forms that bypass the staged-file ship-path check. Check `pgrep -f claude` before any operation touching root HEAD. When Claude cannot perform a required root correction, the founder runs it via the `!` prefix (that path is not hooked). Never use `--no-verify`, admin bypass, or `--no-gpg-sign` to get past a block — fix the cause.
  1032	Ref: `command-safety.sh`, `check-commit-gate.sh`.
  1033	===== /Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/rules/workflow-process.md =====
  1034	# Workflow Process
  1035	
  1036	How code moves from idea to merged. Council checks coverage; Codex checks plan facts and the diff against code reality.
  1037	
  1038	## RULE: never-batch-deny-prone-commands
  1039	Rule: Run deny-prone commands (`gh issue view`, protected-path edits, `git push`, anything a PreToolUse hook can deny) alone or first in a turn. A deny cancels the parallel batch; follow its text before batching safe work.
  1040	Ref: 2026-05-30 #832/#913; `.claude/scripts/gate-gh-issue-view.sh`.
  1041	
  1042	## RULE: main-writes-code-subagents-readonly
  1043	Rule: The main thread writes all code. Subagents may scan, research, perform persona council, or review read-only; never delegate implementation.
  1044	Ref: pre-#154 incidents.
  1045	
  1046	## RULE: ten-step-shape
  1047	Rule: Every shipped-product code change follows these 10 ordered steps. Council output feeds Grounded Review, not a separate revision pass. After every PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, revise and repeat Grounded Review until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  1048	
  1049	- **0. Gate 0 — Prior context.** Run `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,state,labels,comments` AND `grep -nE "#<N>([^0-9]|$)" .claude/knowledge/session-log.md`; post one paragraph: `Prior context for #<N>: ...`. If an adopted plan exists, skip to Gate 2. Use `--json`, never bare `--comments` (github-light.md FACT: finding-issues). `check-issue-prior-context.sh` partially enforces new-plan creation; `gate-gh-issue-view.sh` enforces the command shape.
  1050	- **1. Gate 0.5 — User Rubric.** For epics #314 / #316 / #317 / #320 / #321, answer `TEMPLATE.md`’s 9 questions for a named `personas.md` persona; paste all 9 answers, or `User Rubric: N/A — internal-only`, before Gate 1. Enforced structurally by `check-rubric-answered.sh`.
  1051	- **2. Gate 1 — Intent check.** Report user benefit in persona words, UX, value, and preliminary scope. If adding responsibility to a coordinator/manager/App-owned home or introducing one, state: `This will live on [X] because [reason]; the alternative would be [Y] but [trade-off].` Skip that sentence only for prompt/copy/catalog/config. **STOP for approval.**
  1052	- **3. Plan — Grounding brief → Design → self-audit → Council.** Save `TEMPLATE.md` as `docs/feature-requests/issue-<N>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`. Complete §2.5 before §3. Trace producer → owner → consumer end to end, naming each concrete mechanism. Paste code evidence for every symbol, module edge, process/init claim, quoted literal, negative claim, and owner search. Complete §3b Active-epic cross-check after evidence establishes current topology. Before design, run a problem-only Codex consult when the decision depends on topology/who-calls-whom, async/XPC/cancellation/state-machine lifecycle, dependency lifecycle machinery, an unsettled negative infrastructure claim, or an uncertain owner search. Ask for current reality and naive-design traps, not a solution. `check-knowledge-prereads.sh` non-blockingly supplies matching FACT/RULE headings as `additionalContext` and audits read/unread status. Before step 4 and every step-5 round, re-walk §2.5 evidence, sanity-check scope counts, state `self-audit clean` in chat, and revise if false. Council runs only after this sequence.
  1053	- **4. Council — ONE round, coverage only.** Ask: `What did we forget? Premise, placement, metric, workflow-stage, validation-strategy, persona.` Run GPT + Gemini with §2 inline preamble; use persona-roleplay for human-centric features. Save raw outputs to `/tmp/<scope>/{gpt,gemini}-critique.md`. Council does not certify code claims.
  1054	- **5. Grounded Review — iterate to PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.** Run Codex (`codex exec`) read-only. If the plan changes module boundaries, ownership, orchestration, feature placement, dependency direction, or cross-module visibility, instruct Codex to read `.claude/rules/architecture-rules.md` before Q1; its laws are vetoes, not a mandate to invent a deeper layer. **Q1 Direction:** validate structural choice or pivot. **Q2 Fact-check:** classify every council finding TRUE / FALSE / PARTIAL / JUDGMENT-CALL with grep-verified `file:line`. **Q3 Consolidation scan:** lead with dominant root concern yes/no/uncertain, confidence, recommended single owner/tool, consolidation sites, and independent concerns that must not merge. `No consolidation` is valid; correctness/security findings remain mandatory. **Q4 Proposed edits:** every finding includes concise, verbatim, drop-in replacement text; owner: RULE: codex-findings-ship-fixes-and-i-adjudicate. Verdicts: PROCEED-AS-PLANNED / PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS / PIVOT. PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS mandates step 6 and another step 5. Only PROCEED-AS-PLANNED unlocks Gate 2. PIVOT means re-plan. Same-root recurrence across ≥2 rounds means STOP and consolidate to one authority before another round. Backstop: flat/rising unresolved root clusters after 4 rounds means escalate to the founder with a forced choice: consolidate / split PR / rewrite plan / accept-with-documented-rationale / revert partial fixes and restart from a clean plan / declare N independent concerns. For cross-product/FSM surfaces use RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces.
  1055	- **6. Revise — one pass per round.** Apply the Codex verdict and accepted council findings in one edit. PIVOT supersedes the original plan. After PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, rerun step 5 unconditionally and recheck old plus new defects. Never return to council. Stop only on PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  1056	- **7. Gate 2 — Plan sign-off.** Present the revised plan in plain English with blast radius and council/Codex digest. Precondition: step 5 returned PROCEED-AS-PLANNED. Any other verdict at Gate 2 is a process violation. **STOP for approval.**
  1057	- **8. Build.**
  1058	- **9. Phase 3 — validation.** Run `scripts/validate-pr.sh` → `.validation/runs/<timestamp>-<shortsha>/`. Required caller order: logic tests → Codex code-diff, iterated to clean → smoke + Live UAT using ONE rebuild on clean code, never between Codex rounds (RULE: codex-clean-gates-runtime-uat) → push → open PR → evaluate GitHub Codex cloud review before arming auto-merge (local clean ≠ cloud review; github.md RULE: codex-cloud-review-gate) → arm `--auto`. Before push, record any skipped step in `skip-note.txt` or escalate to Stage 2. Smoke is not UAT. Mechanics and lanes: [phase3-validation.md](../knowledge/phase3-validation.md). Note: the current `validate-pr.sh` scaffolder performs smoke before writing its Codex stub; reconcile that script before claiming it enforces this order.
  1059	
  1060	Ref: #329.
  1061	
  1062	## RULE: plain-english-human-gates
  1063	Rule: At Gate 0, Gate 0.5, Gate 1, Gate 2, mid-task pivots, and wind-down, use no class/file names, API jargon, or bare tier labels. Write so a non-coder can catch a wrong direction.
  1064	Ref: project communication baseline.
  1065	
  1066	## RULE: gate-0-adopted-plan-shortcut
  1067	Rule: If Gate 0 finds an adopted plan, read it, summarize `Plan from <date>: <one paragraph>. Intent still matches?`, and skip to Gate 2. Do not rewrite it or rerun council.
  1068	Ref: `check-issue-prior-context.sh`; Gate 0 hook.

  1070	## FACT: lane-classification
  1071	Six exact-case lanes, enforced by `validate-pr.sh`: `Code`, `Content`, `CI/workflow`, `Eval-harness`, `Worker`, `Docs/dev-tooling`. There is no `Local`. Gitignored `.claude/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`, and root `scripts/*.sh` are `Docs/dev-tooling`. Path globs, obligations, and artifacts are owned solely by phase3-validation.md FACT: lane-obligations.
  1072	
  1073	Primary signal: `git check-ignore -v <path>`; a match means gitignored and no PR is possible.
  1074	
  1075	Codex still applies to gitignored work. Logic-bearing `Docs/dev-tooling` changes, including hooks, validators, workflow scripts, lane/rule/plan logic, command recipes, topology-critical docs, or future-agent decision paths, require a `codex exec` grounded check. Prose-only typo/session-log/narrative edits do not. See validation-discipline.md RULE: codex-grounds-topology-claims.

  1177	|---|---|

  1200	## RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration
  1201	Rule: Before coding MEDIUM+, enumerate every async operation against six classes: Interrupted (cancelled mid-flight?), Deleted (data deleted while running?), Mutated (settings/config changed in-flight?), Concurrent (two valid user actions overlap?), Nil (weak reference or optional dependency nil; fail open or closed?), and Stale (cached/snapshot value read after completion?). Record every answer in the Issue or PR. Justify accepted edges; otherwise design the guard before the happy path.
  1202	
  1203	**Closed-set trigger, any tier, overriding MEDIUM+:** Run the full `state × event` matrix only when BOTH hold:
  1204	
  1205	1. The change adds, changes, or reinterprets a closed lifecycle, outcome, or durability contract: state/terminal transition, cancellation/preemption route, session identity, or durable save/cleanup/delete/recovery ordering.
  1206	2. Before durable or user-visible commit, two or more ingress classes can affect it: user command, lifecycle/preemption event, timer/task cancellation, or async completion.
  1207	
  1208	ALSO run it when changing the branch that decides whether the heart emits raw text after limb failure, cancellation, or timeout.
  1209	
  1210	Retry, timeout, persistence, status, or fallback mentions alone do not trigger the matrix; use §5/§7-§9 and the six classes. `only`/`exactly`/`never`/`always` are hints, not gates.
  1211	
  1212	Event population: user commands; lifecycle/preemption events including app quit, sleep/wake, device removal, permission revocation, owner deinit, retry timer; and async completions that are absent, duplicate, late, or stale. Enumerate each event’s durable side effects, cleanup, and source-of-truth mutations before terminal state; terminal invariants alone are insufficient.
  1213	
  1214	Run this at plan time from invariant shape. RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces is separate and triggers after 3+ code-diff rounds reveal new cross-product defects.
  1215	Ref: async edge baseline; #1408 (`.discarded`/`.noSpeech` → `.discard` deleted a spool `.audioInterrupted` retained; `KernelDictationDriver.swift` `endedWithoutSaveKind`); `docs/audits/2026-07-10-grounding-rule-grounded-review-r1.txt`.
  1216

  1222	## RULE: definition-of-done
  1223	Rule: A change is not done until ALL pass:
  1224	
  1225	1. Xcode release build, `EnviousWispr-Release`.
  1226	2. Logic tests via `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; use `--release` for local reproduction or when full Release-suite execution is specifically required.

  1232	8. Close via `gh issue close <number> --comment "reason"`.
  1233

  1254	## RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces
  1255	Rule: If a PR adds methods to a surface crossed with FSM states and code-diff review finds a new substantive defect in each of 3+ rounds, STOP iterating.   1259	## RULE: close-the-window-never-handle-it
  1260	Rule: When a plan or invariant says an event CANNOT happen in a window (control disabled, state unreachable), implement the impossibility; never build a handler "to be safe." A handler admits the event, and every admitted event multiplies the state x event surface.
  1261	Why: #1386 PR-1 v1 — the plan said "Settings Remove is DISABLED during the transition"; the build instead grew ~120 lines of removal-deferral machinery. 14 of 30+ defects including all 4 cloud P1s trace to that one deviation (25 review rounds). Corollary (same RCA): on the FIRST defect of a class, audit the whole class (all writers/exits/deletes) before patching the shown instance — patched families recur; audited families die.
  1262	How to apply: In self-review, any code servicing an event the plan ruled out is a defect even if correct. Full RCA: `docs/postmortems/2026-07-11-1386-pr1-defect-cascade.md`; measured context: workflow-effectiveness.md.
  1263	Ref: #1386 PR-1 / PR #1497 (2026-07-11); founder-binding.
  1264	
  1265	## RULE: port-proven-patterns-wholesale
  1266	Rule: Port proven state/concurrency patterns whole, including every field and cleanup transition, or state why this instance differs. Never port piecewise across review rounds. If review finds a partial port, stop patching, inventory all fields/transitions, and fix once.
  1267	Ref: #1275; council session `ew-1275-warmup-retro-2026-07-02`.

  1269	## RULE: route-gaps-not-block-on-them
  1270	Rule: In a complex multi-PR rebuild, route each newly discovered gap to this PR / next PR / new follow-up issue instead of treating every gap as off-plan and replanning.
  1271	How to apply: Before founder escalation: fix bugs introduced here in this PR; route earlier-PR contract bugs to follow-up issues; route cutover-only validation to the cutover PR with Live UAT. Record routing in the PR description, not only commits.
  1272	Ref: PR-4b.2.

  1274	## RULE: no-follow-up-tickets-for-the-same-coherent-unit
  1275	Rule: Never defer part of the same coherent unit through a follow-up issue or unused seam/mode/flag. Finish it now. Follow-ups are only for a different subsystem, founder decision, or work that cannot be validated with this change.
  1276	How to apply: If an abstraction is added for later, wire it now. Split large work into smaller complete slices, never a complete slice plus its deferred remainder. `route-gaps-not-block-on-them` is the narrow exception for unrelated gaps in complex multi-PR rebuilds.
  1277	Ref: 2026-06-22 #1151/#1157; CLAUDE.md Rule 14.

Escalate only founder decisions: spend, scope, product, or a genuine fork among sound options.

  1286	How to apply: Use `see §3.2 filter 3`. Keep consumer-specific inputs and observable results. This is the document form of RULE: self-review-and-grep-before-codex and Grounded Review step 5’s single-authority rule.

  1288	===== /Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/rules/grounding-discipline.md =====
  1289	# Grounding Discipline
  1290	
  1291	## RULE: lookup-ladder
  1292	Rule: Walk this ladder in order; stop at the first tier that answers, and name any tier-skip in chat.
  1293	| Tier | Source | Use when |
  1294	|---|---|---|
  1295	| 0 | `.claude/knowledge/*.md` | Question is about an EW decision, gotcha, or past investigation. Pathway map in `CLAUDE.md` § Reference. |
  1296	| 1 | Vendor MCP (table in `tech-stack.md` § MCP servers) | Live data OR docs maintained by that vendor's MCP. |
  1297	| 2 | `context7` (`resolve-library-id` → `query-docs`, `researchMode: true` on retry) | Public framework / library / SDK / CLI docs. |
  1298	| 3 | Checkout grep (`.build/checkouts/<dep>/`, `Package.resolved` for SHA, `node_modules/<dep>/`) | Pinned versions, fork-specific patches (`saurabhav88/FluidAudio` `e7948e1a`), undocumented internals. |
  1299	| 4 | WebFetch / WebSearch | Tiers 0–3 returned nothing. Cite the URL. |
  1300	| 5 | Ask Saurabh | Product / business / preference only. Never for technical lookups. |
  1301	Why: Tier-skips cause drift.
  1302	Ref: 2026-05-03 — context7 covers public docs; a custom RAG over them wasn't the fit then (re-evaluate if corpus/tooling grows). Retrieval over our OWN knowledge base is a separate, still-open question.
  1303	
  1304	## RULE: tier-skip-must-be-named
  1305	Rule: Name every Tier 1 or Tier 2 skip in chat, then stop and use the right tier if the skip was accidental.
  1306	Why: Naming forces a sanity check and creates a grep-able audit trail.
  1307	Ref: 2026-05-03.
  1308	
  1309	## RULE: pinned-fork-grep-only
  1310	Rule: Grep `.build/checkouts/FluidAudio/` for `saurabhav88/FluidAudio` and any fork pinned off upstream `main`; do not trust upstream docs.
  1311	Why: Upstream docs describe code we're not running because we pinned the fork for its patches.
  1312	Ref: 2026-05-03.
  1313	
  1314	## RULE: absence-claims-need-a-capability-grep
  1315	Rule: In a plan, council prompt, Codex prompt, or chat, any “we have no X,” “X does not exist,” or “no consumers” claim needs a pasted capability search, not a search for the expected name. Absence of memory is not evidence. Negative-claim twin of [[search-existing-owner-by-capability]]. This is the one home for the command shape; `TEMPLATE.md` §2.5 item 5 references it and must not restate it.
  1316	
  1317	```
  1318	$ grep -rln "<syn1>\|<syn2>" Sources/ Tests/ workers/ website/ .github/ scripts/ .claude/ docs/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md | sort
  1319	```
  1320	
  1321	- Name the lane and justify every excluded root. These roots are defaults, not a population. Tooling searches include `.claude/` and `docs/`; omitting them hides the 26 validators in `.claude/scripts/`.
  1322	- A directory list never reaches a root-level FILE. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are gitignored and live at the repo root, so `git grep` and every directory-scoped sweep skip both. #1459's retirement sweep scoped itself to `scripts/ Sources/ Tests/ .github/` plus `.claude/` and declared the tracked tree clean; five references to the retired launcher were still sitting in `AGENTS.md`, the file that configures the Codex reviewer (2026-07-09).
  1323	- `| sort` is mandatory. Paste every hit verbatim and uncurated; put interpretation below the block.
  1324	- Synonyms: alerting → `alert|threshold|THRESHOLDS|notify|webhook`; scheduling → `cron|schedule|workflow_dispatch`; telemetry → `capture|emit|track|event`.
  1325	- A hit kills the claim only when it implements the capability. Classify incidental matches before concluding.
  1326	
  1327	| Class | Required proof |
  1328	|---|---|
  1329	| **Closed-world:** a finite authority defines all members, such as an enum, state switch, dispatcher, or conformer set. | Cite the authority (`file:line`), paste the structural enumeration, state expected and observed counts, and account for every member. Do not search for the counterexample you expect. |
  1330	| **Open-world:** no finite authority defines all members, such as alerting infrastructure, external consumers, vendor rules, dashboards, or unversioned configuration. | Search every justified source and write “no implementation found in `<sources>`,” never “X does not exist.” Do not invent an authority. |
  1331	
  1332	`grep -rn "editUI" Sources/` is not closed-world proof because it neither enumerates an authority nor accounts for its members. Closed-set lifecycle invariants follow `workflow-process.md` RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration, which owns the trigger, matrix, and tier scope.
  1333	
  1334	Ref: #1408, #1446, #1453; `docs/audits/2026-07-10-grounding-rule-grounded-review-r1.txt`.
  1335	
  1336	## RULE: read-the-fact-not-the-first-n-lines
  1337	Rule: When the non-blocking pre-read hook or pathway map names a knowledge file, LOOK UP the fact needed for the decision — `grep -n "<capability>"` the file, then read the matching `## FACT:` / `## RULE:` entry. Opening the first lines is not a lookup.
  1338	Why: #1446 read `analytics-operations.md` in full and later contradicted `FACT: product-health-worker`. The file was present in context; the failure was treating retrieval as compliance and making a negative claim without the required capability grep. The non-blocking hook now resurfaces matching headings and records read/unread status, but the §2.5 grounding brief owns proof.
  1339	How to apply: `grep -n "^## FACT:\|^## RULE:" <file>` to see the file's index, then read the entries that match your scope. Cheaper than a full read and it cannot miss a fact that lives at line 150. If two knowledge files disagree, that is a DRY defect — fix it in the same session (one fact, one home; the other file gets a cross-link), do not silently pick the one you read first.
  1340	Ref: #1446 (2026-07-09); the stale duplicate lived in `sentry-operations.md` FACT: live-sentry-alert-rules, corrected the same day.
  1341	
  1342	## RULE: grep-the-dependency-for-lifecycle-before-hand-rolling
  1343	Rule: Before designing ANY bespoke lifecycle/state-machine/manager/coalescing/retry infrastructure around a dependency (model load/unload, connection pool, session lifecycle, single-flight, cache), FIRST grep that dependency's `.build/checkouts/<dep>/` for an existing manager/state type it already ships (`*Manager`, `*State`, `*Coordinator`, `ensure*`, `coalesc`, `enum .*State`) — and check whether the object you already hold exposes it. Adopt-vs-invent is a DESIGN-TIME decision, not a post-hoc discovery.
  1344	Why: #1276 Step 1 designed a bespoke 9-field load-state machine + single-flight through 5 Codex rounds + council + an adversarial robustness pass — then the founder asked "are we reinventing the wheel?" and a 10-minute source grep found the toolkit already ships `ModelState` (a canonical lifecycle enum, live on every `WhisperKit` instance) AND `ModelManager` (download→load→unload state machine WITH concurrency coalescing + retry). ~Half the plan was reinvention. The review rounds validated invariants but never asked "does the library already do this."
  1345	How to apply: Extends [[search-existing-owner-by-capability]] (which greps OUR `Sources/`) to the DEPENDENCY's checkout. The §2.5 grounding brief for any infra plan must include a "did I grep the library for an existing lifecycle/manager?" line with the negative-or-positive grep pasted. Genuinely-ours policy (EW-specific latency tricks, fail-open budgets, use-leases) is what survives the cross-reference — build a thin layer of THAT on the library's machinery, not a parallel machine.
  1346	Ref: #1276 (2026-07-03); inventory `docs/feature-requests/issue-1276-step1-buy-vs-build-inventory.md`; whisperkit-research.md FACT: toolkit ships its OWN model-lifecycle machinery.
  1347	
  1348	## RULE: never-hand-a-reviewer-an-unchecked-premise
  1349	Rule: A council or Codex prompt gives every asserted fact the plan’s evidence burden. Verify each premise or label it “not verified” in the prompt. Reviewer prompts are plan text.
  1350	
  1351	How to apply: Check every negative, historical, causal, and quantitative claim before sending it. Negative claims follow [[absence-claims-need-a-capability-grep]]. Council has no repo access; agreement with an unchecked premise is not validation.
  1352	
  1353	A claim about a PRIOR REVIEW's contents is a premise. Grep the audit file for the finding; never read its tail through a fixed line window. A `codex exec` transcript repeats the final block, so a window can straddle two copies and silently truncate the findings list. #1462: told the reviewer it had shipped no fix for a section when it had, after reading a truncated Q4 of an 866 KB audit — then miscounted the same list twice more (6, then 8; it was 9).
  1354	
  1355	Ref: #1446, #1453, #1457, #1462.

  1376	Rule: Do not build Swift↔Python code generation, shared runtime prompt files, a Swift dumper, or PythonKit sync.

  1380	## FACT: polish-mode-flow
  1381	`PolishMode` is internal; there is no user picker.
  1382	- `DefaultPromptPlanner` forces `.message` for OpenAI, Gemini, native EG-1, and Ollama EG-1. Cloud uses `CloudFixedPromptBuilder`; EG-1 uses `EGOnePromptBuilder`. Both builders ignore mode.
  1383	- Only generic Ollama uses `TranscriptAnalyzer`: Gemma → `GemmaPromptBuilder`; other models → `OpenAIPromptBuilder`.
  1384	- Analyzer thresholds: ≤35 words no cues → inline; ≤35 with cues or 36–110 → message; >70 with cues or >110 → structured, except nil `appName` stays conservative.
  1385	- Observable output, not the enum, is the product contract.
  1386	
  1387	## RULE: test-output-not-mode
  1388	Rule: Assert output behavior, such as a real spoken list becoming bullets or short text staying one paragraph; do not assert `PolishMode` unless testing the analyzer itself.
  1389	Why: Correct output can survive a routing change; an enum assertion cannot prove user-visible quality.
  1390	How to apply: Cloud formatting changes edit cloud v6 and its mirrors. Generic Ollama formatting changes edit `TranscriptAnalyzer` plus its selected builder. EG-1 behavior follows its fixed prompt; see `eg1-operations.md`.
  1391	
  1392	## RULE: one-polish-path
  1393	Rule: Add polish capabilities through the existing single polish call and canonical corpus; do not add a parallel polish path.
  1394	Why: Parallel paths fragment evaluation and bypass the regression gate.
  1395	
  1396	## RULE: natural-dictation-samples-only
  1397	Rule: Use speech-reachable, punctuation-light dictation from real surfaces; reject engineered text that depends on characters or cue words people do not say.
  1398	Why: `apple_runner` and JSONL feeds bypass ASR, so synthetic triggers can manufacture unreachable bugs.
  1399	How to apply: Prefer “hey babe pick up milk bread and eggs” over “my shopping list is: milk, bread, eggs.” Build the realistic-sample corpus first and share it plus the heuristic at Gate 1; if a design depends on punctuation ASR won’t produce, the design is broken — pivot to succession detection or trust the existing bullet rule. Use `personas.md` sample banks when a named user context matters. Ref: #342.
  1400

  1403	Current tag handling:
  1404	- `EnviousOutputFilter` strips transcript wrappers on its AFM defense path.
  1405	- Ollama and AFM use `strippingLLMPreamble()` with tag stripping.
  1406	- OpenAI and Gemini pass `stripTranscriptTags: false` because cloud v6 has no transcript sandwich; literal dictated tags survive.
  1407	Ref: `EnviousOutputFilter.swift` `strippingTranscriptWrapperOnly`; `LLMProtocol.swift` `strippingLLMPreamble`; `OpenAIConnector.swift` and `GeminiConnector.swift` call sites. `<`/`>` are unreachable by dictation (spoken as words, ITN does not convert), so #578's synthetic `<transcript>` loss was closed won't-fix.

  1524	## RULE: extend-corpus-with-feature
  1525	Rule: Ship public positive, negative, and boundary cases with every new polish capability, then recapture the baseline in the same PR.
  1526	Why: Otherwise the gate cannot detect regression.
  1527	How to apply:
  1528	1. Extend the correct existing category, for example `filler_removal`, or add and document one.
  1529	2. Write 20–50 natural labeled cases: positive (fires), negative (must NOT fire), edge (boundary).
  1530	3. Fill `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` / `must_preserve` / `edit_budget` authoring hints and `expected_output`.
  1531	4. Run `--mode selftest`, then `--mode run --polish-model gpt-4o-mini`.
  1532	5. Recapture baseline with `--mode baseline --reason "<reason>"` and add founder-approved `BASELINE-BUMP:` text.
  1533	6. Corpus + prompt + new baseline ride in the same PR as the feature.

  1544	Rule: Download `polish-eval-pr` and classify each failure as true regression, approved tradeoff, or flaky infra; never baseline-bump to hide red.
  1545	Why: Bumping the baseline to hide a regression is the exact failure this gate prevents.

Intentional tradeoff → founder approval + `BASELINE-BUMP: <reason>` tag + `--mode baseline` recapture, commit. Flaky provider → "Re-run failed jobs" in GitHub UI.

  1562	## RULE: apple-runner-bench-verify-build
  1563	Rule: Run `cd scripts/eval/apple_runner && swift build -c release` separately and confirm `Build complete!` before executing the binary; never pipe the build through `tail`.
  1564	Why: A pipe makes the chain's exit status `tail`'s, so a compile error is swallowed and the STALE binary runs (a 2026-06-12 #963 bench silently measured the previous prompt).
  1565	How to apply: Run the same corpus twice and diff outputs when validating binary identity — greedy decoding is deterministic, so any diff means two different binaries. If a new source is omitted from SwiftPM discovery, `touch Package.swift`, rebuild, recheck.

  1567	## FACT: competitor-prompt-bakeoff-pattern
  1568	`apple_runner` resolves `--system-prompt` before `--system-prompt-file` before its built-in fallback; `--help` omits both prompt flags. Use `--system-prompt-file` to isolate prompt text while holding connector, corpus, and judge fixed — the mechanism for benching a competitor's Apple Intelligence prompt apples-to-apples. The 2026-07-08 Vox "General" prompt scored 64.5% / 89 S4 vs v38's 66.3% / 70 S4 on the identical exam. Use the artifacts, not narrative, for future comparisons. Full writeup: `docs/competitive-analysis/2026-07-08-vox-rizen-teardown.md`.

  1574	Retain these decisions from the v33→v38 work (shipped PR #1086, +11pp on ci151 tier-bench):
  1575	- Examples are the highest-leverage prompt component (ablation: deleting the 2 examples dropped 80.6%→69.3%, −11pp). Prefer formula/principle phrasing over word-lists for rules; use KEEP/ADD examples for contested behaviors (opener-keep, hedge-keep, mid-filler-drop).
  1576	- AFM is brittle to ANY prompt edit — no change is local. A one-rule wording tweak perturbed 11 unrelated outputs (−3pp). Every candidate needs a FULL tier-bench.
  1577	- Judge noise ≈ ±5pp; use reps and ignore sub-5pp deltas.
  1578	- Do not credit prompts for deterministic-owned categories (emoji/number/url/date/custom-vocab); use `deterministic-features.md`.

  1584	## RULE: afm-bench-throttle-cooldown
  1585	Rule: Use at least 0.3s inter-case sleep for sustained direct `apple_runner` runs; on a sudden error cascade, STOP, let the model idle (~6 min), and probe one case before blaming the prompt.
  1586	Why: A no-sleep 151-case run (#1083) drove FoundationModels into a persistent `ModelManagerError 1013` state where every subsequent call fails fast until recovery. Purely a sustained-benchmark artifact; real one-at-a-time dictation never hits it.
  1587	How to apply: Direct runner uses `--sleep-seconds 0.3`; `acceptance_gate.py --mode bench` uses `--afm-sleep-seconds 0.3`. `tier-bench` currently exposes NO sleep option — do not use it for a long AFM sweep without first resolving that parity gap.

  1616	## RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract
  1617	Rule: Shipping EG-1 v2 / EG-2 = upload the new artifact set + license to R2; update `eg1-delivery-manifest.json` with the new revision, per-shard file paths + measured `sizeBytes`/`sha256`, `totalBytes`, and `admission.layout`/`entrypointFile` (this manifest owns hashes/sizes/layout); then update `eg1-manifest.json`'s runtime config to match (`version`, `contextTokens`/`promptTemplateID`/`minAppVersion`/`licenseURL`) — `eg1-manifest.json` no longer carries `sha256`/`sizeBytes` (dead fields removed #1417, see FACT: eg1-artifact-identity). Keep `modelName`/`promptTemplateID` unless the PROMPT changed; bump `minAppVersion` if runtime behavior requires it. Zero code changes unless the prompt template changes (then: new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case + builder; unknown template IDs read RED "app_update_required" in old apps by design).
  1618	Why: `EGOneRuntime` refuses manifests whose `modelName != "eg-1"` (fixed Core literal `LLMProvider.egOneModelName`); `refreshInstalledState` purges the previous version's artifact family automatically (extension-scoped).
  1619	How to apply: R2 upload runbook below; validate the new host object with HEAD (etag+length), a Range request (expect 206), and a full curl+shasum before updating the manifest.
  1620	Ref: #1271 plan §hot-swap; purge added Codex r11.
  1621	
  1622	## FACT: kill-switch-stops-mutation-not-format-drift (#1386 PR-1, 2026-07-11)
  1623	`modelDelivery.egOne.enabled=false` guarantees exactly ONE thing: no EG-1 model bytes are moved, deleted, or fetched. It does NOT guarantee polish keeps working, and for one cohort it structurally cannot.
  1624	
  1625	A user still on the previously-shipped MONOLITH (`eg-1-v1.gguf`, every release ≤ v2.3.2) holds bytes a sharded build cannot load at all: `EGOneRuntime` boots `manifest.resolvedEntrypointPath` (shard 1), so no directory choice makes a monolith loadable. Turning the switch off therefore leaves that user with raw text (EG-1 is a limb) and their model completely untouched; turning it back on runs the migration and polish returns. Nothing is lost, only deferred.
  1626	
  1627	**Do NOT "fix" this by restoring the monolithic load path.** That means shipping the old manifest AND the old load path alongside the new ones, permanently — dual-format support carried forever for a rollback lever. Rejected on scope (founder 2026-07-11: don't over-engineer). Codex PR-1 review r14 raised it as DIAGNOSIS-ONLY; the resolution is this documented limitation, not code.
  1628	
  1629	Corollary for any FUTURE model-format change (EG-2, a new quantization): the kill switch is a byte-mutation stop, not a version rollback. If a format change ever needs a true rollback, that is a deliberate design (ship both manifests), not something the flag gives you for free.
  1630	
  1631	## FACT: eg1-monolith-retirement-and-owned-home (#1386 PR-1, PR #1500, 2026-07-11)
  1632	Shipped delivery shape since PR #1500: EG-1 installs to `~/Library/Application Support/EnviousWispr/Models/eg-1` (owned home; old `PolishModels` is the RETIRED store). At launch `EGOneLegacyUpgradeCoordinator` retires the one shipped monolith (`eg-1-v1.gguf`, 2_889_511_680 bytes, sha256 `3343fc1a...74f6`) by exact size+digest proof: containment gate (resolved-to-resolved, firmlink-safe) → durable `eg1-v1-replacement-owed` marker in `ModelDelivery/` → delete → normal ModelDeliveryController download. Marker clears ONLY on admission or explicit Cancel/Remove (decline counts even kill-switched — contract §5c.10). Post-replacement the RUNTIME decides activation via `activateAfterAutomaticReplacementIfNeeded()` (live `isActiveProvider`; the install-state stream never activates). Telemetry: `eg1.legacy_detected` (+`selected_provider`) / `legacy_retired` / `legacy_retirement_failed(reason: marker_write|delete|unreadable|containment)` / `replacement_completed` / `replacement_declined`; release ship-criterion: every detected distinct_id eventually shows completed/declined/diagnosable-failed. UAT fixture: genuine monolith kept at `~/Developer/EnviousLabs/eg1-uat-fixture/eg-1-v1.gguf` (digest-verified; monolith still hosted at models.enviouslabs.co/eg1/eg-1-v1-q5km.gguf). Contract authority: `docs/model-delivery/model-delivery-contract.md` v1.3 §5c (delete-first ONLY for cryptographically-identified app-owned assets the runtime cannot load — does NOT authorize delete-first for working files, e.g. WhisperKit). Plan+RCA: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1386-2026-07-11-eg1-retire-monolith-rev2.md`, `docs/postmortems/2026-07-11-1386-pr1-defect-cascade.md`.

  1639	## FACT: eg1-shard-authoring-runbook (#1417, 2026-07-08)
  1640	Splitting EG-1 into CDN-cache-eligible shards (each safely under Cloudflare's 512MB ceiling, target ≤450MB per the Phase-3 warn line) reuses `llama.cpp`'s native `gguf-split` tool and the shared delivery engine's existing `componentSet` layout (already proven by Parakeet's 23-file case) — no new reassembly code, no changes to `ManifestFetchTask`/`CacheAdmission`. One-time steps when cutting a new sharded EG-1 revision:
  1641	1. **Split:** run `gguf-split` against the real (unsplit) model weights, choosing `--split-max-tensors` so every output shard lands comfortably under 450MB (shards are NOT byte-range slices — each is an independently-headered valid GGUF file with its own metadata, so per-shard size varies with tensor boundaries, never assume equal division).
  1642	2. **Measure, never assume:** compute each shard's real `sizeBytes`/`sha256` from the actual output files — the manifest's `totalBytes` must equal the measured sum, and every `sizeBytes` must be re-verified ≤450MB after the real split (the pre-split total does not divide evenly by shard count).
  1643	3. **Upload:** each shard to R2 (`r2-hosting-runbook` above) under a NEW versioned sub-path (e.g. `/eg1/v2-sharded/`) — never reuse the legacy single-file path, so the new Cloudflare Cache Rule (scoped to the new sub-path only) can never accidentally match the old monolithic file, which is over the cache-eligible size ceiling.
  1644	4. **Author the manifest:** `admission.layout: "componentSet"`, `admission.entrypointFile` naming the shard `DeliveryManifest.resolvedEntrypointPath`/`EGOneDeliveryAdapter.installedArtifactURL` should boot from (shard 1, by `llama.cpp` convention — it auto-discovers siblings by filename pattern once pointed at shard 1), one `files[]` entry per shard with real measured hash/size.
  1645	5. **Validate before shipping:** every `sizeBytes` ≤450,000,000; `totalBytes` == sum of `files[].sizeBytes`; `entrypointFile` resolves to exactly one `resolvedInstallPath` (enforced by `DeliveryManifest.validateStructure()`, throws otherwise); no duplicate `installPath` values (already enforced); every shard file on disk matches its declared `sha256` before upload.
  1646	6. **Cloudflare Cache Rule + Transform Rule:** scope to `starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/eg1/v2-sharded/")` (or whatever the new sub-path is) — same shape as Parakeet's rule (edge TTL 1y, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, no-transform`). This is a production infra mutation, executed with explicit founder go, separate from the code/manifest change.
  1647	Existing EG-1 installs on the OLD single-file manifest are swept as stale download sidecars by `EGOneDeliveryAdapter.migrateLegacyStoreArtifacts()`'s version-agnostic cleanup and re-download once under the new manifest — the old file stays usable throughout (deleted only after the new N-shard set fully verifies and promotes, via `CacheAdmission`'s existing promote-time orphan cleanup). Full plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1417-2026-07-08-eg1-cdn-sharding.md`.

  1656	All exits verified live 2026-07-02 (kill drills + AX switch drill):
  1657	| Event | Behavior |
  1658	|---|---|
  1659	| Provider switch away | server killed, RAM freed (defers while a recording froze `.egOne`; terminal-state retry) |
  1660	| App quit | synchronous kill via `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` mirror (`applicationWillTerminate`) |
  1661	| App crash orphan | pkill sweep (anchored regex, exact binary path) — in-spawn + actor-gated `reapOrphansIfIdle` on every no-spawn launch path |
  1662	| Crash once | restart-once (~1 s warm) |
  1663	| Crash twice | stays down; recovery = settings-open probe or provider re-pick or relaunch |
  1664	| Critical memory pressure | killed even while starting |
  1665	| Dictation while dead | silent raw paste (~0.5 s; `local_polish_not_ready`) — verified live |

  1667	## FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines
  1668	Quality: 92.4% behavior / 0 critical on hard-340 at exact ship config (native; same artifact via Ollama scored 89.7%); 94.7% on full 1,890 (the number quoted in settings UI copy). Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. **ACCEPTED NUMBER SPLIT (founder decision 2026-07-05, do NOT re-raise):** in-app settings/release copy keeps **94.7%** (original internal full-1,890 run); the public README + r/macapps post use **93.7%** from the later reproducible `scripts/eval/runs/type-b-1199/eg1_native_shipped_1890/scores/summary.json` (`pass_rate_pct`, same `--system new` judge). This ~1pp split is a deliberate accepted state, not an open reconcile item — do not silently change either number (session-log 2026-07-05). Perf (live, M4 Pro): typical dictations 0.3-0.9 s polish, e2e 0.8-1.3 s Parakeet / 1.9-2.2 s WhisperKit; 1,817 chars in 8.0 s (~230 chars/s throughput). Re-benchmark recipe: `scripts/eval/subset_polish_runner.py --endpoint` against a locally-launched server with the SHIPPING flags (never via Ollama — different runtime, different numbers; see [ollama-operations.md](ollama-operations.md)).
  1669	**Shipped-config topic_shift regression (2026-07-05, NOT root-caused):** on the Type B 1,890 exam, `topic_shift` (paragraph breaks) scored 97% via the tuning harness but 78% through the shipped engine (−19pp), driving nearly the whole 94.4→93.7 gap (e.g. TS-026/TS-028 emit zero `\n\n` where the tuning outputs broke between topics). Same Q5_K_M model both runs, so the suspect is the SHIPPING RUNTIME config — most likely the q8_0 KV-cache quantization (the 4.1 GB-footprint choice, FACT: eg1-runtime-config) degrading long-range structuring. Clean test = re-run with fp16 KV cache (`--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16`) and see if topic_shift recovers. Possible customer-facing product issue (worse paragraph breaks than the tuned model can deliver); founder to decide whether to chase. Benchmark methodology owner: [polish-eval.md](polish-eval.md).
  1670	
  1671	## FACT: eg1-list-formatting-trigger
  1672	EG-1 builds a real **bullet list** from a lead-in phrase followed by a natural run of items with **no spoken ordinals** ("the team needs to confirm backups, feature flags, and the traffic drain" → lead-in `:` then one `- item` per line). Spoken ordinals ("first do X, second do Y, third Z") stay INLINE as sentences — the model reads them as sequential steps, not a list. Verified: `scripts/eval/corpus/list_format_v1.jsonl` + the shipped `type-b-1199/eg1_native_shipped_1890` run passed 74/100 list cases with real bullet output on exactly the lead-in-plus-run pattern; a founder demo dictation using "first/second/third" produced inline prose twice (2026-07-05). Implication for demos/marketing: to SHOW EG-1 building a list, script a lead-in + comma-run, never ordinals. Paragraph structuring + self-correction + filler removal work regardless of phrasing. A true marker list is an EG-1 / cloud behavior, NOT an Apple Intelligence one (AFM list detection is run-to-run inconsistent, confirmed live).
  1673	
  1674	## RULE: eg1-thresholds-are-provisional
  1675	Rule: EVERY EG-1 numeric threshold is a PROVISIONAL dial pending measured calibration (#1277) — treat none of them as design constraints; each is one constant at one site, changeable with data + eval gate. FOUNDER DIRECTIVE (2026-07-02): the 15 s polish budget WILL likely change — it is the top calibration item and must never be written about or planned around as a hard rule.
  1676	| Dial | Current | Status |
  1677	|---|---|---|
  1678	| Polish time budget | 15 s (`LLMPolishStep` maxDuration) | PROVISIONAL — the de-facto length limit (~3,000 chars at measured 230 chars/s), binds before the token cap; founder expects to raise |
  1679	| Context preflight | worst-case both sides (~8k chars) | PROVISIONAL — deliberately conservative; llama-server usage fields give true per-script ratios |
  1680	| Probe "slow" | 5 s | guess; measure warm-probe distribution |
  1681	| Disk preflight | 2.2× (partial bytes count as reclaimable) | guess; fine unless telemetry shows disk failures |
  1682	| Crash-retry delay | 750 ms single retry | cannot beat ~9 s cold reload (accepted r17); a second retry ~1.5 s would rescue warm-restart (~1 s) crashes — decide from telemetry |
  1683	How to apply: failure direction is always "raw text pasted" (silent), never truncation/error — `finish_reason == length` skips whole. Change a dial → update this table + #1277 in the same session.
  1684	Ref: #1277 (measured baselines recorded there).
  1685	
  1686	## FACT: eg1-telemetry
  1687	EG-1 downloads ride the shared `model_delivery.*` funnel with `family=eg1` (`TelemetryService.swift`) — the legacy `eg1.download_started/completed/failed` events were RETIRED (#1348 Phase 3, `EGOneTelemetryBridge.swift`). Runtime health still emits `eg1.health_changed(from,to,reason)` via `EGOneTelemetryBridge` (content-free by construction). Polish skips ride the `llm.polish_skipped` PostHog event (Swift `TelemetryService.polishSkipped`) with reasons `local_polish_{not_ready,download_pending,crashed,input_too_long,output_truncated}` + runner `local_polish_timeout`. These are the calibration inputs for #1277.
  1688	
  1689	## FACT: eg1-legal-posture
  1690	EG-1 Community Model License v1.0 (`docs/launch-assets/EG-1-MODEL-LICENSE.txt`, hosted next to the artifact): free in-app/personal/research/benchmarking; NO redistribution, NO embedding in competing commercial products, NO training/distilling commercial models from outputs. Base Qwen Apache-2.0 permits this. Motivation: competitor founder publicly fishing for our prompts (Reddit). IP-attorney review flagged non-blocking, still open. Weights+prompt are inherently extractable from a local install — the license is the legal deterrent, training data + iteration engine remain the real moat. llama.cpp attribution is a SEPARATE obligation (MIT notice, see engine section).
  1691	
  1692	## FACT: eg1-download-drain-gate (#1287/#1279, PR #1322, 2026-07-04)
  1693	Cancel→Try Again is single-flight through a drain gate in `EGOneModelStore`: cancel/remove stash the live task as `drainingTask` (guarded — nil never clobbers a pending drain), an accepted retry publishes `.downloading(existingFraction)` synchronously at acceptance (instant Cancel; no dead Try Again while draining), awaits the predecessor's `Task.value` before running (task completion IS the drain signal: delegate continuation resumes only on `didCompleteWithError`, then the handle closes), and `runDownload` refuses stale generations before any disk touch. NO timer escape by design (`timeout-numbers-need-distribution-evidence`); a wedged drain presents as a stalled download with live Cancel, diagnosable via the debug drain-wait log lines ("EG-1 retry waiting for cancelled download to drain" / "drain wait finished in ..."). Tests are negative-control validated (protection removed → test fails); lesson: an absence-of-effect test window must outlast the un-gated mutation latency — pre-warm `AppLogger` in the test or first-time logger init masks the violation. Live drill precedent (real host, same-second cancel/retry at 15%/40%, resume + verified install): session-log 2026-07-04.
  1694	
  1695	## FACT: eg1-review-lessons
  1696	For the next new-subsystem feature (this cost 17 local review rounds + founder stop-call):
  1697	1. Async/long-running machinery (downloads, child processes) gets the FULL situation-grid enumeration at PLAN time (async-edge-case-enumeration rule applied hard, not shallowly) — the dictation path planned this way stayed clean through every round.
  1698	2. Budget the plain review loop: 3-4 rounds, then SWITCH MODES to one-pass exhaustive enumeration (matrix / callback-staleness populations). The matrix+enumeration passes here each replaced ~4 discovery rounds.
  1699	3. Threshold findings are calibration items, not review arguments — route to measurement immediately (founder directive; see thresholds rule above).
  1700	4. The recurring defect family was "async completion acts on a stale generation" — every callback/queued-Task/post-await resume needs a named staleness guard (generation token, state re-check, single-flight flag, actor-idle gate). Enumerate the population once; audits at `docs/audits/2026-07-02-1271-{eg1-lifecycle-matrix,callback-enumeration}.txt`.
  1701	Ref: session-log 2026-07-02; #1271.

  1704	# EG-1 Model Provenance (how the model was MADE)
  1705	
  1706	When to load: any question about how EG-1 was trained — "is it a full fine-tune or a LoRA," base model, training method/config, training data, per-language coverage, "did we build our own model from scratch," or how to build EG-2/EG-3 (retrain recipe). This is the "how it was made" record; [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) is the "how it runs / how it ships" record (hosting, runtime flags, unload matrix, licensing). Do not duplicate — cross-link.
  1707	
  1708	Source of record: GitHub issue **#1265** (closed, founder-approved 2026-07-02) — its "Method of record" + results comments are authoritative; research + citations in `docs/competitive-analysis/2026-07-02-tune-base-model-vs-fluid1.md`. Training data lives (gitignored, Docs/dev-tooling lane) in `scripts/eval/runs/bakeoff-1265/train_sft_v{1,2}.jsonl`. Epic: **#1190**. Wiring into the app: **#1269 / #1271**.
  1709	
  1710	July 15-16 multilingual/list research resume point: `docs/experiments/eg1-multilingual/CLAUDE-CODE-SALVAGE-HANDOFF-2026-07-16.md` and GitHub issue **#1570**. They classify what is proven, reusable, rejected, and missing after the paused 24-hour run. Read them before resuming PR #1562 or the older running tracker #1364.
  1711	
  1712	## FACT: eg1-headline-what-it-is
  1713	| Question | Answer |
  1714	|---|---|
  1715	| Full fine-tune or LoRA? | **QLoRA** (LoRA on the 4-bit-quantized base) — NOT a full-parameter retrain. |
  1716	| Adapter shipped separately? | **No.** The LoRA adapter is **merged back into the base weights**, then converted and quantized; there is no runtime "base + adapter." Physical packaging + the current shard identity are owned by [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity (EG-1 ships as 8 componentSet GGUF shards, #1417 — not one file). |
  1717	| Base model | **Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507** (Alibaba, Apache-2.0, the non-thinking variant). |
  1718	| Built from scratch? | No. It is a fine-tuned **derivative** of Qwen3-4B — this is why the README says "fine-tuned derivative of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0)" and the EG-1 license applies to the *fine-tuned weights*, not the base. |
  1719	| Plain-English framing for Saurabh | "We took Alibaba's Qwen 4B, taught it our dictation-cleanup behavior with a QLoRA fine-tune, and baked the result into one custom model. It's ours, but it stands on an open base." |
  1720	
  1721	The one-line honest positioning: **"a QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-4B, merged and quantized."** Do NOT claim "full fine-tune" (false — it's LoRA) and do NOT claim "trained our own model from scratch" (false — Qwen3-4B is the base).
  1722	
  1723	## FACT: eg1-training-config
  1724	Settled by council + Codex (#1265), trained on the RTX 4090:
  1725	| Knob | Value |
  1726	|---|---|
  1727	| Method | QLoRA via **Unsloth** (CUDA-only; does not run on Apple Silicon) |
  1728	| LoRA rank / alpha | **r16 / a32** |
  1729	| Learning rate | **5e-5** (dropped from the research doc's 2e-4 starting point) |
  1730	| Epochs | **2** |
  1731	| Loss | **response-only** (loss on the cleaned output, not the transcript/prompt) |
  1732	| Target modules | all attention + MLP projections |
  1733	| Precision | bf16, adamw_8bit, gradient checkpointing |
  1734	| Rig | **AlienSV RTX 4090** (24 GB, WSL2 Ubuntu), always-on via Tailscale. **$0 spend** — owned hardware, no cloud GPU. |
  1735	| Division of labor | TRAIN on the PC, EVAL on the Mac (llama.cpp/Ollama + judge harness), ship the merged GGUF back over Tailscale. |
  1736	
  1737	Rig details: `~/.claude/knowledge/infra/aliensv-pc.md`.
  1738	
  1739	## FACT: eg1-build-pipeline
  1740	The end-to-end pipeline (mirror of Fluid-1's exact approach — competitor-proven):
  1741	```
  1742	QLoRA train (4090)  →  merge adapter into base  →  GGUF convert  →  Q5_K_M quantize  →  judge the QUANTIZED artifact
  1743	```
  1744	- **Judge the quantized artifact, never the fp16 checkpoint.** The shipped quality number must be measured on exactly the GGUF users run. (Q5_K_M was chosen over Q4_K_M: Q4 scored 86.5% vs Q5 88.8% on the hard-340 at bake-off; the feared Qwen-Q4 collapse did not materialize, but Q5's ~2pp edge + fewer criticals won.)
  1745	- Shipped quant: **Q5_K_M, ~2.7–2.9 GB total**. Current sharded artifact identity + exact per-shard SHAs: [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity.
  1746	
  1747	## FACT: eg1-training-data
  1748	Two data generations; **v2 is what shipped** (`train_sft_v2.jsonl`, **5,656 pairs**). Format is flat `{id, source, input(raw) → output(cleaned)}` JSONL.
  1749	- **v1 (3,036 pairs):** SFT built from 1,549 Type-B-approved rows after excluding the hard-340 IDs/texts, plus founder dictations. The exclusion protected the hard-340 exact cases, not the full 1,890 working set. The 900-case overflow set stayed exact-text sealed but was derived from the same provenance families.
  1750	- **v2 = v1 + 1,924 teacher-distilled real dictations** (teacher = gemini-2.5-flash + the v6 cloud prompt; hallucination-filtered, noop-capped) **+ 696 targeted convention drills.**
  1751	- **Leakage correction (2026-07-15):** shipping v2 has exact ID and normalized-input overlap with **1,549/1,890** full Type B rows; conservative normalization finds 1,551. Provenance-family components expose 1,866/1,890 approved rows and 899/900 overflow rows. The old zero-overlap statement conflated the protected hard-340/exact-overflow checks with the broader working set. The old 1,890 and overflow scores are historical development/robustness evidence, not held-out quality estimates. Owner receipt: `docs/experiments/eg1-multilingual/OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md` TYPE-B-001.
  1752	- **Prompt = training contract:** the model was trained AND ships with ONE fixed short system prompt + `<TRANSCRIPT>…</TRANSCRIPT>` wrapper (`scripts/eval/prompts/eg1-polish-prompt-v1.txt`, pinned by a golden-string test in `EGOnePromptBuilder`). Training prompt MUST equal inference prompt — prompt-shape drift cost ±18pp on the untuned base. This is why EG-1 gets its own `.egOneFixed` prompt family and ignores per-mode prompt rules (behavior is in the weights).
  1753	
  1754	## FACT: eg1-quality-and-bias-gate
  1755	Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. (Numbers here are the #1265 acceptance run; note the separate marketing-vs-settings discrepancy tracked in `eg1-operations.md` FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines — 94.4/94.7 internal vs 93.7 public, same model, different run.)
  1756	- **Hard-340 subset:** 94.7%, **0 critical fails** (beat the gpt-4o + v6 cloud champion same-batch: 93.5%, 2 crit).
  1757	- **Full 1,890:** 94.4% (traps 97.3%, false-positive 2.4%).
  1758	- **Historical one-time bias gate:** exact-text-sealed 900-overflow scored 88.0% vs untuned-base anchor 61.2%; Type-C mixed slice 94.5%; 100 train-excluded real dictations ~95%. This does not prove held-out generalization because the 2026-07-15 provenance audit found 899/900 overflow rows in training-exposed Type B families.
  1759	
  1760	## FACT: eg1-language-coverage-provenance
  1761	- **Trained overwhelmingly on English.** The v2 corpus is English-oriented `raw → cleaned` dictation data, but it is not literally ASCII-only. The historical quality numbers above are English.
  1762	- **Base is multilingual** (Qwen3-4B handles ~100+ languages) and the fixed prompt says "keep the same language … never translate," so EG-1 will *accept* and attempt to polish non-English — but that rides on base-model ability, un-benchmarked per-language. Lower-resourced languages will be rougher.
  1763	- **Multilingual training pairs are an explicit v3 lever** (epic #1190 follow-ups), not shipped in EG-1 v1/v2.
  1764	- Do not conflate with transcription: the ASR engines (Parakeet = English + 24 European; WhisperKit = 99) are a separate stage feeding EG-1 (`architecture.md`).
  1765	
  1766	## RULE: eg1-retrain-recipe-for-eg2
  1767	Rule: To build EG-2 (or EG-1 v3), reuse this exact pipeline — QLoRA (Unsloth, 4090) → merge → GGUF → quantize → judge the quantized artifact against the SEALED holdout — and keep the training prompt byte-identical to the shipped prompt. A PROMPT change means a new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case (see `eg1-operations.md` RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract); a weights-only update keeps the template id.
  1768	Why: prompt-shape drift alone swings quality ±18pp; judging fp16 instead of the quantized GGUF ships a number users never see.
  1769	How to apply: expand data on the v2 recipe (synthetic + teacher-distilled real dictations + targeted drills), preserve zero-overlap with the eval, re-run the one-time bias gate on any new data generation, and route any prompt-family change through a code-lane PR. Distribution (R2 upload, manifest bump) is `eg1-operations.md`.
  1770	Ref: #1265 method-of-record; #1190 epic.

  1866	## RULE: stable-dev-certificate
  1867	Rule: Use a stable self-signed "EnviousWispr Dev" certificate for dev builds so TCC grants persist across rebuilds.
  1868	Why: macOS anchors TCC to (bundle ID + signing identity); rotating signing identity loses Accessibility/Microphone grants on every rebuild.
  1869	How to apply: First-time setup creates a 10-year self-signed cert and grants Accessibility once in System Settings; subsequent rebuilds preserve grants.
  1870	```bash
  1871	TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
  1872	openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -days 3650 \
  1873	  -keyout "$TMPDIR/dev.key" -out "$TMPDIR/dev.crt" \
  1874	  -subj "/CN=EnviousWispr Dev/O=EnviousWispr Development"
  1875	openssl pkcs12 -export -out "$TMPDIR/dev.p12" \
  1876	  -inkey "$TMPDIR/dev.key" -in "$TMPDIR/dev.crt" -passout pass:""
  1877	security import "$TMPDIR/dev.p12" -k ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db \
  1878	  -T /usr/bin/codesign -f pkcs12 -P ""
  1879	sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
  1880	  -k ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db "$TMPDIR/dev.crt"
  1881	rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
  1882	```
  1883	Delete: `security delete-certificate -c "EnviousWispr Dev" ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`.

  2052	===== /Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/knowledge/model-delivery.md =====
  2053	<!-- tier: 2 -->
  2054	# Model Delivery (epic #1348)
  2055	
  2056	**when:** ANY work touching how model bytes reach a user's machine — Parakeet/WhisperKit/EG-1 downloads, the models.enviouslabs.co mirror, download telemetry, cache validation/repair, first-run model UX, or planning any #1348 phase.
  2057	**why:** the #1339 launch-night incident proved the default model path depended on a borrowed downloader (FluidAudio's → Hugging Face) with no failover/verification/cancel; the founder-ratified pivot is one owned, verified cache-admission layer.
  2058	**Authority:** `docs/model-delivery/model-delivery-contract.md` (LIVE contract, currently v1.2). This knowledge file is the stable pointer + invariants summary; the contract wins where they diverge. Phases 1-3 shipped; Phase 4 WhisperKit convergence remains parked. Durable final artifacts are posted to epic #1348 as comments (one per artifact). At epic completion, promote the final contract INTO this file.
  2059	
  2060	## RULE: model-delivery-contract-is-the-authority
  2061	Rule: Before designing, reviewing, or amending ANYTHING in the delivery layer, read `docs/model-delivery/model-delivery-contract.md`; a plan that needs to deviate amends the contract FIRST, with rationale, and posts the amendment to epic #1348.
  2062	Why: architecture negotiated through PR comments is the failure mode that cost 17 review rounds on EG-1 (#1271) and 7 on the parked PR-2.
  2063	Ref: epic #1348; founder directive 2026-07-06 ("document all of this... in-depth plan phase, large/refactor tier").
  2064	
  2065	## FACT: the-ten-invariants (contract §1, stable)
  2066	1. Verified or absent — no unverified bytes in a final cache path; temp download → SHA-256 BEFORE admission → atomic move.
  2067	2. One writer — single-flight per ModelIdentity; readers only after admission.
  2068	3. Atomic admission — old valid state or new valid state, never a mix.
  2069	4. Manifest-pinned — versioned manifest (files+sizes+SHA-256+source templates); NO runtime listing calls (#1339 failure mode #1).
  2070	5. Cooperative cancellation — typed result, never process kill; no partial in final cache; temp resumable or discardable.
  2071	6. Resumable where possible — URLSession resume data + Range (mirror serves full Range semantics).
  2072	7. Source-aware — our copy (models.enviouslabs.co) first, upstream backup second, per-file failover, order overridable.
  2073	8. Telemetry-complete — every attempt speaks the shared 14 emitted failure classes plus the reserved `constrained_network_deferred` class (contract §7); Ollama included at lifecycle granularity.
  2074	9. Runtime-agnostic — the layer ENDS at a verified cache location; never loads/compiles models.
  2075	10. Deletes old supervision code — net launch-path complexity DOWN per migration PR (deletion ledger is a merge criterion).
  2076	
  2077	Plus (v1.1): manifest trust root — source selection is mutable; expected identity/hash/size is immutable except via trusted app update (bundled pin is the authority; a drifted mirror can never achieve admission). Disk lifecycle — preflight before fetch, stale-version eviction, disk-full is a first-class recoverable failure; constrained/metered-network policy is a deliberate decision, not a default-by-omission.
  2078	
  2079	## FACT: scope-guardrails (founder + CTO agreed, binding)
  2080	Unify ONLY where WE move bytes: Parakeet, WhisperKit, EG-1. Ollama = shared telemetry only (its daemon owns bytes; `OllamaSetupService` commands it). Sparkle = fully out of scope. No god-layer: one fetcher + thin per-backend adapters. The shared `ModelDeliveryController` + `ManifestFetchTask` + `CacheAdmission` engine (`Sources/EnviousWisprModelDelivery/`) generalized the now-retired `EGOneModelStore`'s mechanisms (resume identity, generation tokens, cancel drain-gate, SHA-before-install, disk preflight, stale purge) from one file to manifest sets.

  2094	## FACT: install-phase-false-wedge-is-NOT-a-download-problem (#1388, fixed 2026-07-09)
  2095	Do not re-diagnose "Setup is taking longer than expected... check your VPN" (or `wedge_detected` with `observed_phase="Installing model..."`) as a download problem. Production forensics (14d): **117 of 126 wedge fires happened during the CoreML INSTALL (compile) phase**, which runs with networking disabled — every one a false positive. Root cause: the guard's post-signal silence gate ("gate B", `silence > max(floor, 5x maxGap)`) assumes homogeneous work units, but the compile emits ~52 ticks ~1.5s apart (small models) then goes silent for one ~445MB encoder taking ~20x longer — the ratio self-calibrates on the wrong distribution and the 15s floor becomes the sole trigger. Worse, the fire's teardown never resumed the pending load continuation (`ASRManagerProxy`'s invalidation handler didn't touch it), so **119/126 fires reached no terminal outcome** — the launch warm-up silently hung, the guard slot leaked, and users got warm only via the separate onboarding warm-up. #1388 fixed the completion contract (resume-once, typed causes: death → `serviceUnreachable` and the adapter's one-shot retry; cancel → `ASRLoadCancelledError`, non-transport so the retry can't resurrect it), REMOVED gate B from the model-load guard (gate A — the 120s no-signal-at-all deadline — survives, and the Phase-2 download parking (`downloadOwnedPhases`/`wasInDownloadPhase` + boundary reset) is RETAINED because it protects gate A too, not just gate B — without it download ticks satisfy the pre-first-signal deadline and a service that hangs before its first LOAD signal is undetectable (Codex r2 P1); only `transferSilenceFloorSeconds` was deleted as genuinely gate-B-only), added a user Cancel during install (`EngineWarmupOutcome.cancelled`, never a failure), corrected the copy, and added un-truncated install telemetry (`install_duration_ms`/`install_silence_max_ms` on `coldstart.warmup_completed`). Success-duration data justified removal over re-tuning: onboarding warm-up p99.9 = 2080s, so any non-false-firing deadline would exceed ~35 minutes — a give-up policy, not a detector. Plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1388-2026-07-09-install-phase-false-wedge.md` (5 grounded-review rounds). Fault drill: `A11_asr_kill_mid_model_load`.
  2096

Plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1405-2026-07-07-model-delivery-global-cdn.md` (Phase 1/2); Phase 2 root-cause pivot plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1405-2026-07-08-downloader-owns-stall.md`. EG-1 already inherits Phase 2 retry/resume via `ManifestFetchTask` (self-heals like Parakeet), and each shard is now SIZE-eligible for free-tier caching — but the Cloudflare Cache Rule covering the shard path is a separate, founder-gated infra mutation NOT yet deployed (cloudflare.md still scopes caching to `/parakeet/`; `/eg1/` excluded), so EG-1 gets no edge-cache HIT benefit yet. Still single-source (no mirror/backup), unlike Parakeet's mirror+HF failover. Canonical artifact/hosting/authoring: [eg1-operations.md](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity + FACT: eg1-shard-authoring-runbook.   2106	# Workflow Process
  2107	
  2108	How code moves from idea to merged. Council checks coverage; Codex checks plan facts and the diff against code reality.
  2109	
  2110	## RULE: never-batch-deny-prone-commands
  2111	Rule: Run deny-prone commands (`gh issue view`, protected-path edits, `git push`, anything a PreToolUse hook can deny) alone or first in a turn. A deny cancels the parallel batch; follow its text before batching safe work.
  2112	Ref: 2026-05-30 #832/#913; `.claude/scripts/gate-gh-issue-view.sh`.
  2113	
  2114	## RULE: main-writes-code-subagents-readonly
  2115	Rule: The main thread writes all code. Subagents may scan, research, perform persona council, or review read-only; never delegate implementation.
  2116	Ref: pre-#154 incidents.
  2117	
  2118	## RULE: ten-step-shape
  2119	Rule: Every shipped-product code change follows these 10 ordered steps. Council output feeds Grounded Review, not a separate revision pass. After every PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, revise and repeat Grounded Review until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  2120	
  2121	- **0. Gate 0 — Prior context.** Run `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,state,labels,comments` AND `grep -nE "#<N>([^0-9]|$)" .claude/knowledge/session-log.md`; post one paragraph: `Prior context for #<N>: ...`. If an adopted plan exists, skip to Gate 2. Use `--json`, never bare `--comments` (github-light.md FACT: finding-issues). `check-issue-prior-context.sh` partially enforces new-plan creation; `gate-gh-issue-view.sh` enforces the command shape.
  2122	- **1. Gate 0.5 — User Rubric.** For epics #314 / #316 / #317 / #320 / #321, answer `TEMPLATE.md`’s 9 questions for a named `personas.md` persona; paste all 9 answers, or `User Rubric: N/A — internal-only`, before Gate 1. Enforced structurally by `check-rubric-answered.sh`.
  2123	- **2. Gate 1 — Intent check.** Report user benefit in persona words, UX, value, and preliminary scope. If adding responsibility to a coordinator/manager/App-owned home or introducing one, state: `This will live on [X] because [reason]; the alternative would be [Y] but [trade-off].` Skip that sentence only for prompt/copy/catalog/config. **STOP for approval.**
  2124	- **3. Plan — Grounding brief → Design → self-audit → Council.** Save `TEMPLATE.md` as `docs/feature-requests/issue-<N>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`. Complete §2.5 before §3. Trace producer → owner → consumer end to end, naming each concrete mechanism. Paste code evidence for every symbol, module edge, process/init claim, quoted literal, negative claim, and owner search. Complete §3b Active-epic cross-check after evidence establishes current topology. Before design, run a problem-only Codex consult when the decision depends on topology/who-calls-whom, async/XPC/cancellation/state-machine lifecycle, dependency lifecycle machinery, an unsettled negative infrastructure claim, or an uncertain owner search. Ask for current reality and naive-design traps, not a solution. `check-knowledge-prereads.sh` non-blockingly supplies matching FACT/RULE headings as `additionalContext` and audits read/unread status. Before step 4 and every step-5 round, re-walk §2.5 evidence, sanity-check scope counts, state `self-audit clean` in chat, and revise if false. Council runs only after this sequence.
  2125	- **4. Council — ONE round, coverage only.** Ask: `What did we forget? Premise, placement, metric, workflow-stage, validation-strategy, persona.` Run GPT + Gemini with §2 inline preamble; use persona-roleplay for human-centric features. Save raw outputs to `/tmp/<scope>/{gpt,gemini}-critique.md`. Council does not certify code claims.
  2126	- **5. Grounded Review — iterate to PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.** Run Codex (`codex exec`) read-only. If the plan changes module boundaries, ownership, orchestration, feature placement, dependency direction, or cross-module visibility, instruct Codex to read `.claude/rules/architecture-rules.md` before Q1; its laws are vetoes, not a mandate to invent a deeper layer. **Q1 Direction:** validate structural choice or pivot. **Q2 Fact-check:** classify every council finding TRUE / FALSE / PARTIAL / JUDGMENT-CALL with grep-verified `file:line`. **Q3 Consolidation scan:** lead with dominant root concern yes/no/uncertain, confidence, recommended single owner/tool, consolidation sites, and independent concerns that must not merge. `No consolidation` is valid; correctness/security findings remain mandatory. **Q4 Proposed edits:** every finding includes concise, verbatim, drop-in replacement text; owner: RULE: codex-findings-ship-fixes-and-i-adjudicate. Verdicts: PROCEED-AS-PLANNED / PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS / PIVOT. PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS mandates step 6 and another step 5. Only PROCEED-AS-PLANNED unlocks Gate 2. PIVOT means re-plan. Same-root recurrence across ≥2 rounds means STOP and consolidate to one authority before another round. Backstop: flat/rising unresolved root clusters after 4 rounds means escalate to the founder with a forced choice: consolidate / split PR / rewrite plan / accept-with-documented-rationale / revert partial fixes and restart from a clean plan / declare N independent concerns. For cross-product/FSM surfaces use RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces.
  2127	- **6. Revise — one pass per round.** Apply the Codex verdict and accepted council findings in one edit. PIVOT supersedes the original plan. After PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, rerun step 5 unconditionally and recheck old plus new defects. Never return to council. Stop only on PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  2128	- **7. Gate 2 — Plan sign-off.** Present the revised plan in plain English with blast radius and council/Codex digest. Precondition: step 5 returned PROCEED-AS-PLANNED. Any other verdict at Gate 2 is a process violation. **STOP for approval.**
  2129	- **8. Build.**
  2130	- **9. Phase 3 — validation.** Run `scripts/validate-pr.sh` → `.validation/runs/<timestamp>-<shortsha>/`. Required caller order: logic tests → Codex code-diff, iterated to clean → smoke + Live UAT using ONE rebuild on clean code, never between Codex rounds (RULE: codex-clean-gates-runtime-uat) → push → open PR → evaluate GitHub Codex cloud review before arming auto-merge (local clean ≠ cloud review; github.md RULE: codex-cloud-review-gate) → arm `--auto`. Before push, record any skipped step in `skip-note.txt` or escalate to Stage 2. Smoke is not UAT. Mechanics and lanes: [phase3-validation.md](../knowledge/phase3-validation.md). Note: the current `validate-pr.sh` scaffolder performs smoke before writing its Codex stub; reconcile that script before claiming it enforces this order.

  2143	Six exact-case lanes, enforced by `validate-pr.sh`: `Code`, `Content`, `CI/workflow`, `Eval-harness`, `Worker`, `Docs/dev-tooling`. There is no `Local`. Gitignored `.claude/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`, and root `scripts/*.sh` are `Docs/dev-tooling`. Path globs, obligations, and artifacts are owned solely by phase3-validation.md FACT: lane-obligations.

Any failure or ambiguity requires full process. PR tag: `council-skip: zero-blast-radius (<bucket>)`. Still require 1 Codex diff round, 1 human sanity-check, and tier-appropriate tests/rebuild.

  2228	Rule: When §2.5 or §3c asks whether an owner, telemetry path, or handler exists, grep capability synonyms across `Sources/ Tests/`, never only the proposed symbol. Enumerate every caller of the primitive being wrapped. Do not trust issue claims that X lacks Y; paste a negative grep that would have found Y.
  2229	How to apply: Search verb+noun plus 2-3 domain synonyms. Telemetry example: `warmup|preload|cold.?start|load.*(ms|duration|started|completed|failed)`. This extends RULE: self-review-and-grep-before-codex and §2.5.
  2230	Ref: #1174 PR-5b, 2026-06-23.
