  2232	## RULE: audit-all-terminal-paths-for-state-reading-telemetry
  2233	Rule: When an FSM-terminal capture/read consumes earlier session state, enumerate every path into that terminal and verify: (a) this path sets/freezes the state before transition; (b) for single-winner/latched exits, state is FIRST-WINS under the same latch so later signals cannot decouple it from the winning exit.
  2234	How to apply: Grep every terminal transition, including `finishTerminal(.X)`, `deliverRecordingExit(.X)`, and forced transitions, plus every state producer. Mirror the working sibling terminal. Guard state under the same acceptance condition, e.g. `state == .recording && !recordingExitLatched`. This is async-edge-case-enumeration’s Stale + Concurrent case.
  2235	Ref: #1174 PR-5b, 2026-06-24.

  2242	Rule: At REFACTOR/LARGE tier, add no technical debt; if the plan fails, stop and pivot through council. Use existing context7, MCPs, eval harness, and tests rather than reinventing. Agents may scan/research/review only, never change code.

  2245	## FACT: tier-routing
  2246	Classify in the GitHub Issue: `Tier: MEDIUM | Test: required (PostProcessing) | Modules: PostProcessing, Core`.
  2247	
  2248	| Tier | Surface |
  2249	|---|---|
  2250	| REFACTOR | `Package.swift`, target/module moves, dependency graph, shared protocol reshaping; any module move or multi-conformer protocol change remains REFACTOR regardless of diff size |
  2251	| LARGE | Pipeline orchestration, XPC boundaries, app startup, both ASR backends |
  2252	| MEDIUM | Audio capture, one ASR backend, Services, permissions, paste path, net-new runtime behavior |
  2253	| SMALL | Isolated post-processing, LLM prompt changes, UI layout/copy, config tweaks |
  2254	
  2255	Escalate upward, never downward. Any code edit after validation invalidates that validation. Tier controls test obligations and runtime breadth via RULE: test-obligations and phase3-validation.md FACT: lane-obligations. Plan/council/Codex gates apply except where RULE: council-skip-zero-blast-radius or RULE: council-skip-codex-grounded-review-settled explicitly allows a skip.

  2257	## RULE: test-obligations
  2258	Rule: In testable Core, PostProcessing, LLM, and Pipeline state/routing: bug fixes require a failing `@Test` before the fix; new logic requires `@Test` alongside or before implementation; threshold/scoring/routing changes require just-above, just-below, and ambiguity tests; subtle refactors require characterization tests first. If no test is added, document why in issue and PR.
  2259	How to apply: Use `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; gotchas.md RULE: xcode-test-entrypoint explains why raw `swift test` is not the gate. Runtime-only Audio, XPC, UI, permissions, paste, and hardware are exempt.
  2260	Ref: project test baseline.

  2262	## RULE: matcher-set-adversarial-tests
  2263	Rule: When adding to a skip list, allow list, imperative/preservation set, or matcher where set membership flips routing, test the entry in its non-intended semantic class. A positive plus one happy-path negative is insufficient.
  2264	How to apply: Name the intended class, enumerate alternate readings, and add an explicit negative for every meaning-changing alternate. The test harness, not Codex review, must catch it.
  2265	Ref: PR #436.
  2266	
  2267	## RULE: parse-structured-input-dont-regex-and-iterate
  2268	Rule: Before coding a guard/validator/matcher for structured input, including URL path+query, versions, key=value config, semver, or dates, choose a parser and enumerate the full axes × value-classes matrix. Never ship naive substring/regex matching and discover gaps round by round.
  2269	How to apply: List axes, write the complete pass/fail fixture grid, and run a LOCAL adversarial Codex enumeration, `find every input that bypasses each rule across the whole space`, before first push, not through ordinary diff or cloud review. Explicitly document accepted-scope non-authoring inputs such as percent-encoding or backslash normalization.
  2270	Ref: PR #1241; [[matcher-set-adversarial-tests]]; [[async-edge-case-enumeration]].
  2271	
  2272	## RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration
  2273	Rule: Before coding MEDIUM+, enumerate every async operation against six classes: Interrupted (cancelled mid-flight?), Deleted (data deleted while running?), Mutated (settings/config changed in-flight?), Concurrent (two valid user actions overlap?), Nil (weak reference or optional dependency nil; fail open or closed?), and Stale (cached/snapshot value read after completion?). Record every answer in the Issue or PR. Justify accepted edges; otherwise design the guard before the happy path.
  2274	
  2275	**Closed-set trigger, any tier, overriding MEDIUM+:** Run the full `state × event` matrix only when BOTH hold:
  2276	
  2277	1. The change adds, changes, or reinterprets a closed lifecycle, outcome, or durability contract: state/terminal transition, cancellation/preemption route, session identity, or durable save/cleanup/delete/recovery ordering.
  2278	2. Before durable or user-visible commit, two or more ingress classes can affect it: user command, lifecycle/preemption event, timer/task cancellation, or async completion.
  2279	
  2280	ALSO run it when changing the branch that decides whether the heart emits raw text after limb failure, cancellation, or timeout.
  2281	
  2282	Retry, timeout, persistence, status, or fallback mentions alone do not trigger the matrix; use §5/§7-§9 and the six classes. `only`/`exactly`/`never`/`always` are hints, not gates.
  2283	
  2284	Event population: user commands; lifecycle/preemption events including app quit, sleep/wake, device removal, permission revocation, owner deinit, retry timer; and async completions that are absent, duplicate, late, or stale. Enumerate each event’s durable side effects, cleanup, and source-of-truth mutations before terminal state; terminal invariants alone are insufficient.
  2285	
  2286	Run this at plan time from invariant shape. RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces is separate and triggers after 3+ code-diff rounds reveal new cross-product defects.
  2287	Ref: async edge baseline; #1408 (`.discarded`/`.noSpeech` → `.discard` deleted a spool `.audioInterrupted` retained; `KernelDictationDriver.swift` `endedWithoutSaveKind`); `docs/audits/2026-07-10-grounding-rule-grounded-review-r1.txt`.
  2288	
  2289	## RULE: lane-detection-match-plan
  2290	Rule: Tier controls test scope; lane controls Phase 3. Detect lane with `git diff --name-only <merge-base origin/main HEAD>..HEAD`, never plain `origin/main`. The plan’s lane must match detection.
  2291	How to apply: [phase3-validation.md](../knowledge/phase3-validation.md) FACT: lane-obligations solely owns lane globs, obligations, artifacts, and `mixed_pr`. Eval-harness reporting never replaces app Live UAT.
  2292	Ref: `scripts/validate-pr.sh`; `detect_lane_from_diff`.

  2294	## RULE: definition-of-done
  2295	Rule: A change is not done until ALL pass:
  2296	
  2297	1. Xcode release build, `EnviousWispr-Release`.
  2298	2. Logic tests via `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; use `--release` for local reproduction or when full Release-suite execution is specifically required.
  2299	3. Dev `.app` rebuild + relaunch via `/wispr-rebuild-and-relaunch` (`scripts/build-dev-app.sh`).
  2300	4. Each wispr-eyes scope item is VERIFIED or validly SKIPPED per [tools-and-apps.md](./tools-and-apps.md).
  2301	5. Council coverage approval on plan and Codex clean on diff, subject only to explicit skip rules.
  2302	6. If `/ask-gpt` is used, GPT sign-off after rounds to clean.
  2303	7. CI `build-check` green.
  2304	8. Close via `gh issue close <number> --comment "reason"`.
  2305	
  2306	How to apply: Checklist numbering is not run order. Codex-clean item 5 precedes items 3-4; then perform one rebuild and Live UAT per RULE: codex-clean-gates-runtime-uat. Wispr-eyes todos use `Fix X in Y (user-visible result Z)` and a fresh list per project. Architecture-sensitive changes also complete [architecture-rules.md § Architecture Definition of Done](./architecture-rules.md) and include Architecture Closeout in the issue closure comment. `.claude/scripts/check-push-discipline.sh` invokes `scripts/check-dependency-direction.sh` on ship-path pushes and blocks violations; SPM cyclic-import compilation is the second line.
  2307	Ref: project DoD.

  2309	## RULE: grounded-review-mechanics
  2310	Rule: After council, before Gate 2, run `codex exec` against the plan with full codebase access. Require PROCEED-AS-PLANNED / PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS / PIVOT and grep-verified `file:line` corrections. PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS → revise → rerun until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED. No other verdict reaches Gate 2. Every round verifies prior fixes and scans for new defects.
  2311	How to apply: Run `cat <prompt-file> | ~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check > docs/audits/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<scope>-grounded-review[-rN].txt 2>&1` via `Bash run_in_background: true`; run from repo root or use an absolute output path. Round 1 contains unrevised plan, both council critiques, and Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4; Q3 is consolidation, Q4 drop-in fixes. Later rounds contain revised plan, prior revision list, and `verify each landed, scan for new defects.` Skip for zero-blast-radius. Flat/rising defect count after 4 rounds is the escalation signal. Cost is $0 via ChatGPT subscription.
  2312	Ref: #319; PR-1 #827 3 rounds; #827 epic 7.
  2313	
  2314	## FACT: review-gates-summary
  2315	| Gate | Tool | When | Rounds |
  2316	|---|---|---|---|
  2317	| Council | `~/.local/bin/council ask` | After plan draft | 1, never iterated |
  2318	| Grounded Review | `codex exec` | After council, before Gate 2 | Until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED |
  2319	| Code-diff review | `codex review` local | After logic tests + self-review, before smoke + Live UAT rebuild | Multiple until clean |
  2320	| Cloud review | `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` GitHub | After PR open, before auto-merge | Evaluate every finding; fix loop ≤3 per github.md RULE: codex-cloud-review-gate |
  2321	
  2322	Council owns coverage; Grounded Review owns code reality; cloud review independently reviews the open PR. Skip none except RULE: council-skip-zero-blast-radius and RULE: council-skip-codex-grounded-review-settled.
  2323	
  2324	`check-selfreview-before-codex.sh` gates both local Codex passes. `codex review` requires commit `Self-audit-*`; `codex exec` requires fresh `/tmp/.ew-codex-selfreview-attested` with `Checked:`/`Grep:`/`Owner:`. See RULE: self-review-and-grep-before-codex.
  2325	
  2326	## RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces
  2327	Rule: If a PR adds methods to a surface crossed with FSM states and code-diff review finds a new substantive defect in each of 3+ rounds, STOP iterating. Ask Codex for the full surface × state matrix; every cell names expected behavior, parity reference, and GAP. Apply only GAP cells naturally belonging to this PR.
  2328	How to apply: After 3 consecutive qualifying rounds, prompt with every added/public surface entry, every FSM state, and the parity implementation. Require a markdown matrix, implementation list, and parametric `@Test` freeze test. Use Codex r5 on PR-4b.2 as template.
  2329	Ref: PR #856.
  2330	
  2331	## RULE: close-the-window-never-handle-it
  2332	Rule: When a plan or invariant says an event CANNOT happen in a window (control disabled, state unreachable), implement the impossibility; never build a handler "to be safe." A handler admits the event, and every admitted event multiplies the state x event surface.
  2333	Why: #1386 PR-1 v1 — the plan said "Settings Remove is DISABLED during the transition"; the build instead grew ~120 lines of removal-deferral machinery. 14 of 30+ defects including all 4 cloud P1s trace to that one deviation (25 review rounds). Corollary (same RCA): on the FIRST defect of a class, audit the whole class (all writers/exits/deletes) before patching the shown instance — patched families recur; audited families die.
  2334	How to apply: In self-review, any code servicing an event the plan ruled out is a defect even if correct. Full RCA: `docs/postmortems/2026-07-11-1386-pr1-defect-cascade.md`; measured context: workflow-effectiveness.md.
  2335	Ref: #1386 PR-1 / PR #1497 (2026-07-11); founder-binding.
  2336	
  2337	## RULE: port-proven-patterns-wholesale
  2338	Rule: Port proven state/concurrency patterns whole, including every field and cleanup transition, or state why this instance differs. Never port piecewise across review rounds. If review finds a partial port, stop patching, inventory all fields/transitions, and fix once.
  2339	Ref: #1275; council session `ew-1275-warmup-retro-2026-07-02`.
  2340	
  2341	## RULE: route-gaps-not-block-on-them
  2342	Rule: In a complex multi-PR rebuild, route each newly discovered gap to this PR / next PR / new follow-up issue instead of treating every gap as off-plan and replanning.
  2343	How to apply: Before founder escalation: fix bugs introduced here in this PR; route earlier-PR contract bugs to follow-up issues; route cutover-only validation to the cutover PR with Live UAT. Record routing in the PR description, not only commits.
  2344	Ref: PR-4b.2.
  2345	
  2346	## RULE: no-follow-up-tickets-for-the-same-coherent-unit
  2347	Rule: Never defer part of the same coherent unit through a follow-up issue or unused seam/mode/flag. Finish it now. Follow-ups are only for a different subsystem, founder decision, or work that cannot be validated with this change.
  2348	How to apply: If an abstraction is added for later, wire it now. Split large work into smaller complete slices, never a complete slice plus its deferred remainder. `route-gaps-not-block-on-them` is the narrow exception for unrelated gaps in complex multi-PR rebuilds.
  2349	Ref: 2026-06-22 #1151/#1157; CLAUDE.md Rule 14.
  2350	
  2351	## RULE: consult-before-concluding-at-walls
  2352	Rule: At dependency conflicts, build failures, apparent impossibility, or a Codex finding implying pivot, consult Codex for code-reality walls or council for design walls before drafting a conclusion or fix direction. Escalate only founder decisions: spend, scope, product, or a genuine fork among sound options.
  2353	How to apply: First run the empirical/grounded check, such as resolution attempt, `codex exec`, or generated-code read. Present only options proven workable.
  2354	Ref: 2026-05-29 #832.
  2355	
  2356	## RULE: plan-consumers-point-at-the-contract
  2357	Rule: One plan section owns each behavioral contract. Plan §5, §7, §9, §11, and §13 identify their local path, caller, projection, or oracle and reference the owner by number; never paraphrase it. Before revising a contract, grep the whole plan for its terms.
  2358	How to apply: Use `see §3.2 filter 3`. Keep consumer-specific inputs and observable results. This is the document form of RULE: self-review-and-grep-before-codex and Grounded Review step 5’s single-authority rule.
  2359	Ref: #1457.

  2362	## RULE: lookup-ladder
  2363	Rule: Walk this ladder in order; stop at the first tier that answers, and name any tier-skip in chat.
  2364	| Tier | Source | Use when |
  2365	|---|---|---|
  2366	| 0 | `.claude/knowledge/*.md` | Question is about an EW decision, gotcha, or past investigation. Pathway map in `CLAUDE.md` § Reference. |
  2367	| 1 | Vendor MCP (table in `tech-stack.md` § MCP servers) | Live data OR docs maintained by that vendor's MCP. |
  2368	| 2 | `context7` (`resolve-library-id` → `query-docs`, `researchMode: true` on retry) | Public framework / library / SDK / CLI docs. |
  2369	| 3 | Checkout grep (`.build/checkouts/<dep>/`, `Package.resolved` for SHA, `node_modules/<dep>/`) | Pinned versions, fork-specific patches (`saurabhav88/FluidAudio` `e7948e1a`), undocumented internals. |
  2370	| 4 | WebFetch / WebSearch | Tiers 0–3 returned nothing. Cite the URL. |
  2371	| 5 | Ask Saurabh | Product / business / preference only. Never for technical lookups. |
  2372	Why: Tier-skips cause drift.
  2373	Ref: 2026-05-03 — context7 covers public docs; a custom RAG over them wasn't the fit then (re-evaluate if corpus/tooling grows). Retrieval over our OWN knowledge base is a separate, still-open question.
  2374	
  2375	## RULE: tier-skip-must-be-named
  2376	Rule: Name every Tier 1 or Tier 2 skip in chat, then stop and use the right tier if the skip was accidental.
  2377	Why: Naming forces a sanity check and creates a grep-able audit trail.
  2378	Ref: 2026-05-03.
  2379	
  2380	## RULE: pinned-fork-grep-only
  2381	Rule: Grep `.build/checkouts/FluidAudio/` for `saurabhav88/FluidAudio` and any fork pinned off upstream `main`; do not trust upstream docs.
  2382	Why: Upstream docs describe code we're not running because we pinned the fork for its patches.
  2383	Ref: 2026-05-03.
  2384	
  2385	## RULE: absence-claims-need-a-capability-grep
  2386	Rule: In a plan, council prompt, Codex prompt, or chat, any “we have no X,” “X does not exist,” or “no consumers” claim needs a pasted capability search, not a search for the expected name. Absence of memory is not evidence. Negative-claim twin of [[search-existing-owner-by-capability]]. This is the one home for the command shape; `TEMPLATE.md` §2.5 item 5 references it and must not restate it.
  2387	
  2388	```
  2389	$ grep -rln "<syn1>\|<syn2>" Sources/ Tests/ workers/ website/ .github/ scripts/ .claude/ docs/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md | sort
  2390	```
  2391	
  2392	- Name the lane and justify every excluded root. These roots are defaults, not a population. Tooling searches include `.claude/` and `docs/`; omitting them hides the 26 validators in `.claude/scripts/`.
  2393	- A directory list never reaches a root-level FILE. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are gitignored and live at the repo root, so `git grep` and every directory-scoped sweep skip both. #1459's retirement sweep scoped itself to `scripts/ Sources/ Tests/ .github/` plus `.claude/` and declared the tracked tree clean; five references to the retired launcher were still sitting in `AGENTS.md`, the file that configures the Codex reviewer (2026-07-09).
  2394	- `| sort` is mandatory. Paste every hit verbatim and uncurated; put interpretation below the block.
  2395	- Synonyms: alerting → `alert|threshold|THRESHOLDS|notify|webhook`; scheduling → `cron|schedule|workflow_dispatch`; telemetry → `capture|emit|track|event`.
  2396	- A hit kills the claim only when it implements the capability. Classify incidental matches before concluding.
  2397	
  2398	| Class | Required proof |
  2399	|---|---|
  2400	| **Closed-world:** a finite authority defines all members, such as an enum, state switch, dispatcher, or conformer set. | Cite the authority (`file:line`), paste the structural enumeration, state expected and observed counts, and account for every member. Do not search for the counterexample you expect. |
  2401	| **Open-world:** no finite authority defines all members, such as alerting infrastructure, external consumers, vendor rules, dashboards, or unversioned configuration. | Search every justified source and write “no implementation found in `<sources>`,” never “X does not exist.” Do not invent an authority. |
  2402	
  2403	`grep -rn "editUI" Sources/` is not closed-world proof because it neither enumerates an authority nor accounts for its members. Closed-set lifecycle invariants follow `workflow-process.md` RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration, which owns the trigger, matrix, and tier scope.
  2404	
  2405	Ref: #1408, #1446, #1453; `docs/audits/2026-07-10-grounding-rule-grounded-review-r1.txt`.
  2406	
  2407	## RULE: read-the-fact-not-the-first-n-lines
  2408	Rule: When the non-blocking pre-read hook or pathway map names a knowledge file, LOOK UP the fact needed for the decision — `grep -n "<capability>"` the file, then read the matching `## FACT:` / `## RULE:` entry. Opening the first lines is not a lookup.
  2409	Why: #1446 read `analytics-operations.md` in full and later contradicted `FACT: product-health-worker`. The file was present in context; the failure was treating retrieval as compliance and making a negative claim without the required capability grep. The non-blocking hook now resurfaces matching headings and records read/unread status, but the §2.5 grounding brief owns proof.
  2410	How to apply: `grep -n "^## FACT:\|^## RULE:" <file>` to see the file's index, then read the entries that match your scope. Cheaper than a full read and it cannot miss a fact that lives at line 150. If two knowledge files disagree, that is a DRY defect — fix it in the same session (one fact, one home; the other file gets a cross-link), do not silently pick the one you read first.
  2411	Ref: #1446 (2026-07-09); the stale duplicate lived in `sentry-operations.md` FACT: live-sentry-alert-rules, corrected the same day.
  2412	
  2413	## RULE: grep-the-dependency-for-lifecycle-before-hand-rolling
  2414	Rule: Before designing ANY bespoke lifecycle/state-machine/manager/coalescing/retry infrastructure around a dependency (model load/unload, connection pool, session lifecycle, single-flight, cache), FIRST grep that dependency's `.build/checkouts/<dep>/` for an existing manager/state type it already ships (`*Manager`, `*State`, `*Coordinator`, `ensure*`, `coalesc`, `enum .*State`) — and check whether the object you already hold exposes it. Adopt-vs-invent is a DESIGN-TIME decision, not a post-hoc discovery.
  2415	Why: #1276 Step 1 designed a bespoke 9-field load-state machine + single-flight through 5 Codex rounds + council + an adversarial robustness pass — then the founder asked "are we reinventing the wheel?" and a 10-minute source grep found the toolkit already ships `ModelState` (a canonical lifecycle enum, live on every `WhisperKit` instance) AND `ModelManager` (download→load→unload state machine WITH concurrency coalescing + retry). ~Half the plan was reinvention. The review rounds validated invariants but never asked "does the library already do this."
  2416	How to apply: Extends [[search-existing-owner-by-capability]] (which greps OUR `Sources/`) to the DEPENDENCY's checkout. The §2.5 grounding brief for any infra plan must include a "did I grep the library for an existing lifecycle/manager?" line with the negative-or-positive grep pasted. Genuinely-ours policy (EW-specific latency tricks, fail-open budgets, use-leases) is what survives the cross-reference — build a thin layer of THAT on the library's machinery, not a parallel machine.
  2417	Ref: #1276 (2026-07-03); inventory `docs/feature-requests/issue-1276-step1-buy-vs-build-inventory.md`; whisperkit-research.md FACT: toolkit ships its OWN model-lifecycle machinery.
  2418	
  2419	## RULE: never-hand-a-reviewer-an-unchecked-premise
  2420	Rule: A council or Codex prompt gives every asserted fact the plan’s evidence burden. Verify each premise or label it “not verified” in the prompt. Reviewer prompts are plan text.
  2421	
  2422	How to apply: Check every negative, historical, causal, and quantitative claim before sending it. Negative claims follow [[absence-claims-need-a-capability-grep]]. Council has no repo access; agreement with an unchecked premise is not validation.
  2423	
  2424	A claim about a PRIOR REVIEW's contents is a premise. Grep the audit file for the finding; never read its tail through a fixed line window. A `codex exec` transcript repeats the final block, so a window can straddle two copies and silently truncate the findings list. #1462: told the reviewer it had shipped no fix for a section when it had, after reading a truncated Q4 of an 866 KB audit — then miscounted the same list twice more (6, then 8; it was 9).
  2425	
  2426	Ref: #1446, #1453, #1457, #1462.

  2440	2. Run `python3 scripts/eval/acceptance_gate.py --mode selftest`.
  2441	3. Run `python3 scripts/eval/acceptance_gate.py --mode baseline --polish-model gpt-4o-mini --reason "<reason>"`.
  2442	4. Commit `scripts/eval/baselines/gpt-4o-mini.json` and add `BASELINE-BUMP: <reason>` to the PR body.
  2443	Carve-out: Ollama-only `gemmaFewShot`/`openAIProse`/`egOneFixed` changes require no CI mirror/baseline update unless cloud v6 or custom vocabulary also changes. State the carve-out in the PR.
  2444	
  2445	## RULE: no-auto-sync-mechanism
  2446	Rule: Do not build Swift↔Python code generation, shared runtime prompt files, a Swift dumper, or PythonKit sync.
  2447	Why: Founder-approved policy treats rigid auto-sync as costlier than manual sync for volatile prompt architecture.
  2448	Ref: #299. Reconsider only with founder approval and new evidence.
  2449	
  2450	## FACT: polish-mode-flow
  2451	`PolishMode` is internal; there is no user picker.
  2452	- `DefaultPromptPlanner` forces `.message` for OpenAI, Gemini, native EG-1, and Ollama EG-1. Cloud uses `CloudFixedPromptBuilder`; EG-1 uses `EGOnePromptBuilder`. Both builders ignore mode.
  2453	- Only generic Ollama uses `TranscriptAnalyzer`: Gemma → `GemmaPromptBuilder`; other models → `OpenAIPromptBuilder`.
  2454	- Analyzer thresholds: ≤35 words no cues → inline; ≤35 with cues or 36–110 → message; >70 with cues or >110 → structured, except nil `appName` stays conservative.
  2455	- Observable output, not the enum, is the product contract.
  2456	
  2457	## RULE: test-output-not-mode
  2458	Rule: Assert output behavior, such as a real spoken list becoming bullets or short text staying one paragraph; do not assert `PolishMode` unless testing the analyzer itself.
  2459	Why: Correct output can survive a routing change; an enum assertion cannot prove user-visible quality.
  2460	How to apply: Cloud formatting changes edit cloud v6 and its mirrors. Generic Ollama formatting changes edit `TranscriptAnalyzer` plus its selected builder. EG-1 behavior follows its fixed prompt; see `eg1-operations.md`.
  2461	
  2462	## RULE: one-polish-path
  2463	Rule: Add polish capabilities through the existing single polish call and canonical corpus; do not add a parallel polish path.
  2464	Why: Parallel paths fragment evaluation and bypass the regression gate.
  2465	
  2466	## RULE: natural-dictation-samples-only
  2467	Rule: Use speech-reachable, punctuation-light dictation from real surfaces; reject engineered text that depends on characters or cue words people do not say.
  2468	Why: `apple_runner` and JSONL feeds bypass ASR, so synthetic triggers can manufacture unreachable bugs.
  2469	How to apply: Prefer “hey babe pick up milk bread and eggs” over “my shopping list is: milk, bread, eggs.” Build the realistic-sample corpus first and share it plus the heuristic at Gate 1; if a design depends on punctuation ASR won’t produce, the design is broken — pivot to succession detection or trust the existing bullet rule. Use `personas.md` sample banks when a named user context matters. Ref: #342.
  2470	
  2471	## FACT: eval-asr-input-must-be-speech-reachable
  2472	Corpus `asr_input` is injected after ASR. Before scoping a corpus failure, reproduce the trigger by voice or confirm it appears in `CORRECTION_DEBUG [RAW ASR]`.
  2473	Current tag handling:
  2474	- `EnviousOutputFilter` strips transcript wrappers on its AFM defense path.
  2475	- Ollama and AFM use `strippingLLMPreamble()` with tag stripping.
  2476	- OpenAI and Gemini pass `stripTranscriptTags: false` because cloud v6 has no transcript sandwich; literal dictated tags survive.
  2477	Ref: `EnviousOutputFilter.swift` `strippingTranscriptWrapperOnly`; `LLMProtocol.swift` `strippingLLMPreamble`; `OpenAIConnector.swift` and `GeminiConnector.swift` call sites. `<`/`>` are unreachable by dictation (spoken as words, ITN does not convert), so #578's synthetic `<transcript>` loss was closed won't-fix.
  2478	
  2479	## FACT: real-dictation-log-measurement
  2480	Use `~/Library/Logs/EnviousWispr/app.log` as the shipped-quality check: `CORRECTION_DEBUG [RAW ASR]` is pre-pipeline input and `[LLM Polish] OUT:` is final polished output. This includes real ASR and the deterministic stack that naked corpora bypass. Validate a synthetic quality claim here before adding a fix. `Tests/RuntimeUAT/wispr_eyes.py` already parses both markers. Lesson: a synthetic-corpus metric that bypasses an upstream stage over-states a downstream gap — #449's "80% missing terminal punctuation" was an artifact of the ASR bypass; real shipped finals are ~99% terminal-punctuated.

  2553	## RULE: polish-scored-by-judge-not-string-match
  2554	Rule: Score semantic polish with an LLM judge and inspect raw samples; never use `must_contain`, `must_not_contain`, `edit_budget`, or exact equality as the quality verdict.
  2555	Why: Equivalent outputs vary in digits, wording, and punctuation — a 2026-06-23 string-match scorer manufactured a bogus 42% on self-corrections that were really ~80-90% correct.
  2556	How to apply: Public CI uses its pinned cross-family judge; Type B uses `behavior_judge.py`. To save spend the judge can be this Claude session or Codex (both free); reserve paid judges for CI and final receipts. Corpus assertion fields are authoring context only.

  2594	## RULE: extend-corpus-with-feature
  2595	Rule: Ship public positive, negative, and boundary cases with every new polish capability, then recapture the baseline in the same PR.
  2596	Why: Otherwise the gate cannot detect regression.
  2597	How to apply:
  2598	1. Extend the correct existing category, for example `filler_removal`, or add and document one.
  2599	2. Write 20–50 natural labeled cases: positive (fires), negative (must NOT fire), edge (boundary).
  2600	3. Fill `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` / `must_preserve` / `edit_budget` authoring hints and `expected_output`.
  2601	4. Run `--mode selftest`, then `--mode run --polish-model gpt-4o-mini`.
  2602	5. Recapture baseline with `--mode baseline --reason "<reason>"` and add founder-approved `BASELINE-BUMP:` text.
  2603	6. Corpus + prompt + new baseline ride in the same PR as the feature.

  2606	- Workflow: `.github/workflows/polish-eval-smoke.yml`; job `polish-quality-gate`; advisory.

  2613	## RULE: debug-red-polish-gate
  2614	Rule: Download `polish-eval-pr` and classify each failure as true regression, approved tradeoff, or flaky infra; never baseline-bump to hide red.
  2615	Why: Bumping the baseline to hide a regression is the exact failure this gate prevents.
  2616	How to apply: Read `report.json` `fail_records`: id, category, input, candidate, committed baseline, judge axes, and reasons. True regression → fix prompt, push, CI re-runs. Intentional tradeoff → founder approval + `BASELINE-BUMP: <reason>` tag + `--mode baseline` recapture, commit. Flaky provider → "Re-run failed jobs" in GitHub UI.

  2632	## RULE: apple-runner-bench-verify-build
  2633	Rule: Run `cd scripts/eval/apple_runner && swift build -c release` separately and confirm `Build complete!` before executing the binary; never pipe the build through `tail`.
  2634	Why: A pipe makes the chain's exit status `tail`'s, so a compile error is swallowed and the STALE binary runs (a 2026-06-12 #963 bench silently measured the previous prompt).
  2635	How to apply: Run the same corpus twice and diff outputs when validating binary identity — greedy decoding is deterministic, so any diff means two different binaries. If a new source is omitted from SwiftPM discovery, `touch Package.swift`, rebuild, recheck.

  2637	## FACT: competitor-prompt-bakeoff-pattern
  2638	`apple_runner` resolves `--system-prompt` before `--system-prompt-file` before its built-in fallback; `--help` omits both prompt flags. Use `--system-prompt-file` to isolate prompt text while holding connector, corpus, and judge fixed — the mechanism for benching a competitor's Apple Intelligence prompt apples-to-apples. The 2026-07-08 Vox "General" prompt scored 64.5% / 89 S4 vs v38's 66.3% / 70 S4 on the identical exam. Use the artifacts, not narrative, for future comparisons. Full writeup: `docs/competitive-analysis/2026-07-08-vox-rizen-teardown.md`.

  2641	Prompt wording alone did not eliminate opener deletion: #963 recorded 13/20 onset-marker cases even with a direct "NEVER delete the first word" rule; gpt-4o-mini shows the same failure at ~10% (#1036). `Sources/EnviousWisprLLM/LeadingMarkerRepair.swift` is the shipped AFM-only deterministic repair; `onset_marker` (20 public cases) pins it. See `deterministic-features.md` for the owner.

  2643	## FACT: afm-prompt-iteration-learnings
  2644	Retain these decisions from the v33→v38 work (shipped PR #1086, +11pp on ci151 tier-bench):
  2645	- Examples are the highest-leverage prompt component (ablation: deleting the 2 examples dropped 80.6%→69.3%, −11pp). Prefer formula/principle phrasing over word-lists for rules; use KEEP/ADD examples for contested behaviors (opener-keep, hedge-keep, mid-filler-drop).
  2646	- AFM is brittle to ANY prompt edit — no change is local. A one-rule wording tweak perturbed 11 unrelated outputs (−3pp). Every candidate needs a FULL tier-bench.
  2647	- Judge noise ≈ ±5pp; use reps and ignore sub-5pp deltas.
  2648	- Do not credit prompts for deterministic-owned categories (emoji/number/url/date/custom-vocab); use `deterministic-features.md`.

  2654	## RULE: afm-bench-throttle-cooldown
  2655	Rule: Use at least 0.3s inter-case sleep for sustained direct `apple_runner` runs; on a sudden error cascade, STOP, let the model idle (~6 min), and probe one case before blaming the prompt.
  2656	Why: A no-sleep 151-case run (#1083) drove FoundationModels into a persistent `ModelManagerError 1013` state where every subsequent call fails fast until recovery. Purely a sustained-benchmark artifact; real one-at-a-time dictation never hits it.
  2657	How to apply: Direct runner uses `--sleep-seconds 0.3`; `acceptance_gate.py --mode bench` uses `--afm-sleep-seconds 0.3`. `tier-bench` currently exposes NO sleep option — do not use it for a long AFM sweep without first resolving that parity gap.

  2666	## RULE: never-batch-deny-prone-commands

  2674	## RULE: ten-step-shape
  2675	Rule: Every shipped-product code change follows these 10 ordered steps. Council output feeds Grounded Review, not a separate revision pass. After every PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, revise and repeat Grounded Review until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  2676	
  2677	- **0. Gate 0 — Prior context.** Run `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,state,labels,comments` AND `grep -nE "#<N>([^0-9]|$)" .claude/knowledge/session-log.md`; post one paragraph: `Prior context for #<N>: ...`. If an adopted plan exists, skip to Gate 2. Use `--json`, never bare `--comments` (github-light.md FACT: finding-issues). `check-issue-prior-context.sh` partially enforces new-plan creation; `gate-gh-issue-view.sh` enforces the command shape.
  2678	- **1. Gate 0.5 — User Rubric.** For epics #314 / #316 / #317 / #320 / #321, answer `TEMPLATE.md`’s 9 questions for a named `personas.md` persona; paste all 9 answers, or `User Rubric: N/A — internal-only`, before Gate 1. Enforced structurally by `check-rubric-answered.sh`.
  2679	- **2. Gate 1 — Intent check.** Report user benefit in persona words, UX, value, and preliminary scope. If adding responsibility to a coordinator/manager/App-owned home or introducing one, state: `This will live on [X] because [reason]; the alternative would be [Y] but [trade-off].` Skip that sentence only for prompt/copy/catalog/config. **STOP for approval.**
  2680	- **3. Plan — Grounding brief → Design → self-audit → Council.** Save `TEMPLATE.md` as `docs/feature-requests/issue-<N>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`. Complete §2.5 before §3. Trace producer → owner → consumer end to end, naming each concrete mechanism. Paste code evidence for every symbol, module edge, process/init claim, quoted literal, negative claim, and owner search. Complete §3b Active-epic cross-check after evidence establishes current topology. Before design, run a problem-only Codex consult when the decision depends on topology/who-calls-whom, async/XPC/cancellation/state-machine lifecycle, dependency lifecycle machinery, an unsettled negative infrastructure claim, or an uncertain owner search. Ask for current reality and naive-design traps, not a solution. `check-knowledge-prereads.sh` non-blockingly supplies matching FACT/RULE headings as `additionalContext` and audits read/unread status. Before step 4 and every step-5 round, re-walk §2.5 evidence, sanity-check scope counts, state `self-audit clean` in chat, and revise if false. Council runs only after this sequence.
  2681	- **4. Council — ONE round, coverage only.** Ask: `What did we forget? Premise, placement, metric, workflow-stage, validation-strategy, persona.` Run GPT + Gemini with §2 inline preamble; use persona-roleplay for human-centric features. Save raw outputs to `/tmp/<scope>/{gpt,gemini}-critique.md`. Council does not certify code claims.
  2682	- **5. Grounded Review — iterate to PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.** Run Codex (`codex exec`) read-only. If the plan changes module boundaries, ownership, orchestration, feature placement, dependency direction, or cross-module visibility, instruct Codex to read `.claude/rules/architecture-rules.md` before Q1; its laws are vetoes, not a mandate to invent a deeper layer. **Q1 Direction:** validate structural choice or pivot. **Q2 Fact-check:** classify every council finding TRUE / FALSE / PARTIAL / JUDGMENT-CALL with grep-verified `file:line`. **Q3 Consolidation scan:** lead with dominant root concern yes/no/uncertain, confidence, recommended single owner/tool, consolidation sites, and independent concerns that must not merge. `No consolidation` is valid; correctness/security findings remain mandatory. **Q4 Proposed edits:** every finding includes concise, verbatim, drop-in replacement text; owner: RULE: codex-findings-ship-fixes-and-i-adjudicate. Verdicts: PROCEED-AS-PLANNED / PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS / PIVOT. PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS mandates step 6 and another step 5. Only PROCEED-AS-PLANNED unlocks Gate 2. PIVOT means re-plan. Same-root recurrence across ≥2 rounds means STOP and consolidate to one authority before another round. Backstop: flat/rising unresolved root clusters after 4 rounds means escalate to the founder with a forced choice: consolidate / split PR / rewrite plan / accept-with-documented-rationale / revert partial fixes and restart from a clean plan / declare N independent concerns. For cross-product/FSM surfaces use RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces.
  2683	- **6. Revise — one pass per round.** Apply the Codex verdict and accepted council findings in one edit. PIVOT supersedes the original plan. After PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS, rerun step 5 unconditionally and recheck old plus new defects. Never return to council. Stop only on PROCEED-AS-PLANNED.
  2684	- **7. Gate 2 — Plan sign-off.** Present the revised plan in plain English with blast radius and council/Codex digest. Precondition: step 5 returned PROCEED-AS-PLANNED. Any other verdict at Gate 2 is a process violation. **STOP for approval.**
  2685	- **8. Build.**
  2686	- **9. Phase 3 — validation.** Run `scripts/validate-pr.sh` → `.validation/runs/<timestamp>-<shortsha>/`. Required caller order: logic tests → Codex code-diff, iterated to clean → smoke + Live UAT using ONE rebuild on clean code, never between Codex rounds (RULE: codex-clean-gates-runtime-uat) → push → open PR → evaluate GitHub Codex cloud review before arming auto-merge (local clean ≠ cloud review; github.md RULE: codex-cloud-review-gate) → arm `--auto`. Before push, record any skipped step in `skip-note.txt` or escalate to Stage 2. Smoke is not UAT. Mechanics and lanes: [phase3-validation.md](../knowledge/phase3-validation.md). Note: the current `validate-pr.sh` scaffolder performs smoke before writing its Codex stub; reconcile that script before claiming it enforces this order.

  2789	Rule: When an FSM-terminal capture/read consumes earlier session state, enumerate every path into that terminal and verify: (a) this path sets/freezes the state before transition; (b) for single-winner/latched exits, state is FIRST-WINS under the same latch so later signals cannot decouple it from the winning exit.

  2801	## FACT: tier-routing
  2802	Classify in the GitHub Issue: `Tier: MEDIUM | Test: required (PostProcessing) | Modules: PostProcessing, Core`.
  2803	
  2804	| Tier | Surface |
  2805	|---|---|
  2806	| REFACTOR | `Package.swift`, target/module moves, dependency graph, shared protocol reshaping; any module move or multi-conformer protocol change remains REFACTOR regardless of diff size |
  2807	| LARGE | Pipeline orchestration, XPC boundaries, app startup, both ASR backends |
  2808	| MEDIUM | Audio capture, one ASR backend, Services, permissions, paste path, net-new runtime behavior |
  2809	| SMALL | Isolated post-processing, LLM prompt changes, UI layout/copy, config tweaks |
  2810	
  2811	Escalate upward, never downward. Any code edit after validation invalidates that validation. Tier controls test obligations and runtime breadth via RULE: test-obligations and phase3-validation.md FACT: lane-obligations. Plan/council/Codex gates apply except where RULE: council-skip-zero-blast-radius or RULE: council-skip-codex-grounded-review-settled explicitly allows a skip.
  2812	
  2813	## RULE: test-obligations
  2814	Rule: In testable Core, PostProcessing, LLM, and Pipeline state/routing: bug fixes require a failing `@Test` before the fix; new logic requires `@Test` alongside or before implementation; threshold/scoring/routing changes require just-above, just-below, and ambiguity tests; subtle refactors require characterization tests first. If no test is added, document why in issue and PR.
  2815	How to apply: Use `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; gotchas.md RULE: xcode-test-entrypoint explains why raw `swift test` is not the gate. Runtime-only Audio, XPC, UI, permissions, paste, and hardware are exempt.
  2816	Ref: project test baseline.
  2817	
  2818	## RULE: matcher-set-adversarial-tests
  2819	Rule: When adding to a skip list, allow list, imperative/preservation set, or matcher where set membership flips routing, test the entry in its non-intended semantic class. A positive plus one happy-path negative is insufficient.
  2820	How to apply: Name the intended class, enumerate alternate readings, and add an explicit negative for every meaning-changing alternate. The test harness, not Codex review, must catch it.
  2821	Ref: PR #436.
  2822	
  2823	## RULE: parse-structured-input-dont-regex-and-iterate
  2824	Rule: Before coding a guard/validator/matcher for structured input, including URL path+query, versions, key=value config, semver, or dates, choose a parser and enumerate the full axes × value-classes matrix. Never ship naive substring/regex matching and discover gaps round by round.
  2825	How to apply: List axes, write the complete pass/fail fixture grid, and run a LOCAL adversarial Codex enumeration, `find every input that bypasses each rule across the whole space`, before first push, not through ordinary diff or cloud review. Explicitly document accepted-scope non-authoring inputs such as percent-encoding or backslash normalization.
  2826	Ref: PR #1241; [[matcher-set-adversarial-tests]]; [[async-edge-case-enumeration]].
  2827	
  2828	## RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration
  2829	Rule: Before coding MEDIUM+, enumerate every async operation against six classes: Interrupted (cancelled mid-flight?), Deleted (data deleted while running?), Mutated (settings/config changed in-flight?), Concurrent (two valid user actions overlap?), Nil (weak reference or optional dependency nil; fail open or closed?), and Stale (cached/snapshot value read after completion?). Record every answer in the Issue or PR. Justify accepted edges; otherwise design the guard before the happy path.
  2830	
  2831	**Closed-set trigger, any tier, overriding MEDIUM+:** Run the full `state × event` matrix only when BOTH hold:
  2832	
  2833	1. The change adds, changes, or reinterprets a closed lifecycle, outcome, or durability contract: state/terminal transition, cancellation/preemption route, session identity, or durable save/cleanup/delete/recovery ordering.
  2834	2. Before durable or user-visible commit, two or more ingress classes can affect it: user command, lifecycle/preemption event, timer/task cancellation, or async completion.
  2835	
  2836	ALSO run it when changing the branch that decides whether the heart emits raw text after limb failure, cancellation, or timeout.
  2837	
  2838	Retry, timeout, persistence, status, or fallback mentions alone do not trigger the matrix; use §5/§7-§9 and the six classes. `only`/`exactly`/`never`/`always` are hints, not gates.
  2839	
  2840	Event population: user commands; lifecycle/preemption events including app quit, sleep/wake, device removal, permission revocation, owner deinit, retry timer; and async completions that are absent, duplicate, late, or stale. Enumerate each event’s durable side effects, cleanup, and source-of-truth mutations before terminal state; terminal invariants alone are insufficient.
  2841	
  2842	Run this at plan time from invariant shape. RULE: matrix-review-for-cross-product-surfaces is separate and triggers after 3+ code-diff rounds reveal new cross-product defects.
  2843	Ref: async edge baseline; #1408 (`.discarded`/`.noSpeech` → `.discard` deleted a spool `.audioInterrupted` retained; `KernelDictationDriver.swift` `endedWithoutSaveKind`); `docs/audits/2026-07-10-grounding-rule-grounded-review-r1.txt`.
  2844	
  2845	## RULE: lane-detection-match-plan
  2846	Rule: Tier controls test scope; lane controls Phase 3. Detect lane with `git diff --name-only <merge-base origin/main HEAD>..HEAD`, never plain `origin/main`. The plan’s lane must match detection.
  2847	How to apply: [phase3-validation.md](../knowledge/phase3-validation.md) FACT: lane-obligations solely owns lane globs, obligations, artifacts, and `mixed_pr`. Eval-harness reporting never replaces app Live UAT.
  2848	Ref: `scripts/validate-pr.sh`; `detect_lane_from_diff`.

  2850	## RULE: definition-of-done
  2851	Rule: A change is not done until ALL pass:
  2852	
  2853	1. Xcode release build, `EnviousWispr-Release`.
  2854	2. Logic tests via `scripts/xcode-test.sh`; use `--release` for local reproduction or when full Release-suite execution is specifically required.
  2855	3. Dev `.app` rebuild + relaunch via `/wispr-rebuild-and-relaunch` (`scripts/build-dev-app.sh`).
  2856	4. Each wispr-eyes scope item is VERIFIED or validly SKIPPED per [tools-and-apps.md](./tools-and-apps.md).
  2857	5. Council coverage approval on plan and Codex clean on diff, subject only to explicit skip rules.
  2858	6. If `/ask-gpt` is used, GPT sign-off after rounds to clean.
  2859	7. CI `build-check` green.
  2860	8. Close via `gh issue close <number> --comment "reason"`.
  2861	
  2862	How to apply: Checklist numbering is not run order. Codex-clean item 5 precedes items 3-4; then perform one rebuild and Live UAT per RULE: codex-clean-gates-runtime-uat. Wispr-eyes todos use `Fix X in Y (user-visible result Z)` and a fresh list per project. Architecture-sensitive changes also complete [architecture-rules.md § Architecture Definition of Done](./architecture-rules.md) and include Architecture Closeout in the issue closure comment. `.claude/scripts/check-push-discipline.sh` invokes `scripts/check-dependency-direction.sh` on ship-path pushes and blocks violations; SPM cyclic-import compilation is the second line.
  2863	Ref: project DoD.

  2865	## RULE: grounded-review-mechanics
  2866	Rule: After council, before Gate 2, run `codex exec` against the plan with full codebase access. Require PROCEED-AS-PLANNED / PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS / PIVOT and grep-verified `file:line` corrections. PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS → revise → rerun until PROCEED-AS-PLANNED. No other verdict reaches Gate 2. Every round verifies prior fixes and scans for new defects.
  2867	How to apply: Run `cat <prompt-file> | ~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check > docs/audits/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<scope>-grounded-review[-rN].txt 2>&1` via `Bash run_in_background: true`; run from repo root or use an absolute output path. Round 1 contains unrevised plan, both council critiques, and Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4; Q3 is consolidation, Q4 drop-in fixes. Later rounds contain revised plan, prior revision list, and `verify each landed, scan for new defects.` Skip for zero-blast-radius. Flat/rising defect count after 4 rounds is the escalation signal. Cost is $0 via ChatGPT subscription.

  2887	## RULE: close-the-window-never-handle-it
  2888	Rule: When a plan or invariant says an event CANNOT happen in a window (control disabled, state unreachable), implement the impossibility; never build a handler "to be safe." A handler admits the event, and every admitted event multiplies the state x event surface.
  2889	Why: #1386 PR-1 v1 — the plan said "Settings Remove is DISABLED during the transition"; the build instead grew ~120 lines of removal-deferral machinery. 14 of 30+ defects including all 4 cloud P1s trace to that one deviation (25 review rounds). Corollary (same RCA): on the FIRST defect of a class, audit the whole class (all writers/exits/deletes) before patching the shown instance — patched families recur; audited families die.
  2890	How to apply: In self-review, any code servicing an event the plan ruled out is a defect even if correct. Full RCA: `docs/postmortems/2026-07-11-1386-pr1-defect-cascade.md`; measured context: workflow-effectiveness.md.
  2891	Ref: #1386 PR-1 / PR #1497 (2026-07-11); founder-binding.

  2894	Rule: Port proven state/concurrency patterns whole, including every field and cleanup transition, or state why this instance differs. Never port piecewise across review rounds. If review finds a partial port, stop patching, inventory all fields/transitions, and fix once.

  2899	How to apply: Before founder escalation: fix bugs introduced here in this PR; route earlier-PR contract bugs to follow-up issues; route cutover-only validation to the cutover PR with Live UAT. Record routing in the PR description, not only commits.

  2932	## FACT: eg1-headline-what-it-is
  2933	| Question | Answer |
  2934	|---|---|
  2935	| Full fine-tune or LoRA? | **QLoRA** (LoRA on the 4-bit-quantized base) — NOT a full-parameter retrain. |
  2936	| Adapter shipped separately? | **No.** The LoRA adapter is **merged back into the base weights**, then converted and quantized; there is no runtime "base + adapter." Physical packaging + the current shard identity are owned by [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity (EG-1 ships as 8 componentSet GGUF shards, #1417 — not one file). |
  2937	| Base model | **Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507** (Alibaba, Apache-2.0, the non-thinking variant). |
  2938	| Built from scratch? | No. It is a fine-tuned **derivative** of Qwen3-4B — this is why the README says "fine-tuned derivative of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0)" and the EG-1 license applies to the *fine-tuned weights*, not the base. |
  2939	| Plain-English framing for Saurabh | "We took Alibaba's Qwen 4B, taught it our dictation-cleanup behavior with a QLoRA fine-tune, and baked the result into one custom model. It's ours, but it stands on an open base." |
  2940	
  2941	The one-line honest positioning: **"a QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-4B, merged and quantized."** Do NOT claim "full fine-tune" (false — it's LoRA) and do NOT claim "trained our own model from scratch" (false — Qwen3-4B is the base).

  2943	## FACT: eg1-training-config
  2944	Settled by council + Codex (#1265), trained on the RTX 4090:
  2945	| Knob | Value |
  2946	|---|---|
  2947	| Method | QLoRA via **Unsloth** (CUDA-only; does not run on Apple Silicon) |
  2948	| LoRA rank / alpha | **r16 / a32** |
  2949	| Learning rate | **5e-5** (dropped from the research doc's 2e-4 starting point) |
  2950	| Epochs | **2** |
  2951	| Loss | **response-only** (loss on the cleaned output, not the transcript/prompt) |
  2952	| Target modules | all attention + MLP projections |
  2953	| Precision | bf16, adamw_8bit, gradient checkpointing |
  2954	| Rig | **AlienSV RTX 4090** (24 GB, WSL2 Ubuntu), always-on via Tailscale. **$0 spend** — owned hardware, no cloud GPU. |
  2955	| Division of labor | TRAIN on the PC, EVAL on the Mac (llama.cpp/Ollama + judge harness), ship the merged GGUF back over Tailscale. |
  2956

  2959	## FACT: eg1-build-pipeline
  2960	The end-to-end pipeline (mirror of Fluid-1's exact approach — competitor-proven):
  2961	```
  2962	QLoRA train (4090)  →  merge adapter into base  →  GGUF convert  →  Q5_K_M quantize  →  judge the QUANTIZED artifact
  2963	```
  2964	- **Judge the quantized artifact, never the fp16 checkpoint.** The shipped quality number must be measured on exactly the GGUF users run. (Q5_K_M was chosen over Q4_K_M: Q4 scored 86.5% vs Q5 88.8% on the hard-340 at bake-off; the feared Qwen-Q4 collapse did not materialize, but Q5's ~2pp edge + fewer criticals won.)
  2965	- Shipped quant: **Q5_K_M, ~2.7–2.9 GB total**. Current sharded artifact identity + exact per-shard SHAs: [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity.
  2966	
  2967	## FACT: eg1-training-data
  2968	Two data generations; **v2 is what shipped** (`train_sft_v2.jsonl`, **5,656 pairs**). Format is flat `{id, source, input(raw) → output(cleaned)}` JSONL.
  2969	- **v1 (3,036 pairs):** SFT built from 1,549 Type-B-approved rows after excluding the hard-340 IDs/texts, plus founder dictations. The exclusion protected the hard-340 exact cases, not the full 1,890 working set. The 900-case overflow set stayed exact-text sealed but was derived from the same provenance families.
  2970	- **v2 = v1 + 1,924 teacher-distilled real dictations** (teacher = gemini-2.5-flash + the v6 cloud prompt; hallucination-filtered, noop-capped) **+ 696 targeted convention drills.**
  2971	- **Leakage correction (2026-07-15):** shipping v2 has exact ID and normalized-input overlap with **1,549/1,890** full Type B rows; conservative normalization finds 1,551. Provenance-family components expose 1,866/1,890 approved rows and 899/900 overflow rows. The old zero-overlap statement conflated the protected hard-340/exact-overflow checks with the broader working set. The old 1,890 and overflow scores are historical development/robustness evidence, not held-out quality estimates. Owner receipt: `docs/experiments/eg1-multilingual/OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md` TYPE-B-001.
  2972	- **Prompt = training contract:** the model was trained AND ships with ONE fixed short system prompt + `<TRANSCRIPT>…</TRANSCRIPT>` wrapper (`scripts/eval/prompts/eg1-polish-prompt-v1.txt`, pinned by a golden-string test in `EGOnePromptBuilder`). Training prompt MUST equal inference prompt — prompt-shape drift cost ±18pp on the untuned base. This is why EG-1 gets its own `.egOneFixed` prompt family and ignores per-mode prompt rules (behavior is in the weights).
  2973	
  2974	## FACT: eg1-quality-and-bias-gate
  2975	Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. (Numbers here are the #1265 acceptance run; note the separate marketing-vs-settings discrepancy tracked in `eg1-operations.md` FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines — 94.4/94.7 internal vs 93.7 public, same model, different run.)
  2976	- **Hard-340 subset:** 94.7%, **0 critical fails** (beat the gpt-4o + v6 cloud champion same-batch: 93.5%, 2 crit).
  2977	- **Full 1,890:** 94.4% (traps 97.3%, false-positive 2.4%).
  2978	- **Historical one-time bias gate:** exact-text-sealed 900-overflow scored 88.0% vs untuned-base anchor 61.2%; Type-C mixed slice 94.5%; 100 train-excluded real dictations ~95%. This does not prove held-out generalization because the 2026-07-15 provenance audit found 899/900 overflow rows in training-exposed Type B families.
  2979	
  2980	## FACT: eg1-language-coverage-provenance
  2981	- **Trained overwhelmingly on English.** The v2 corpus is English-oriented `raw → cleaned` dictation data, but it is not literally ASCII-only. The historical quality numbers above are English.
  2982	- **Base is multilingual** (Qwen3-4B handles ~100+ languages) and the fixed prompt says "keep the same language … never translate," so EG-1 will *accept* and attempt to polish non-English — but that rides on base-model ability, un-benchmarked per-language. Lower-resourced languages will be rougher.
  2983	- **Multilingual training pairs are an explicit v3 lever** (epic #1190 follow-ups), not shipped in EG-1 v1/v2.
  2984	- Do not conflate with transcription: the ASR engines (Parakeet = English + 24 European; WhisperKit = 99) are a separate stage feeding EG-1 (`architecture.md`).
  2985	
  2986	## RULE: eg1-retrain-recipe-for-eg2
  2987	Rule: To build EG-2 (or EG-1 v3), reuse this exact pipeline — QLoRA (Unsloth, 4090) → merge → GGUF → quantize → judge the quantized artifact against the SEALED holdout — and keep the training prompt byte-identical to the shipped prompt. A PROMPT change means a new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case (see `eg1-operations.md` RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract); a weights-only update keeps the template id.
  2988	Why: prompt-shape drift alone swings quality ±18pp; judging fp16 instead of the quantized GGUF ships a number users never see.
  2989	How to apply: expand data on the v2 recipe (synthetic + teacher-distilled real dictations + targeted drills), preserve zero-overlap with the eval, re-run the one-time bias gate on any new data generation, and route any prompt-family change through a code-lane PR. Distribution (R2 upload, manifest bump) is `eg1-operations.md`.
  2990	Ref: #1265 method-of-record; #1190 epic.

  3029	## RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract
  3030	Rule: Shipping EG-1 v2 / EG-2 = upload the new artifact set + license to R2; update `eg1-delivery-manifest.json` with the new revision, per-shard file paths + measured `sizeBytes`/`sha256`, `totalBytes`, and `admission.layout`/`entrypointFile` (this manifest owns hashes/sizes/layout); then update `eg1-manifest.json`'s runtime config to match (`version`, `contextTokens`/`promptTemplateID`/`minAppVersion`/`licenseURL`) — `eg1-manifest.json` no longer carries `sha256`/`sizeBytes` (dead fields removed #1417, see FACT: eg1-artifact-identity). Keep `modelName`/`promptTemplateID` unless the PROMPT changed; bump `minAppVersion` if runtime behavior requires it. Zero code changes unless the prompt template changes (then: new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case + builder; unknown template IDs read RED "app_update_required" in old apps by design).
  3031	Why: `EGOneRuntime` refuses manifests whose `modelName != "eg-1"` (fixed Core literal `LLMProvider.egOneModelName`); `refreshInstalledState` purges the previous version's artifact family automatically (extension-scoped).
  3032	How to apply: R2 upload runbook below; validate the new host object with HEAD (etag+length), a Range request (expect 206), and a full curl+shasum before updating the manifest.
  3033	Ref: #1271 plan §hot-swap; purge added Codex r11.
  3034	
  3035	## FACT: kill-switch-stops-mutation-not-format-drift (#1386 PR-1, 2026-07-11)
  3036	`modelDelivery.egOne.enabled=false` guarantees exactly ONE thing: no EG-1 model bytes are moved, deleted, or fetched. It does NOT guarantee polish keeps working, and for one cohort it structurally cannot.
  3037	
  3038	A user still on the previously-shipped MONOLITH (`eg-1-v1.gguf`, every release ≤ v2.3.2) holds bytes a sharded build cannot load at all: `EGOneRuntime` boots `manifest.resolvedEntrypointPath` (shard 1), so no directory choice makes a monolith loadable. Turning the switch off therefore leaves that user with raw text (EG-1 is a limb) and their model completely untouched; turning it back on runs the migration and polish returns. Nothing is lost, only deferred.
  3039	
  3040	**Do NOT "fix" this by restoring the monolithic load path.** That means shipping the old manifest AND the old load path alongside the new ones, permanently — dual-format support carried forever for a rollback lever. Rejected on scope (founder 2026-07-11: don't over-engineer). Codex PR-1 review r14 raised it as DIAGNOSIS-ONLY; the resolution is this documented limitation, not code.
  3041	
  3042	Corollary for any FUTURE model-format change (EG-2, a new quantization): the kill switch is a byte-mutation stop, not a version rollback. If a format change ever needs a true rollback, that is a deliberate design (ship both manifests), not something the flag gives you for free.
  3043	
  3044	## FACT: eg1-monolith-retirement-and-owned-home (#1386 PR-1, PR #1500, 2026-07-11)
  3045	Shipped delivery shape since PR #1500: EG-1 installs to `~/Library/Application Support/EnviousWispr/Models/eg-1` (owned home; old `PolishModels` is the RETIRED store). At launch `EGOneLegacyUpgradeCoordinator` retires the one shipped monolith (`eg-1-v1.gguf`, 2_889_511_680 bytes, sha256 `3343fc1a...74f6`) by exact size+digest proof: containment gate (resolved-to-resolved, firmlink-safe) → durable `eg1-v1-replacement-owed` marker in `ModelDelivery/` → delete → normal ModelDeliveryController download. Marker clears ONLY on admission or explicit Cancel/Remove (decline counts even kill-switched — contract §5c.10). Post-replacement the RUNTIME decides activation via `activateAfterAutomaticReplacementIfNeeded()` (live `isActiveProvider`; the install-state stream never activates). Telemetry: `eg1.legacy_detected` (+`selected_provider`) / `legacy_retired` / `legacy_retirement_failed(reason: marker_write|delete|unreadable|containment)` / `replacement_completed` / `replacement_declined`; release ship-criterion: every detected distinct_id eventually shows completed/declined/diagnosable-failed. UAT fixture: genuine monolith kept at `~/Developer/EnviousLabs/eg1-uat-fixture/eg-1-v1.gguf` (digest-verified; monolith still hosted at models.enviouslabs.co/eg1/eg-1-v1-q5km.gguf).   3052	## FACT: eg1-shard-authoring-runbook (#1417, 2026-07-08)
  3053	Splitting EG-1 into CDN-cache-eligible shards (each safely under Cloudflare's 512MB ceiling, target ≤450MB per the Phase-3 warn line) reuses `llama.cpp`'s native `gguf-split` tool and the shared delivery engine's existing `componentSet` layout (already proven by Parakeet's 23-file case) — no new reassembly code, no changes to `ManifestFetchTask`/`CacheAdmission`. One-time steps when cutting a new sharded EG-1 revision:
  3054	1. **Split:** run `gguf-split` against the real (unsplit) model weights, choosing `--split-max-tensors` so every output shard lands comfortably under 450MB (shards are NOT byte-range slices — each is an independently-headered valid GGUF file with its own metadata, so per-shard size varies with tensor boundaries, never assume equal division).
  3055	2. **Measure, never assume:** compute each shard's real `sizeBytes`/`sha256` from the actual output files — the manifest's `totalBytes` must equal the measured sum, and every `sizeBytes` must be re-verified ≤450MB after the real split (the pre-split total does not divide evenly by shard count).
  3056	3. **Upload:** each shard to R2 (`r2-hosting-runbook` above) under a NEW versioned sub-path (e.g. `/eg1/v2-sharded/`) — never reuse the legacy single-file path, so the new Cloudflare Cache Rule (scoped to the new sub-path only) can never accidentally match the old monolithic file, which is over the cache-eligible size ceiling.
  3057	4. **Author the manifest:** `admission.layout: "componentSet"`, `admission.entrypointFile` naming the shard `DeliveryManifest.resolvedEntrypointPath`/`EGOneDeliveryAdapter.installedArtifactURL` should boot from (shard 1, by `llama.cpp` convention — it auto-discovers siblings by filename pattern once pointed at shard 1), one `files[]` entry per shard with real measured hash/size.
  3058	5. **Validate before shipping:** every `sizeBytes` ≤450,000,000; `totalBytes` == sum of `files[].sizeBytes`; `entrypointFile` resolves to exactly one `resolvedInstallPath` (enforced by `DeliveryManifest.validateStructure()`, throws otherwise); no duplicate `installPath` values (already enforced); every shard file on disk matches its declared `sha256` before upload.
  3059	6. **Cloudflare Cache Rule + Transform Rule:** scope to `starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/eg1/v2-sharded/")` (or whatever the new sub-path is) — same shape as Parakeet's rule (edge TTL 1y, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, no-transform`). This is a production infra mutation, executed with explicit founder go, separate from the code/manifest change.
  3060	Existing EG-1 installs on the OLD single-file manifest are swept as stale download sidecars by `EGOneDeliveryAdapter.migrateLegacyStoreArtifacts()`'s version-agnostic cleanup and re-download once under the new manifest — the old file stays usable throughout (deleted only after the new N-shard set fully verifies and promotes, via `CacheAdmission`'s existing promote-time orphan cleanup). Full plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1417-2026-07-08-eg1-cdn-sharding.md`.

  3069	All exits verified live 2026-07-02 (kill drills + AX switch drill):
  3070	| Event | Behavior |
  3071	|---|---|
  3072	| Provider switch away | server killed, RAM freed (defers while a recording froze `.egOne`; terminal-state retry) |
  3073	| App quit | synchronous kill via `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` mirror (`applicationWillTerminate`) |
  3074	| App crash orphan | pkill sweep (anchored regex, exact binary path) — in-spawn + actor-gated `reapOrphansIfIdle` on every no-spawn launch path |
  3075	| Crash once | restart-once (~1 s warm) |
  3076	| Crash twice | stays down; recovery = settings-open probe or provider re-pick or relaunch |
  3077	| Critical memory pressure | killed even while starting |
  3078	| Dictation while dead | silent raw paste (~0.5 s; `local_polish_not_ready`) — verified live |

  3080	## FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines
  3081	Quality: 92.4% behavior / 0 critical on hard-340 at exact ship config (native; same artifact via Ollama scored 89.7%); 94.7% on full 1,890 (the number quoted in settings UI copy). Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. **ACCEPTED NUMBER SPLIT (founder decision 2026-07-05, do NOT re-raise):** in-app settings/release copy keeps **94.7%** (original internal full-1,890 run); the public README + r/macapps post use **93.7%** from the later reproducible `scripts/eval/runs/type-b-1199/eg1_native_shipped_1890/scores/summary.json` (`pass_rate_pct`, same `--system new` judge). This ~1pp split is a deliberate accepted state, not an open reconcile item — do not silently change either number (session-log 2026-07-05). Perf (live, M4 Pro): typical dictations 0.3-0.9 s polish, e2e 0.8-1.3 s Parakeet / 1.9-2.2 s WhisperKit; 1,817 chars in 8.0 s (~230 chars/s throughput). Re-benchmark recipe: `scripts/eval/subset_polish_runner.py --endpoint` against a locally-launched server with the SHIPPING flags (never via Ollama — different runtime, different numbers; see [ollama-operations.md](ollama-operations.md)).
  3082	**Shipped-config topic_shift regression (2026-07-05, NOT root-caused):** on the Type B 1,890 exam, `topic_shift` (paragraph breaks) scored 97% via the tuning harness but 78% through the shipped engine (−19pp), driving nearly the whole 94.4→93.7 gap (e.g. TS-026/TS-028 emit zero `\n\n` where the tuning outputs broke between topics). Same Q5_K_M model both runs, so the suspect is the SHIPPING RUNTIME config — most likely the q8_0 KV-cache quantization (the 4.1 GB-footprint choice, FACT: eg1-runtime-config) degrading long-range structuring. Clean test = re-run with fp16 KV cache (`--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16`) and see if topic_shift recovers. Possible customer-facing product issue (worse paragraph breaks than the tuned model can deliver); founder to decide whether to chase. Benchmark methodology owner: [polish-eval.md](polish-eval.md).

  3084	## FACT: eg1-list-formatting-trigger
  3085	EG-1 builds a real **bullet list** from a lead-in phrase followed by a natural run of items with **no spoken ordinals** ("the team needs to confirm backups, feature flags, and the traffic drain" → lead-in `:` then one `- item` per line). Spoken ordinals ("first do X, second do Y, third Z") stay INLINE as sentences — the model reads them as sequential steps, not a list. Verified: `scripts/eval/corpus/list_format_v1.jsonl` + the shipped `type-b-1199/eg1_native_shipped_1890` run passed 74/100 list cases with real bullet output on exactly the lead-in-plus-run pattern; a founder demo dictation using "first/second/third" produced inline prose twice (2026-07-05). Implication for demos/marketing: to SHOW EG-1 building a list, script a lead-in + comma-run, never ordinals. Paragraph structuring + self-correction + filler removal work regardless of phrasing. A true marker list is an EG-1 / cloud behavior, NOT an Apple Intelligence one (AFM list detection is run-to-run inconsistent, confirmed live).

  3088	Rule: EVERY EG-1 numeric threshold is a PROVISIONAL dial pending measured calibration (#1277) — treat none of them as design constraints; each is one constant at one site, changeable with data + eval gate. FOUNDER DIRECTIVE (2026-07-02): the 15 s polish budget WILL likely change — it is the top calibration item and must never be written about or planned around as a hard rule.
  3089	| Dial | Current | Status |
  3090	|---|---|---|
  3091	| Polish time budget | 15 s (`LLMPolishStep` maxDuration) | PROVISIONAL — the de-facto length limit (~3,000 chars at measured 230 chars/s), binds before the token cap; founder expects to raise |
  3092	| Context preflight | worst-case both sides (~8k chars) | PROVISIONAL — deliberately conservative; llama-server usage fields give true per-script ratios |
  3093	| Probe "slow" | 5 s | guess; measure warm-probe distribution |
  3094	| Disk preflight | 2.2× (partial bytes count as reclaimable) | guess; fine unless telemetry shows disk failures |
  3095	| Crash-retry delay | 750 ms single retry | cannot beat ~9 s cold reload (accepted r17); a second retry ~1.5 s would rescue warm-restart (~1 s) crashes — decide from telemetry |
  3096	How to apply: failure direction is always "raw text pasted" (silent), never truncation/error — `finish_reason == length` skips whole. Change a dial → update this table + #1277 in the same session.

  3105	## FACT: eg1-download-drain-gate (#1287/#1279, PR #1322, 2026-07-04)
  3106	Cancel→Try Again is single-flight through a drain gate in `EGOneModelStore`: cancel/remove stash the live task as `drainingTask` (guarded — nil never clobbers a pending drain), an accepted retry publishes `.downloading(existingFraction)` synchronously at acceptance (instant Cancel; no dead Try Again while draining), awaits the predecessor's `Task.value` before running (task completion IS the drain signal: delegate continuation resumes only on `didCompleteWithError`, then the handle closes), and `runDownload` refuses stale generations before any disk touch. NO timer escape by design (`timeout-numbers-need-distribution-evidence`); a wedged drain presents as a stalled download with live Cancel, diagnosable via the debug drain-wait log lines ("EG-1 retry waiting for cancelled download to drain" / "drain wait finished in ..."). Tests are negative-control validated (protection removed → test fails); lesson: an absence-of-effect test window must outlast the un-gated mutation latency — pre-warm `AppLogger` in the test or first-time logger init masks the violation. Live drill precedent (real host, same-second cancel/retry at 15%/40%, resume + verified install): session-log 2026-07-04.

  3473	   102	    value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold()
  3474	   103	    return re.sub(r"[^\w]+", " ", value, flags=re.UNICODE).strip()

  3481	   110	def file_sha256(path: Path) -> str:
  3482	   111	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
  3483	   112	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
  3484	   113	        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
  3485	   114	            digest.update(chunk)
  3486	   115	    return digest.hexdigest()

  3489	   118	def char_ngrams(value: str, size: int = 4) -> frozenset[str]:
  3490	   119	    compact = value.replace(" ", "_")
  3491	   120	    if len(compact) < size:
  3492	   121	        return frozenset({compact}) if compact else frozenset()
  3493	   122	    return frozenset(compact[index : index + size] for index in range(len(compact) - size + 1))

  3496	   125	def jaccard(left: frozenset[str], right: frozenset[str]) -> float:
  3497	   126	    if not left or not right:
  3498	   127	        return 0.0
  3499	   128	    return len(left & right) / len(left | right)

  3502	   131	def similarity(left: AuditInput, right: AuditInput) -> tuple[float, dict[str, float]]:
  3503	   132	    length_ratio = min(len(left.normalized), len(right.normalized)) / max(
  3504	   133	        len(left.normalized), len(right.normalized), 1
  3505	   134	    )
  3506	   135	    sequence_ratio = 0.0
  3507	   136	    if length_ratio >= 0.50:
  3508	   137	        sequence_ratio = SequenceMatcher(None, left.normalized, right.normalized, autojunk=False).ratio()
  3509	   138	    scores = {
  3510	   139	        "sequence_ratio": sequence_ratio,
  3511	   140	        "token_jaccard": jaccard(left.tokens, right.tokens),
  3512	   141	        "char_4gram_jaccard": jaccard(left.char_4grams, right.char_4grams),
  3513	   142	    }
  3514	   143	    return max(scores.values()), scores

  3517	   146	def input_value(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
  3518	   147	    for field in INPUT_FIELDS:
  3519	   148	        value = row.get(field)
  3520	   149	        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
  3521	   150	            return value
  3522	   151	    return None

  3525	   154	def load_json_rows_bytes(path: Path, value: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
  3526	   155	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
  3527	   156	    try:
  3528	   157	        text = value.decode("utf-8")
  3529	   158	    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
  3530	   159	        raise ValueError(f"{path} is not UTF-8") from error
  3531	   160	    if path.suffix == ".jsonl":
  3532	   161	        for line_number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
  3533	   162	            if not line.strip():
  3534	   163	                continue
  3535	   164	            row = json.loads(line)
  3536	   165	            if not isinstance(row, dict):
  3537	   166	                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{line_number} is not a JSON object")
  3538	   167	            rows.append(row)
  3539	   168	        return rows
  3540	   169	    parsed = json.loads(text)
  3541	   170	    if isinstance(parsed, list):
  3542	   171	        rows = parsed
  3543	   172	    elif isinstance(parsed, dict):
  3544	   173	        for key in ("rows", "cases", "data"):
  3545	   174	            if isinstance(parsed.get(key), list):
  3546	   175	                rows = parsed[key]
  3547	   176	                break
  3548	   177	    if not rows or not all(isinstance(row, dict) for row in rows):
  3549	   178	        raise ValueError(f"{path} has no supported row array")
  3550	   179	    return rows
  3551	   180	
  3552	   181	
  3553	   182	def load_json_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
  3554	   183	    return load_json_rows_bytes(path, path.read_bytes())

  3557	   186	def load_audit_sources(paths: list[str]) -> tuple[list[AuditInput], list[dict[str, Any]], set[str]]:
  3558	   187	    audit_inputs: list[AuditInput] = []
  3559	   188	    inventories: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
  3560	   189	    families: set[str] = set()
  3561	   190	    for raw_path in paths:
  3562	   191	        path = Path(raw_path).resolve()
  3563	   192	        if not path.is_file():
  3564	   193	            raise ValueError(f"audit source does not exist: {path}")
  3565	   194	        source_bytes = path.read_bytes()
  3566	   195	        rows = load_json_rows_bytes(path, source_bytes)
  3567	   196	        source_sha = sha256_bytes(source_bytes)
  3568	   197	        input_count = 0
  3569	   198	        for index, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
  3570	   199	            family = row.get("family")
  3571	   200	            if isinstance(family, str) and family.strip():
  3572	   201	                families.add(normalized(family))
  3573	   202	            value = input_value(row)
  3574	   203	            if value is None:
  3575	   204	                continue
  3576	   205	            key = normalized(value)
  3577	   206	            if not key:
  3578	   207	                continue
  3579	   208	            input_count += 1
  3580	   209	            audit_inputs.append(
  3581	   210	                AuditInput(
  3582	   211	                    source=str(path),
  3583	   212	                    source_id=str(row.get("id", index)),
  3584	   213	                    normalized=key,
  3585	   214	                    tokens=frozenset(key.split()),
  3586	   215	                    char_4grams=char_ngrams(key),
  3587	   216	                )
  3588	   217	            )
  3589	   218	        inventories.append(
  3590	   219	            {
  3591	   220	                "path": str(path),
  3592	   221	                "sha256": source_sha,
  3593	   222	                "row_count": len(rows),
  3594	   223	                "input_count": input_count,
  3595	   224	            }
  3596	   225	        )
  3597	   226	    if not audit_inputs:
  3598	   227	        raise ValueError("audit sources contain no input/asr_input/raw/transcript values")
  3599	   228	    return audit_inputs, inventories, families

  3602	   231	def pairwise_balance(specs: list[CaseSpec]) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
  3603	   232	    axes = ("domain", "case_type", "item_count", "length_bucket", "compound_required")
  3604	   233	    axis_values = {
  3605	   234	        axis: sorted({getattr(spec, axis) for spec in specs}, key=str)
  3606	   235	        for axis in axes
  3607	   236	    }
  3608	   237	    result: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
  3609	   238	    for left_index, left in enumerate(axes):
  3610	   239	        for right in axes[left_index + 1 :]:
  3611	   240	            counts: Counter[str] = Counter(
  3612	   241	                f"{getattr(spec, left)}|{getattr(spec, right)}" for spec in specs
  3613	   242	            )
  3614	   243	            result[f"{left}_x_{right}"] = {
  3615	   244	                f"{left_value}|{right_value}": counts[f"{left_value}|{right_value}"]
  3616	   245	                for left_value, right_value in product(axis_values[left], axis_values[right])
  3617	   246	            }
  3618	   247	    return result
  3619	   248	
  3620	   249	
  3621	   250	def balanced_specs(role: str, count: int, seed: int) -> list[CaseSpec]:
  3622	   251	    if count <= 0 or count % 20:
  3623	   252	        raise ValueError("--count-per-role must be a positive multiple of 20")
  3624	   253	    case_types = POSITIVE_TYPES if role == "positive_list" else RESTRAINT_TYPES
  3625	   254	    repeats = count // (len(DOMAINS) * len(case_types))
  3626	   255	    slots = [
  3627	   256	        (domain, case_type, repeat, bool((domain_index + type_index + repeat) % 2))
  3628	   257	        for domain_index, domain in enumerate(DOMAINS)
  3629	   258	        for type_index, case_type in enumerate(case_types)
  3630	   259	        for repeat in range(repeats)
  3631	   260	    ]

  3853	   222	def role_losses(model: dict[str, Any], role: str, key: str) -> int:
  3854	   223	    return sum(
  3855	   224	        row["inference_ok"] and not row[key]
