  7237	   785	def scan(*, contract: dict[str, Any], benchmark_rows: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], sources: dict[tuple[str, str], Path], backend_name: str, embedding_backend: EmbeddingBackend, source_bytes: dict[tuple[str, str], bytes] | None = None) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], str]:
  7238	   786	    candidate_inputs, candidate_outputs = text_sides(benchmark_rows, "benchmark")
  7239	   787	    candidate_texts = candidate_inputs + candidate_outputs
  7240	   788	    if not candidate_texts:
  7241	   789	        raise ValueError("benchmark has no scannable text")
  7242	   790	    results = []
  7243	   791	    synthetic_thresholds = contract["synthetic_test_only_thresholds"]
  7244	   792	    for (role, name), path in sorted(sources.items()):
  7245	   793	        value = source_bytes[(role, name)] if source_bytes is not None else path.read_bytes()
  7246	   794	        rows = read_records_bytes(value, f"{role}:{name}")
  7247	   795	        texts = extract_texts(rows)
  7248	   796	        source = {"role": role, "name": name, "sha256": sha256_bytes(value), "record_count": len(rows), "authenticated_raw_text_count": len(texts)}
  7249	   797	        methods: dict[str, Any] = {}
  7250	   798	        if role in REGISTRY_ROLES:
  7251	   799	            if texts:
  7252	   800	                raise ValueError(f"{role}:{name} registry unexpectedly contains raw text")
  7253	   801	            registry_values = {str(value) for row in rows for value in row.values() if isinstance(value, str)}
  7254	   802	            if role == "blocked_text_hash_registry":
  7255	   803	                candidate_values = {
  7256	   804	                    sha256_bytes(v2.normalize_text(value).encode("utf-8"))
  7257	   805	                    for value in candidate_texts
  7258	   806	                }
  7259	   807	            else:
  7260	   808	                candidate_values = {
  7261	   809	                    str(row["semantic_family_id"])
  7262	   810	                    for row in benchmark_rows
  7263	   811	                    if isinstance(row.get("semantic_family_id"), str)
  7264	   812	                }
  7265	   813	            matches = candidate_values & registry_values
  7266	   814	            methods["exact_normalized"] = {"status": "passed" if not matches else "failed", "matches": len(matches)}
  7267	   815	            for method in METHODS[1:]:
  7268	   816	                methods[method] = {"status": "not_applicable_no_raw_text", "authenticated_raw_text_count": 0}
  7269	   817	        elif role in RAW_ROLES:
  7270	   818	            if not texts:
  7271	   819	                raise ValueError(f"{role}:{name} has no authenticated raw text")
  7272	   820	            normalized_candidates = [v2.normalize_text(value) for value in candidate_texts]
  7273	   821	            normalized_sources = [v2.normalize_text(value) for value in texts]
  7274	   822	            exact = set(normalized_candidates) & set(normalized_sources)
  7275	   823	            exact_violations = sum(left == right for left in normalized_candidates for right in normalized_sources)
  7276	   824	            thresholds = synthetic_thresholds if backend_name == "synthetic_test_only" else {method: None for method in METHODS[1:]}
  7277	   825	            source_inputs, source_outputs = text_sides(rows, role)
  7278	   826	            embedding_axes = {
  7279	   827	                "input_input": cosine_stats(candidate_inputs, source_inputs, embedding_backend, thresholds["embedding_cosine"]),
  7280	   828	                "output_output": cosine_stats(candidate_outputs, source_outputs, embedding_backend, thresholds["embedding_cosine"]),
  7281	   829	                "input_output": cosine_stats(candidate_inputs, source_outputs, embedding_backend, thresholds["embedding_cosine"]),
  7282	   830	                "output_input": cosine_stats(candidate_outputs, source_inputs, embedding_backend, thresholds["embedding_cosine"]),
  7283	   831	            }
  7284	   832	            embedding_axis_counts = {
  7285	   833	                "input_input": len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_inputs),
  7286	   834	                "output_output": len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_outputs),
  7287	   835	                "input_output": len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_outputs),
  7288	   836	                "output_input": len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_inputs),
  7289	   837	            }
  7290	   838	            scores = {
  7291	   839	                "token_ngram_jaccard": pairwise_jaccard_stats(candidate_texts, texts, width=contract["token_ngram_width"], characters=False, threshold=thresholds["token_ngram_jaccard"]),
  7292	   840	                "character_ngram_jaccard": pairwise_jaccard_stats(candidate_texts, texts, width=contract["character_ngram_width"], characters=True, threshold=thresholds["character_ngram_jaccard"]),
  7293	   841	                "embedding_cosine": (max(value[0] for value in embedding_axes.values()), None if backend_name == "production" else sum(value[1] or 0 for value in embedding_axes.values())),
  7294	   842	            }
  7295	   843	            comparisons = len(candidate_texts) * len(texts)
  7296	   844	            methods["exact_normalized"] = {"status": "passed" if not exact else "failed", "matches": len(exact), "comparison_count": comparisons, "violation_count": exact_violations}
  7297	   845	            for method, (score, violation_count) in scores.items():
  7298	   846	                if backend_name == "production":
  7299	   847	                    status, threshold = "calibration_required", None
  7300	   848	                else:
  7301	   849	                    threshold = synthetic_thresholds[method]
  7302	   850	                    status = threshold_status(score, threshold)
  7303	   851	                methods[method] = {"status": status, "maximum_score": round(score, 8), "threshold": threshold, "comparison_count": comparisons, "violation_count": violation_count}
  7304	   852	                if method == "embedding_cosine":
  7305	   853	                    methods[method]["comparison_count"] = len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_inputs) + len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_outputs) + len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_outputs) + len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_inputs)
  7306	   854	                    methods[method]["axes"] = {axis: {"maximum_score": round(values[0], 8), "violation_count": values[1], "comparison_count": embedding_axis_counts[axis]} for axis, values in embedding_axes.items()}
  7307	   855	        else:
  7308	   856	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported leakage role: {role}")
  7309	   857	        results.append({"source": source, "methods": methods})
  7310	   858	    all_exact = all(row["methods"]["exact_normalized"]["status"] == "passed" for row in results)
  7311	   859	    if backend_name == "production":
  7312	   860	        overall = "calibration_required_noncertifying" if all_exact else "failed"
  7313	   861	    else:
  7314	   862	        statuses = [method["status"] for row in results for method in row["methods"].values()]
  7315	   863	        overall = "synthetic_not_quality_evidence" if all(value in {"passed", "not_applicable_no_raw_text"} for value in statuses) else "failed"
  7316	   864	    return results, overall

  7393	   130	def model_family(config: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  7394	   131	    model_type = str(config.get("model_type", "")).casefold().replace("_", "")
  7395	   132	    architectures = " ".join(str(item) for item in config.get("architectures", []))
  7396	   133	    if "qwen35" in model_type or "qwen3_5" in architectures.casefold():
  7397	   134	        return QWEN35_FAMILY
  7398	   135	    if "gemma" in model_type or "gemma" in architectures.casefold():
  7399	   136	        return "gemma"
  7400	   137	    return "other"

  7404	   141	    resolved = BF16_LORA_MODE if family == QWEN35_FAMILY else QLORA_MODE
  7405	   142	    if requested != "auto":

  7413	   150	        raise ValueError("BF16 LoRA is currently implemented only for Qwen3.5")

  7630	   230	def mechanical_gate(report: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
  7631	   231	    baseline = report["models"]["baseline"]
  7632	   232	    candidate = report["models"]["candidate"]
  7633	   233	    comparison = next(
  7634	   234	        item
  7635	   235	        for item in report["paired_comparisons"]
  7636	   236	        if item["left_model"] == "baseline" and item["right_model"] == "candidate"
  7637	   237	    )
  7638	   238	    positive = comparison["positive_strict"]
  7639	   239	    net_gain = positive["right_only"] - positive["left_only"]
  7640	   240	    baseline_by_id = {row["id"]: row for row in baseline["case_results"]}
  7641	   241	    candidate_by_id = {row["id"]: row for row in candidate["case_results"]}
  7642	   242	    restraint_ids = [
  7643	   243	        case_id
  7644	   244	        for case_id, row in baseline_by_id.items()
  7645	   245	        if row["role"] == "prose_restraint"
  7646	   246	    ]
  7647	   247	    candidate_only_false_lists = [
  7648	   248	        case_id
  7649	   249	        for case_id in restraint_ids
  7650	   250	        if candidate_by_id[case_id]["false_list"] and not baseline_by_id[case_id]["false_list"]
  7651	   251	    ]
  7652	   252	    loss_checks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
  7653	   253	    for role in ("positive_list", "prose_restraint"):
  7654	   254	        for key in ("items_preserved", "scope_preserved"):
  7655	   255	            name = f"{role}.{key.replace('_preserved', '_loss')}"
  7656	   256	            baseline_loss = role_losses(baseline, role, key)
  7657	   257	            candidate_loss = role_losses(candidate, role, key)
  7658	   258	            loss_checks[name] = {
  7659	   259	                "baseline": baseline_loss,
  7660	   260	                "candidate": candidate_loss,
  7661	   261	                "pass": candidate_loss <= baseline_loss,
  7662	   262	            }
  7663	   263	
  7664	   264	    conditions = {
  7665	   265	        "both_arms_inference_healthy": {
  7666	   266	            "pass": baseline["inference_failure_count"] == 0
  7667	   267	            and candidate["inference_failure_count"] == 0,
  7668	   268	        },
  7669	   269	        "positive_net_gain_at_least_8": {"value": net_gain, "pass": net_gain >= 8},
  7670	   270	        "positive_mcnemar_p_below_0_05": {
  7671	   271	            "value": positive["exact_mcnemar_p_two_sided"],
  7672	   272	            "pass": positive["exact_mcnemar_p_two_sided"] < 0.05,
  7673	   273	        },
  7674	   274	        "zero_candidate_only_restraint_false_lists": {
  7675	   275	            "ids": candidate_only_false_lists,
  7676	   276	            "pass": not candidate_only_false_lists,
  7677	   277	        },
  7678	   278	        "candidate_total_false_lists_not_above_baseline": {
  7679	   279	            "baseline": baseline["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
  7680	   280	            "candidate": candidate["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
  7681	   281	            "pass": candidate["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"]
  7682	   282	            <= baseline["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
  7683	   283	        },
  7684	   284	        "item_and_scope_loss_not_increased_per_lane": {
  7685	   285	            "details": loss_checks,
  7686	   286	            "pass": all(item["pass"] for item in loss_checks.values()),
  7687	   287	        },
  7688	   288	    }

  7691	   291	        "mechanical_pass": all(item["pass"] for item in conditions.values()),
  7692	   292	        "semantic_condition": "pending_arm_blind_review",
  7693	   293	        "candidate_advances": False,
  7694	   294	        "candidate_advances_reason": "semantic review is required after mechanical scoring",
  7695	   295	    }

  7748	    38	def normalized(text: str) -> str:
  7749	    39	    value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text).casefold()
  7750	    40	    value = value.replace("’", "'").replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
  7751	    41	    value = re.sub(r"[-_/]", " ", value)
  7752	    42	    value = re.sub(r"[^\w$%.']+", " ", value)
  7753	    43	    return " ".join(value.split())
  7754	    44	
  7755	    45	
  7756	    46	def contains_phrase(text: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
  7757	    47	    haystack = f" {normalized(text)} "
  7758	    48	    needle = normalized(phrase)
  7759	    49	    return bool(needle) and f" {needle} " in haystack
  7760	    50	
  7761	    51	
  7762	    52	def wilson(successes: int, total: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
  7763	    53	    if total == 0:
  7764	    54	        return 0.0, 0.0
  7765	    55	    z = 1.959963984540054
  7766	    56	    p = successes / total
  7767	    57	    denominator = 1 + z * z / total
  7768	    58	    center = (p + z * z / (2 * total)) / denominator
  7769	    59	    margin = z * math.sqrt((p * (1 - p) + z * z / (4 * total)) / total) / denominator
  7770	    60	    return center - margin, center + margin

  7773	    63	def structure_ok(output: str) -> tuple[bool, int, list[str]]:
  7774	    64	    lines = [line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
  7775	    65	    bullets = [line for line in lines if BULLET_RE.match(line)]
  7776	    66	    other = [line for line in lines if not BULLET_RE.match(line)]
  7777	    67	    bare_list = len(lines) == 2 and len(bullets) == 2
  7778	    68	    headed_list = (
  7779	    69	        len(lines) == 3
  7780	    70	        and not BULLET_RE.match(lines[0])
  7781	    71	        and (lines[0].endswith(":") or lines[0].endswith("—"))
  7782	    72	        and all(BULLET_RE.match(line) for line in lines[1:])
  7783	    73	    )
  7784	    74	    return bare_list or headed_list, len(bullets), other

  7840	    40	def wilson(successes: int, total: int) -> list[float]:
  7841	    41	    if total == 0:
  7842	    42	        return [0.0, 0.0]
  7843	    43	    z = 1.959963984540054
  7844	    44	    p = successes / total
  7845	    45	    denominator = 1 + z * z / total
  7846	    46	    center = (p + z * z / (2 * total)) / denominator
  7847	    47	    margin = z * math.sqrt((p * (1 - p) + z * z / (4 * total)) / total) / denominator
  7848	    48	    return [center - margin, center + margin]

  7851	    51	def group(paths: list[Path]) -> dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
  7852	    52	    grouped: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(dict)
  7853	    53	    for path in paths:
  7854	    54	        part = rows(path)
  7855	    55	        if not part:
  7856	    56	            raise ValueError(f"empty candidate file: {path}")
  7857	    57	        model_id = str(part[0].get("model_id", path.stem))
  7858	    58	        for row in part:
  7859	    59	            row_id = str(row["id"])
  7860	    60	            if row_id in grouped[model_id]:
  7861	    61	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate candidate id {row_id!r} for {model_id}")
  7862	    62	            grouped[model_id][row_id] = row
  7863	    63	    return grouped

  7866	    66	def main() -> None:
  7867	    67	    args = parse_args()
  7868	    68	    positive = {str(row["id"]): row for row in rows(args.positive_corpus)}
  7869	    69	    traps = {str(row["id"]): row for row in rows(args.trap_corpus)}
  7870	    70	    positive_groups = group(args.positive_candidates)
  7871	    71	    trap_groups = group(args.trap_candidates)
  7872	    72	    if set(positive_groups) != set(trap_groups):
  7873	    73	        raise ValueError("positive and trap candidate model sets differ")
  7874	    74	
  7875	    75	    report: dict[str, Any] = {
  7876	    76	        "positive_corpus": str(args.positive_corpus),
  7877	    77	        "trap_corpus": str(args.trap_corpus),
  7878	    78	        "models": {},
  7879	    79	    }
  7880	    80	    for model_id in sorted(positive_groups):
  7881	    81	        positive_rows = positive_groups[model_id]
  7882	    82	        trap_rows = trap_groups[model_id]
  7883	    83	        if set(positive_rows) != set(positive):
  7884	    84	            raise ValueError(f"{model_id}: positive IDs do not match corpus")
  7885	    85	        if set(trap_rows) != set(traps):
  7886	    86	            raise ValueError(f"{model_id}: trap IDs do not match corpus")
  7887	    87	
  7888	    88	        positive_details = []
  7889	    89	        for row_id, case in positive.items():
  7890	    90	            count = list_lines(output_text(positive_rows[row_id]))
  7891	    91	            intended = int(case["item_count"])
  7892	    92	            positive_details.append(
  7893	    93	                {
  7894	    94	                    "id": row_id,
  7895	    95	                    "list_lines": count,
  7896	    96	                    "intended_items": intended,
  7897	    97	                    "activated": count >= 2,
  7898	    98	                    "intended_count": count == intended,
  7899	    99	                }
  7900	   100	            )
  7901	   101	        trap_details = []
  7902	   102	        for row_id in traps:
  7903	   103	            count = list_lines(output_text(trap_rows[row_id]))
  7904	   104	            trap_details.append({"id": row_id, "list_lines": count, "false_list": count >= 2})
  7905	   105	
  7906	   106	        activated = sum(item["activated"] for item in positive_details)
  7907	   107	        intended_count = sum(item["intended_count"] for item in positive_details)
  7908	   108	        false_lists = sum(item["false_list"] for item in trap_details)
  7909	   109	        report["models"][model_id] = {
  7910	   110	            "positive_total": len(positive_details),
  7911	   111	            "activated": activated,

  8250	   842	            }
  8251	   843	            comparisons = len(candidate_texts) * len(texts)
  8252	   844	            methods["exact_normalized"] = {"status": "passed" if not exact else "failed", "matches": len(exact), "comparison_count": comparisons, "violation_count": exact_violations}
  8253	   845	            for method, (score, violation_count) in scores.items():
  8254	   846	                if backend_name == "production":
  8255	   847	                    status, threshold = "calibration_required", None
  8256	   848	                else:
  8257	   849	                    threshold = synthetic_thresholds[method]
  8258	   850	                    status = threshold_status(score, threshold)
  8259	   851	                methods[method] = {"status": status, "maximum_score": round(score, 8), "threshold": threshold, "comparison_count": comparisons, "violation_count": violation_count}
  8260	   852	                if method == "embedding_cosine":
  8261	   853	                    methods[method]["comparison_count"] = len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_inputs) + len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_outputs) + len(candidate_inputs) * len(source_outputs) + len(candidate_outputs) * len(source_inputs)
  8262	   854	                    methods[method]["axes"] = {axis: {"maximum_score": round(values[0], 8), "violation_count": values[1], "comparison_count": embedding_axis_counts[axis]} for axis, values in embedding_axes.items()}
  8263	   855	        else:
  8264	   856	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported leakage role: {role}")
  8265	   857	        results.append({"source": source, "methods": methods})
  8266	   858	    all_exact = all(row["methods"]["exact_normalized"]["status"] == "passed" for row in results)
  8267	   859	    if backend_name == "production":
  8268	   860	        overall = "calibration_required_noncertifying" if all_exact else "failed"
  8269	   861	    else:
  8270	   862	        statuses = [method["status"] for row in results for method in row["methods"].values()]
  8271	   863	        overall = "synthetic_not_quality_evidence" if all(value in {"passed", "not_applicable_no_raw_text"} for value in statuses) else "failed"
  8272	   864	    return results, overall

  8301	   120	def load_corpus(path: Path, role: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
  8302	   121	    cases: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
  8303	   122	    for line_number, case in enumerate(read_jsonl(path), 1):
  8304	   123	        case_id = case.get("id")
  8305	   124	        if not isinstance(case_id, str) or not case_id:
  8306	   125	            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{line_number}: missing id")
  8307	   126	        if case_id in cases:
  8308	   127	            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{line_number}: duplicate corpus id {case_id!r}")
  8309	   128	        if (
  8310	   129	            case.get("split") != "dev"
  8311	   130	            or case.get("gold_status") != "candidate_unreviewed"
  8312	   131	            or case.get("native_reviewed") is not False
  8313	   132	            or case.get("training_eligible") is not False
  8314	   133	        ):
  8315	   134	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: corpus is not development/unreviewed/non-training data")
  8316	   135	        if case.get("benchmark_role") != role:
  8317	   136	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: expected benchmark_role {role!r}")
  8318	   137	        for field in ("domain", "case_type", "length_bucket"):
  8319	   138	            if not isinstance(case.get(field), str) or not case[field]:
  8320	   139	                raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: invalid {field}")
  8321	   140	        if not isinstance(case.get("item_count"), int) or case["item_count"] < 1:
  8322	   141	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: invalid item_count")
  8323	   142	        if not isinstance(case.get("compound_required"), bool):
  8324	   143	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: invalid compound_required")
  8325	   144	        for field in ("items", "compound_items", "scope_anchors", "forbidden"):
  8326	   145	            if not isinstance(case.get(field), list) or not all(
  8327	   146	                isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() for value in case[field]
  8328	   147	            ):
  8329	   148	                raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: invalid {field}")
  8330	   149	        if len(case["items"]) != case["item_count"] or not case["scope_anchors"]:
  8331	   150	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: audited item/scope coverage is invalid")
  8332	   151	        normalized_items = {normalized(value) for value in case["items"]}
  8333	   152	        normalized_compounds = {normalized(value) for value in case["compound_items"]}
  8334	   153	        if (
  8335	   154	            len(normalized_items) != case["item_count"]
  8336	   155	            or not normalized_compounds.issubset(normalized_items)
  8337	   156	            or case["compound_required"] != bool(case["compound_items"])
  8338	   157	        ):
  8339	   158	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: audited compound/item contract is invalid")
  8340	   159	        expected_format = case.get("expected_formatting")
  8341	   160	        allowed = {"bullets", "numbered"} if role == "positive_list" else {"prose"}
  8342	   161	        if expected_format not in allowed:
  8343	   162	            raise ValueError(f"{case_id}: invalid expected_formatting {expected_format!r}")
  8344	   163	        cases[case_id] = case
  8345	   164	    return cases

  8349	   168	    value = row.get("output", row.get("candidate"))

  8542	    28	## RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract
  8543	    29	Rule: Shipping EG-1 v2 / EG-2 = upload the new artifact set + license to R2; update `eg1-delivery-manifest.json` with the new revision, per-shard file paths + measured `sizeBytes`/`sha256`, `totalBytes`, and `admission.layout`/`entrypointFile` (this manifest owns hashes/sizes/layout); then update `eg1-manifest.json`'s runtime config to match (`version`, `contextTokens`/`promptTemplateID`/`minAppVersion`/`licenseURL`) — `eg1-manifest.json` no longer carries `sha256`/`sizeBytes` (dead fields removed #1417, see FACT: eg1-artifact-identity). Keep `modelName`/`promptTemplateID` unless the PROMPT changed; bump `minAppVersion` if runtime behavior requires it. Zero code changes unless the prompt template changes (then: new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case + builder; unknown template IDs read RED "app_update_required" in old apps by design).
  8544	    30	Why: `EGOneRuntime` refuses manifests whose `modelName != "eg-1"` (fixed Core literal `LLMProvider.egOneModelName`); `refreshInstalledState` purges the previous version's artifact family automatically (extension-scoped).
  8545	    31	How to apply: R2 upload runbook below; validate the new host object with HEAD (etag+length), a Range request (expect 206), and a full curl+shasum before updating the manifest.
  8546	    32	Ref: #1271 plan §hot-swap; purge added Codex r11.

  8548	    34	## FACT: kill-switch-stops-mutation-not-format-drift (#1386 PR-1, 2026-07-11)
  8549	    35	`modelDelivery.egOne.enabled=false` guarantees exactly ONE thing: no EG-1 model bytes are moved, deleted, or fetched. It does NOT guarantee polish keeps working, and for one cohort it structurally cannot.
  8550	    36	
  8551	    37	A user still on the previously-shipped MONOLITH (`eg-1-v1.gguf`, every release ≤ v2.3.2) holds bytes a sharded build cannot load at all: `EGOneRuntime` boots `manifest.resolvedEntrypointPath` (shard 1), so no directory choice makes a monolith loadable. Turning the switch off therefore leaves that user with raw text (EG-1 is a limb) and their model completely untouched; turning it back on runs the migration and polish returns. Nothing is lost, only deferred.
  8552	    38	
  8553	    39	**Do NOT "fix" this by restoring the monolithic load path.** That means shipping the old manifest AND the old load path alongside the new ones, permanently — dual-format support carried forever for a rollback lever. Rejected on scope (founder 2026-07-11: don't over-engineer). Codex PR-1 review r14 raised it as DIAGNOSIS-ONLY; the resolution is this documented limitation, not code.
  8554	    40	
  8555	    41	Corollary for any FUTURE model-format change (EG-2, a new quantization): the kill switch is a byte-mutation stop, not a version rollback. If a format change ever needs a true rollback, that is a deliberate design (ship both manifests), not something the flag gives you for free.

  8565	    51	## FACT: eg1-shard-authoring-runbook (#1417, 2026-07-08)
  8566	    52	Splitting EG-1 into CDN-cache-eligible shards (each safely under Cloudflare's 512MB ceiling, target ≤450MB per the Phase-3 warn line) reuses `llama.cpp`'s native `gguf-split` tool and the shared delivery engine's existing `componentSet` layout (already proven by Parakeet's 23-file case) — no new reassembly code, no changes to `ManifestFetchTask`/`CacheAdmission`. One-time steps when cutting a new sharded EG-1 revision:
  8567	    53	1. **Split:** run `gguf-split` against the real (unsplit) model weights, choosing `--split-max-tensors` so every output shard lands comfortably under 450MB (shards are NOT byte-range slices — each is an independently-headered valid GGUF file with its own metadata, so per-shard size varies with tensor boundaries, never assume equal division).
  8568	    54	2. **Measure, never assume:** compute each shard's real `sizeBytes`/`sha256` from the actual output files — the manifest's `totalBytes` must equal the measured sum, and every `sizeBytes` must be re-verified ≤450MB after the real split (the pre-split total does not divide evenly by shard count).
  8569	    55	3. **Upload:** each shard to R2 (`r2-hosting-runbook` above) under a NEW versioned sub-path (e.g. `/eg1/v2-sharded/`) — never reuse the legacy single-file path, so the new Cloudflare Cache Rule (scoped to the new sub-path only) can never accidentally match the old monolithic file, which is over the cache-eligible size ceiling.
  8570	    56	4. **Author the manifest:** `admission.layout: "componentSet"`, `admission.entrypointFile` naming the shard `DeliveryManifest.resolvedEntrypointPath`/`EGOneDeliveryAdapter.installedArtifactURL` should boot from (shard 1, by `llama.cpp` convention — it auto-discovers siblings by filename pattern once pointed at shard 1), one `files[]` entry per shard with real measured hash/size.
  8571	    57	5. **Validate before shipping:** every `sizeBytes` ≤450,000,000; `totalBytes` == sum of `files[].sizeBytes`; `entrypointFile` resolves to exactly one `resolvedInstallPath` (enforced by `DeliveryManifest.validateStructure()`, throws otherwise); no duplicate `installPath` values (already enforced); every shard file on disk matches its declared `sha256` before upload.
  8572	    58	6. **Cloudflare Cache Rule + Transform Rule:** scope to `starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/eg1/v2-sharded/")` (or whatever the new sub-path is) — same shape as Parakeet's rule (edge TTL 1y, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, no-transform`). This is a production infra mutation, executed with explicit founder go, separate from the code/manifest change.
  8573	    59	Existing EG-1 installs on the OLD single-file manifest are swept as stale download sidecars by `EGOneDeliveryAdapter.migrateLegacyStoreArtifacts()`'s version-agnostic cleanup and re-download once under the new manifest — the old file stays usable throughout (deleted only after the new N-shard set fully verifies and promotes, via `CacheAdmission`'s existing promote-time orphan cleanup). Full plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1417-2026-07-08-eg1-cdn-sharding.md`.

  8595	    81	**Shipped-config topic_shift regression (2026-07-05, NOT root-caused):** on the Type B 1,890 exam, `topic_shift` (paragraph breaks) scored 97% via the tuning harness but 78% through the shipped engine (−19pp), driving nearly the whole 94.4→93.7 gap (e.g. TS-026/TS-028 emit zero `\n\n` where the tuning outputs broke between topics). Same Q5_K_M model both runs, so the suspect is the SHIPPING RUNTIME config — most likely the q8_0 KV-cache quantization (the 4.1 GB-footprint choice, FACT: eg1-runtime-config) degrading long-range structuring. Clean test = re-run with fp16 KV cache (`--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16`) and see if topic_shift recovers. Possible customer-facing product issue (worse paragraph breaks than the tuned model can deliver); founder to decide whether to chase. Benchmark methodology owner: [polish-eval.md](polish-eval.md).

  8597	    83	## FACT: eg1-list-formatting-trigger
  8598	    84	EG-1 builds a real **bullet list** from a lead-in phrase followed by a natural run of items with **no spoken ordinals** ("the team needs to confirm backups, feature flags, and the traffic drain" → lead-in `:` then one `- item` per line). Spoken ordinals ("first do X, second do Y, third Z") stay INLINE as sentences — the model reads them as sequential steps, not a list. Verified: `scripts/eval/corpus/list_format_v1.jsonl` + the shipped `type-b-1199/eg1_native_shipped_1890` run passed 74/100 list cases with real bullet output on exactly the lead-in-plus-run pattern; a founder demo dictation using "first/second/third" produced inline prose twice (2026-07-05). Implication for demos/marketing: to SHOW EG-1 building a list, script a lead-in + comma-run, never ordinals. Paragraph structuring + self-correction + filler removal work regardless of phrasing. A true marker list is an EG-1 / cloud behavior, NOT an Apple Intelligence one (AFM list detection is run-to-run inconsistent, confirmed live).

  8601	     2	# Model Delivery (epic #1348)
  8602	     3	
  8603	     4	**when:** ANY work touching how model bytes reach a user's machine — Parakeet/WhisperKit/EG-1 downloads, the models.enviouslabs.co mirror, download telemetry, cache validation/repair, first-run model UX, or planning any #1348 phase.
  8604	     5	**why:** the #1339 launch-night incident proved the default model path depended on a borrowed downloader (FluidAudio's → Hugging Face) with no failover/verification/cancel; the founder-ratified pivot is one owned, verified cache-admission layer.
  8605	     6	**Authority:** `docs/model-delivery/model-delivery-contract.md` (LIVE contract, currently v1.2). This knowledge file is the stable pointer + invariants summary; the contract wins where they diverge. Phases 1-3 shipped; Phase 4 WhisperKit convergence remains parked. Durable final artifacts are posted to epic #1348 as comments (one per artifact). At epic completion, promote the final contract INTO this file.
  8606	     7	
  8607	     8	## RULE: model-delivery-contract-is-the-authority
  8608	     9	Rule: Before designing, reviewing, or amending ANYTHING in the delivery layer, read `docs/model-delivery/model-delivery-contract.md`; a plan that needs to deviate amends the contract FIRST, with rationale, and posts the amendment to epic #1348.
  8609	    10	Why: architecture negotiated through PR comments is the failure mode that cost 17 review rounds on EG-1 (#1271) and 7 on the parked PR-2.
  8610	    11	Ref: epic #1348; founder directive 2026-07-06 ("document all of this... in-depth plan phase, large/refactor tier").
  8611	    12	
  8612	    13	## FACT: the-ten-invariants (contract §1, stable)
  8613	    14	1. Verified or absent — no unverified bytes in a final cache path; temp download → SHA-256 BEFORE admission → atomic move.
  8614	    15	2. One writer — single-flight per ModelIdentity; readers only after admission.
  8615	    16	3. Atomic admission — old valid state or new valid state, never a mix.
  8616	    17	4. Manifest-pinned — versioned manifest (files+sizes+SHA-256+source templates); NO runtime listing calls (#1339 failure mode #1).
  8617	    18	5. Cooperative cancellation — typed result, never process kill; no partial in final cache; temp resumable or discardable.
  8618	    19	6. Resumable where possible — URLSession resume data + Range (mirror serves full Range semantics).
  8619	    20	7. Source-aware — our copy (models.enviouslabs.co) first, upstream backup second, per-file failover, order overridable.
  8620	    21	8. Telemetry-complete — every attempt speaks the shared 14 emitted failure classes plus the reserved `constrained_network_deferred` class (contract §7); Ollama included at lifecycle granularity.
  8621	    22	9. Runtime-agnostic — the layer ENDS at a verified cache location; never loads/compiles models.
  8622	    23	10. Deletes old supervision code — net launch-path complexity DOWN per migration PR (deletion ledger is a merge criterion).
  8623	    24	
  8624	    25	Plus (v1.1): manifest trust root — source selection is mutable; expected identity/hash/size is immutable except via trusted app update (bundled pin is the authority; a drifted mirror can never achieve admission). Disk lifecycle — preflight before fetch, stale-version eviction, disk-full is a first-class recoverable failure; constrained/metered-network policy is a deliberate decision, not a default-by-omission.
  8625	    26	
  8626	    27	## FACT: scope-guardrails (founder + CTO agreed, binding)
  8627	    28	Unify ONLY where WE move bytes: Parakeet, WhisperKit, EG-1. Ollama = shared telemetry only (its daemon owns bytes; `OllamaSetupService` commands it). Sparkle = fully out of scope. No god-layer: one fetcher + thin per-backend adapters. The shared `ModelDeliveryController` + `ManifestFetchTask` + `CacheAdmission` engine (`Sources/EnviousWisprModelDelivery/`) generalized the now-retired `EGOneModelStore`'s mechanisms (resume identity, generation tokens, cancel drain-gate, SHA-before-install, disk preflight, stale purge) from one file to manifest sets.

  8638	    39	## FACT: global-edge-caching (#1405, Phase 1 shipped 2026-07-07, Phase 2 shipped 2026-07-08)
  8639	    40	Far-from-origin first-run downloads stalled on single-region R2 with no edge caching (distance, not volume). **Phase 1 SHIPPED** (no app update — reaches installed users): the worker 302-redirects known downloads to the object's native cache-enabled R2 `/parakeet/…` path; caching is scoped to `/parakeet/` only (`/eg1/` and worker paths excluded). Canonical config + verification: `~/.claude/knowledge/infra/cloudflare.md` FACT: model-delivery-edge-caching and `workers/parakeet-mirror/`. **Phase 2 SHIPPED** (PR #1410, `8316bff`, closes #1371): bounded same-source retry + restored the load watchdog (`LoadProgressWatcher`) to LOAD-only supervision (parked during `downloadOwnedPhases`); the fetcher's own 60s idle timeout is the sole download-stall authority — net deletion, no new timeout number. Canonical retry/backoff/timeout/stall behavior: [download-resilience-standards.md](download-resilience-standards.md).
  8640	    41	
  8641	    42	## FACT: install-phase-false-wedge-is-NOT-a-download-problem (#1388, fixed 2026-07-09)
  8642	    43	Do not re-diagnose "Setup is taking longer than expected... check your VPN" (or `wedge_detected` with `observed_phase="Installing model..."`) as a download problem. Production forensics (14d): **117 of 126 wedge fires happened during the CoreML INSTALL (compile) phase**, which runs with networking disabled — every one a false positive. Root cause: the guard's post-signal silence gate ("gate B", `silence > max(floor, 5x maxGap)`) assumes homogeneous work units, but the compile emits ~52 ticks ~1.5s apart (small models) then goes silent for one ~445MB encoder taking ~20x longer — the ratio self-calibrates on the wrong distribution and the 15s floor becomes the sole trigger. Worse, the fire's teardown never resumed the pending load continuation (`ASRManagerProxy`'s invalidation handler didn't touch it), so **119/126 fires reached no terminal outcome** — the launch warm-up silently hung, the guard slot leaked, and users got warm only via the separate onboarding warm-up. #1388 fixed the completion contract (resume-once, typed causes: death → `serviceUnreachable` and the adapter's one-shot retry; cancel → `ASRLoadCancelledError`, non-transport so the retry can't resurrect it), REMOVED gate B from the model-load guard (gate A — the 120s no-signal-at-all deadline — survives, and the Phase-2 download parking (`downloadOwnedPhases`/`wasInDownloadPhase` + boundary reset) is RETAINED because it protects gate A too, not just gate B — without it download ticks satisfy the pre-first-signal deadline and a service that hangs before its first LOAD signal is undetectable (Codex r2 P1); only `transferSilenceFloorSeconds` was deleted as genuinely gate-B-only), added a user Cancel during install (`EngineWarmupOutcome.cancelled`, never a failure), corrected the copy, and added un-truncated install telemetry (`install_duration_ms`/`install_silence_max_ms` on `coldstart.warmup_completed`). Success-duration data justified removal over re-tuning: onboarding warm-up p99.9 = 2080s, so any non-false-firing deadline would exceed ~35 minutes — a give-up policy, not a detector. Plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1388-2026-07-09-install-phase-false-wedge.md` (5 grounded-review rounds). Fault drill: `A11_asr_kill_mid_model_load`.
  8643	    44	
  8644	    45	**Still open (#1405): Phase 3** = object-size guardrail (>512MB fail / >450MB warn) + cache-HIT/per-country monitoring in `verify-deploy.py` + DE canary — not started, low priority (safety-net/monitoring, not user-facing). Plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1405-2026-07-07-model-delivery-global-cdn.md` (Phase 1/2); Phase 2 root-cause pivot plan: `docs/feature-requests/issue-1405-2026-07-08-downloader-owns-stall.md`. Industry-standard retry/backoff/timeout/stall/resume defaults (cited) + how EW maps to them: [download-resilience-standards.md](download-resilience-standards.md) (read before designing ANY retry/timeout value — copy its §1 consensus numbers, do not invent).
  8645	    46	
  8646	    47	**EG-1 CDN sharding — delivery SHIPPED #1417 (2026-07-08), edge-cache rule still pending:** the monolithic ~2.9GB EG-1 was ~5.6x over the 512MB free-tier cache ceiling. #1417 split it into eight independently-verified GGUF shards (each ≤450MB) using the shared engine's `componentSet` admission (`Sources/EnviousWispr/Resources/eg1-delivery-manifest.json`, baseURL `/eg1/`); shard 1 is the runtime entrypoint and llama.cpp auto-discovers the siblings. EG-1 already inherits Phase 2 retry/resume via `ManifestFetchTask` (self-heals like Parakeet), and each shard is now SIZE-eligible for free-tier caching — but the Cloudflare Cache Rule covering the shard path is a separate, founder-gated infra mutation NOT yet deployed (cloudflare.md still scopes caching to `/parakeet/`; `/eg1/` excluded), so EG-1 gets no edge-cache HIT benefit yet. Still single-source (no mirror/backup), unlike Parakeet's mirror+HF failover. Canonical artifact/hosting/authoring: [eg1-operations.md](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity + FACT: eg1-shard-authoring-runbook. Design rationale/history: [eg1-cdn-sharding.md](eg1-cdn-sharding.md). Briefing: `docs/model-delivery/2026-07-08-cdn-caching-briefing.md`.

  8651	## Verdict: PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS
  8652	
  8653	The core experiment is sound. There is no fatal reason to change bases or rebuild the benchmark system. The plan needs revisions before training, mainly because:
  8654	
  8655	- GovInfo is not automatically public domain.
  8656	- VoxPopuli has upstream conditions beyond CC0.
  8657	- FLEURS should remain outside training because it is part of the planned public-speech evaluation lane.
  8658	- The current held-out sets are development sets, not a clean final shipping exam.
  8659	- The plan overstates what the existing generator, leakage scanner, and trainer have already proven.
  8660	- Issue #1570 currently says the 800-case comparison comes before new training.
  8661	
  8662	This is a licensing review, not legal advice.
  8663	
  8664	## 1. Coverage — missing or under-specified
  8665	
  8666	### Finding 1 — The premise claims causation too early
  8667	
  8668	The training skew makes data starvation the best hypothesis. It does not prove that the base-model ceiling is irrelevant.
  8669	
  8670	Drop-in replacement for §1’s final sentence:
  8671	
  8672	> Codex’s overnight scan makes training-data starvation the leading testable hypothesis: list examples are scarce, two-item lists are nearly absent, and prompt-only tuning caused regressions. Retrain #1 tests that hypothesis. It does not yet prove that the Qwen3-4B base has no relevant ceiling.
  8673	
  8674	### Finding 2 — The plan conflicts with the live workflow stage
  8675	
  8676	The current [issue #1570](https://github.com/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/issues/1570) says the common 800-case comparison must happen before balanced training data is created. The plan silently changes that order.
  8677	
  8678	Add after the Preface:
  8679	
  8680	> ## Workflow-stage authority  
  8681	> Issue #1570 currently requires the common 800-case public-speech comparison before new model training. This English retrain may enter Gate 2 only after either:  
  8682	> 1. that comparison is complete; or  
  8683	> 2. the founder posts an explicit sequencing override and updates issue #1570’s acceptance criteria.  
  8684	> Until one of those happens, this plan may complete sourcing, licensing, and corpus design, but it must not start a full training run or make a ship claim.
  8685	
  8686	### Finding 3 — “Real-web-grounded” overstates data quality
  8687	
  8688	OASST is chat/assistant material, not real dictation. Most AMI meetings are role-played design meetings. Common Voice and FLEURS are read speech. These are useful sources, but none directly represents an English power user dictating emails, notes, and lists.
  8689	
  8690	Add to §3.3:
  8691	
  8692	> **Source realism rule:** call this corpus “public-source-grounded,” not “real-dictation-grounded.” OASST supplies chat-style clean text; AMI supplies mostly scenario-based meeting speech; Common Voice and FLEURS supply read speech. Before acceptance, manually audit a stratified sample of at least 100 generated pairs for ASR-reachable input, realistic dictation phrasing, minimal edits, semantic fidelity, and source-style artifacts. Reject and regenerate any stratum with more than 5% material failures.  
  8693	>  
  8694	> Preserve the target persona explicitly: at least 100 of the 1,000 additions must be email-shaped and at least 100 must be note-shaped. These rows remain subject to the same list/restraint balance and preservation rules.
  8695	
  8696	### Finding 4 — Data acceptance and privacy gates are missing
  8697	
  8698	The plan needs source versions, hashes, provenance, source-level deduplication, PII removal, copyright filtering, and medical/legal safety.
  8699	
  8700	Add to §3.3:
  8701	
  8702	> **Pair acceptance contract:** every accepted row records source name, exact release/revision, source document ID, source URL, source-text hash, license snapshot hash, generation-model ID, generation-prompt hash, and stratum. Acceptance requires: source-document deduplication; PII and secret screening; removal of quotations, code, song lyrics, and embedded third-party material unless separately cleared; exact preservation of entities, numbers, dates, negation, scope, attribution, and obligations; no newly generated medical or legal advice; and no teacher commentary or formatting-command residue in the gold output. Both input and output sides are screened.
  8703	
  8704	### Finding 5 — Training-disjoint is not the same as decision-clean
  8705	
  8706	The existing 75+75, positive-100/restraint-100, and two-item sets have been inspected during prompt and diagnosis work. They are useful development gates, but repeated inspection makes them unsuitable as the only final shipping exam.
  8707	
  8708	Add to §11:
  8709	
  8710	> **Development versus release evidence:** the existing English sets remain the development and regression gates. Before training starts, freeze one small final English release set from unused source documents and families using the existing generator, scorer, and blind semantic-review flow—no new custody system. Do not inspect candidate outputs on that set until the training recipe and shipping seed are fixed. The final set must include lists, matched restraint, core cleanup, and email/note dictation.
  8711	
  8712	### Finding 6 — The metrics are not fully defined
  8713	
  8714	“Measurably,” “core polish,” “meaning damage,” and seed selection need precise meanings. The existing A/B scorer already defines a useful primary gate: net gain ≥8, exact McNemar p<0.05, zero new restraint false lists, and no increased item/scope loss.
  8715	
  8716	Replace §11 with:
  8717	
  8718	> ## 11. Testing / eval — predeclared go/no-go bar  
  8719	> Run the exact shipped prompt, chat template, llama.cpp runtime flags, and quantized Q5_K_M artifact. Record prompt hash, GGUF hash, runtime build, and flags.  
  8720	>  
  8721	> **Primary endpoint:** on the existing 75-case positive-list A/B set, candidate strict wins minus losses must be at least 8 and two-sided exact McNemar p must be below 0.05.  
  8722	>  
  8723	> **Mandatory safety gates:**  
  8724	> 1. Two-item activation improves over the current 11/20 result, with no candidate-only item, scope, entity, number, timing, negation, attribution, or obligation loss.  
  8725	> 2. There are zero candidate-only restraint false lists, total false lists do not exceed baseline, and restraint strict score is at least 98/100.  
  8726	> 3. Blind semantic review finds zero candidate-only S3/S4 failures and no increase in S2+ failures.  
  8727	> 4. Core-polish non-inferiority means the lower bound of the paired 95% bootstrap confidence interval for candidate minus baseline is above -2 percentage points on the frozen core-polish set.  
  8728	> 5. The frozen email/note persona slice has no candidate-only S3/S4 damage and no structural regression.  
  8729	>  
  8730	> Train seeds 1265, 1266, and 1267. Seed 1265 is the predeclared shipping candidate; the other two test robustness and may not be used to cherry-pick a winner. All three must clear the safety gates. Only seed 1265 is opened on the final release set, once.
  8731	
  8732	### Finding 7 — Telemetry and rollback are understated
  8733	
  8734	No text-content telemetry should be introduced, but a model revision still needs safe operational monitoring. Rollback is not merely “repoint a manifest”: the manifests are bundled trust roots, so rollback requires another trusted app/manifest update.
  8735	
  8736	Replace §12:
  8737	
  8738	> ## 12. Blast radius, telemetry, and rollback  
  8739	> The artifact change introduces no transcript or list-content telemetry. Existing non-content telemetry must be segmented by model revision and watched for polish completion, local-polish-not-ready, inference failure, timeout, latency, download/admission failure, and user rollback/removal signals.  
  8740	>  
  8741	> Rollback keeps the current artifact revision immutable and available. If the new revision fails, ship an emergency trusted manifest/app update pointing to the prior shard set and hashes. Never overwrite model objects in place or reuse paths with changed bytes. The delivery kill switch stops byte mutation; it is not a model-version rollback.
  8742	
  8743	That matches the live hot-swap contract: new versioned artifacts plus bundled manifest hashes are required ([eg1-operations.md:28](/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/knowledge/eg1-operations.md:28), [model-delivery.md:13](/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/knowledge/model-delivery.md:13)).

  8758	### Exclusions
  8759	
  8760	- **Enron/AESLC: defer is correct.** The AESLC card has no stated license grant, and public disclosure through FERC is not a reusable copyright license. Founder approval alone cannot clear third-party email copyrights or privacy concerns. ([AESLC card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Yale-LILY/aeslc/blob/main/README.md))
  8761	
  8762	- **WikiHow: exclusion is correct, but “do not re-investigate” is too confident.** The official terms page was blocked by robots during this review. The current secondary record says pre-March 24, 2025 text was CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and newer text is proprietary; CC BY-NC-SA expressly prohibits commercial use. Keep it excluded unless an archived official terms snapshot is obtained. ([current licensing record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiHow), [CC BY-NC-SA legal code](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/legalcode.en))
  8763	
  8764	- **Stack Exchange: exclusion is reasonable, but the date claim is wrong.** Public contributions remain CC BY-SA according to contribution date: 2.5 before April 2011, 3.0 through May 1, 2018, and 4.0 afterward. There is no “July 2024 content license” cutoff. Its current AUP separately prohibits automated collection for ML training without written consent. Commercial reuse is possible under CC BY-SA, but attribution/share-alike and access-method risk make exclusion sensible. ([licensing help](https://stackoverflow.com/help/licensing), [AUP](https://stackoverflow.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy))
  8765	
  8766	- **TED-LIUM: RED is correct.** TED says its content is BY-NC-ND: non-commercial and non-derivative. That is incompatible with commercial model training without separate permission. ([TED licensing guidance](https://help.ted.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004233294-How-do-I-license-TED-or-TEDx-content))
  8767	
  8768	### Exact replacement for §3.2’s license language
  8769	
  8770	> **Round #1 licensing rule:** pin the exact source release/revision, download URL, file hashes, and license snapshot before ingestion. A source-level allowlist controls acceptance; a dataset name alone is not proof.  
  8771	>  
  8772	> - **OASST1/OASST2 — GREEN with notice:** Apache-2.0. Carry the license and applicable notices in the training-source notice bundle and model card. Filter quotations, code, PII, and suspected third-party text.  
  8773	> - **AMI — GREEN for covered material only:** use transcription and only annotations explicitly covered by CC BY 4.0. Carry creator/source attribution, license link, and modification notice.  
  8774	> - **VoxPopuli — GREEN with restrictions:** use only VoxPopuli data/transcripts. Do not use its CC BY-NC code, pretrained models, or separately licensed LM data. Carry European Parliament source attribution and the complete source URL.  
  8775	> - **Common Voice CV11–CV16 — GREEN with access conditions:** pin the precise release, accept its repository terms, never attempt speaker identification, strip speaker IDs/demographics, and do not redistribute the raw corpus.  
  8776	> - **FLEURS — LICENSE-GREEN BUT TRAINING-EXCLUDED:** reserve all FLEURS rows for the public-speech evaluation lane so the benchmark remains disjoint.  
  8777	> - **GovInfo — PER-DOCUMENT YELLOW:** accept only material verified as authored by a federal employee within official duties and containing no third-party, contractor, transferred-copyright, covered-faculty, state/local-government, or separately licensed material. Record the originating agency and verification basis per document.  
  8778	>  
  8779	> **Deferred/excluded:** AESLC/Enron requires actual rights clearance; founder approval alone is insufficient. Stack Exchange remains excluded because CC BY-SA attribution/share-alike duties and current automated-ML access restrictions create unnecessary risk; there is no July-2024 content-license cutoff. WikiHow and TED-LIUM remain excluded for non-commercial/no-derivatives restrictions.

  8795	## 4. Q2 repo fact-check
  8796

  8845	## Verdict: PROCEED-WITH-REVISIONS
  8846	
  8847	The core experiment is sound. There is no fatal reason to change bases or rebuild the benchmark system. The plan needs revisions before training, mainly because:
  8848	
  8849	- GovInfo is not automatically public domain.
  8850	- VoxPopuli has upstream conditions beyond CC0.
  8851	- FLEURS should remain outside training because it is part of the planned public-speech evaluation lane.
  8852	- The current held-out sets are development sets, not a clean final shipping exam.
  8853	- The plan overstates what the existing generator, leakage scanner, and trainer have already proven.
  8854	- Issue #1570 currently says the 800-case comparison comes before new training.
  8855	
  8856	This is a licensing review, not legal advice.
  8857	
  8858	## 1. Coverage — missing or under-specified
  8859	
  8860	### Finding 1 — The premise claims causation too early
  8861	
  8862	The training skew makes data starvation the best hypothesis. It does not prove that the base-model ceiling is irrelevant.
  8863	
  8864	Drop-in replacement for §1’s final sentence:
  8865	
  8866	> Codex’s overnight scan makes training-data starvation the leading testable hypothesis: list examples are scarce, two-item lists are nearly absent, and prompt-only tuning caused regressions. Retrain #1 tests that hypothesis. It does not yet prove that the Qwen3-4B base has no relevant ceiling.
  8867	
  8868	### Finding 2 — The plan conflicts with the live workflow stage
  8869	
  8870	The current [issue #1570](https://github.com/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/issues/1570) says the common 800-case comparison must happen before balanced training data is created. The plan silently changes that order.
  8871	
  8872	Add after the Preface:
  8873	
  8874	> ## Workflow-stage authority  
  8875	> Issue #1570 currently requires the common 800-case public-speech comparison before new model training. This English retrain may enter Gate 2 only after either:  
  8876	> 1. that comparison is complete; or  
  8877	> 2. the founder posts an explicit sequencing override and updates issue #1570’s acceptance criteria.  
  8878	> Until one of those happens, this plan may complete sourcing, licensing, and corpus design, but it must not start a full training run or make a ship claim.
  8879	
  8880	### Finding 3 — “Real-web-grounded” overstates data quality
  8881	
  8882	OASST is chat/assistant material, not real dictation. Most AMI meetings are role-played design meetings. Common Voice and FLEURS are read speech. These are useful sources, but none directly represents an English power user dictating emails, notes, and lists.
  8883	
  8884	Add to §3.3:
  8885	
  8886	> **Source realism rule:** call this corpus “public-source-grounded,” not “real-dictation-grounded.” OASST supplies chat-style clean text; AMI supplies mostly scenario-based meeting speech; Common Voice and FLEURS supply read speech. Before acceptance, manually audit a stratified sample of at least 100 generated pairs for ASR-reachable input, realistic dictation phrasing, minimal edits, semantic fidelity, and source-style artifacts. Reject and regenerate any stratum with more than 5% material failures.  
  8887	>  
  8888	> Preserve the target persona explicitly: at least 100 of the 1,000 additions must be email-shaped and at least 100 must be note-shaped. These rows remain subject to the same list/restraint balance and preservation rules.
  8889	
  8890	### Finding 4 — Data acceptance and privacy gates are missing
  8891	
  8892	The plan needs source versions, hashes, provenance, source-level deduplication, PII removal, copyright filtering, and medical/legal safety.
  8893	
  8894	Add to §3.3:
  8895	
  8896	> **Pair acceptance contract:** every accepted row records source name, exact release/revision, source document ID, source URL, source-text hash, license snapshot hash, generation-model ID, generation-prompt hash, and stratum. Acceptance requires: source-document deduplication; PII and secret screening; removal of quotations, code, song lyrics, and embedded third-party material unless separately cleared; exact preservation of entities, numbers, dates, negation, scope, attribution, and obligations; no newly generated medical or legal advice; and no teacher commentary or formatting-command residue in the gold output. Both input and output sides are screened.
  8897	
  8898	### Finding 5 — Training-disjoint is not the same as decision-clean
  8899	
  8900	The existing 75+75, positive-100/restraint-100, and two-item sets have been inspected during prompt and diagnosis work. They are useful development gates, but repeated inspection makes them unsuitable as the only final shipping exam.
  8901	
  8902	Add to §11:
  8903	
  8904	> **Development versus release evidence:** the existing English sets remain the development and regression gates. Before training starts, freeze one small final English release set from unused source documents and families using the existing generator, scorer, and blind semantic-review flow—no new custody system. Do not inspect candidate outputs on that set until the training recipe and shipping seed are fixed. The final set must include lists, matched restraint, core cleanup, and email/note dictation.
  8905	
  8906	### Finding 6 — The metrics are not fully defined
  8907	
  8908	“Measurably,” “core polish,” “meaning damage,” and seed selection need precise meanings. The existing A/B scorer already defines a useful primary gate: net gain ≥8, exact McNemar p<0.05, zero new restraint false lists, and no increased item/scope loss.
  8909	
  8910	Replace §11 with:
  8911	
  8912	> ## 11. Testing / eval — predeclared go/no-go bar  
  8913	> Run the exact shipped prompt, chat template, llama.cpp runtime flags, and quantized Q5_K_M artifact. Record prompt hash, GGUF hash, runtime build, and flags.  
  8914	>  
  8915	> **Primary endpoint:** on the existing 75-case positive-list A/B set, candidate strict wins minus losses must be at least 8 and two-sided exact McNemar p must be below 0.05.  
  8916	>  
  8917	> **Mandatory safety gates:**  
  8918	> 1. Two-item activation improves over the current 11/20 result, with no candidate-only item, scope, entity, number, timing, negation, attribution, or obligation loss.  
  8919	> 2. There are zero candidate-only restraint false lists, total false lists do not exceed baseline, and restraint strict score is at least 98/100.  
  8920	> 3. Blind semantic review finds zero candidate-only S3/S4 failures and no increase in S2+ failures.  
  8921	> 4. Core-polish non-inferiority means the lower bound of the paired 95% bootstrap confidence interval for candidate minus baseline is above -2 percentage points on the frozen core-polish set.  
  8922	> 5. The frozen email/note persona slice has no candidate-only S3/S4 damage and no structural regression.  
  8923	>  
  8924	> Train seeds 1265, 1266, and 1267. Seed 1265 is the predeclared shipping candidate; the other two test robustness and may not be used to cherry-pick a winner. All three must clear the safety gates. Only seed 1265 is opened on the final release set, once.
  8925	
  8926	### Finding 7 — Telemetry and rollback are understated
  8927	
  8928	No text-content telemetry should be introduced, but a model revision still needs safe operational monitoring. Rollback is not merely “repoint a manifest”: the manifests are bundled trust roots, so rollback requires another trusted app/manifest update.
  8929	
  8930	Replace §12:
  8931	
  8932	> ## 12. Blast radius, telemetry, and rollback  
  8933	> The artifact change introduces no transcript or list-content telemetry. Existing non-content telemetry must be segmented by model revision and watched for polish completion, local-polish-not-ready, inference failure, timeout, latency, download/admission failure, and user rollback/removal signals.  
  8934	>  
  8935	> Rollback keeps the current artifact revision immutable and available. If the new revision fails, ship an emergency trusted manifest/app update pointing to the prior shard set and hashes. Never overwrite model objects in place or reuse paths with changed bytes. The delivery kill switch stops byte mutation; it is not a model-version rollback.
  8936	
  8937	That matches the live hot-swap contract: new versioned artifacts plus bundled manifest hashes are required ([eg1-operations.md:28](/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/knowledge/eg1-operations.md:28), [model-delivery.md:13](/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr/.claude/knowledge/model-delivery.md:13)).

However, FLEURS is part of the public-speech evaluation lane. Training on it would contaminate that comparison. Reserve all FLEURS English material for evaluation. ([FLEURS card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/fleurs), [CC BY 4.0 terms](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/deed.en)) |

([GovInfo policy](https://www.govinfo.gov/about/policies), [current 17 U.S.C. §105](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A17+section%3A105+edition%3Aprelim%29)) |

  8952	### Exclusions
  8953	
  8954	- **Enron/AESLC: defer is correct.** The AESLC card has no stated license grant, and public disclosure through FERC is not a reusable copyright license. Founder approval alone cannot clear third-party email copyrights or privacy concerns. ([AESLC card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Yale-LILY/aeslc/blob/main/README.md))
  8955	
  8956	- **WikiHow: exclusion is correct, but “do not re-investigate” is too confident.** The official terms page was blocked by robots during this review. The current secondary record says pre-March 24, 2025 text was CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and newer text is proprietary; CC BY-NC-SA expressly prohibits commercial use. Keep it excluded unless an archived official terms snapshot is obtained. ([current licensing record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiHow), [CC BY-NC-SA legal code](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/legalcode.en))
  8957	
  8958	- **Stack Exchange: exclusion is reasonable, but the date claim is wrong.** Public contributions remain CC BY-SA according to contribution date: 2.5 before April 2011, 3.0 through May 1, 2018, and 4.0 afterward. There is no “July 2024 content license” cutoff. Its current AUP separately prohibits automated collection for ML training without written consent. Commercial reuse is possible under CC BY-SA, but attribution/share-alike and access-method risk make exclusion sensible. ([licensing help](https://stackoverflow.com/help/licensing), [AUP](https://stackoverflow.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy))
  8959	
  8960	- **TED-LIUM: RED is correct.** TED says its content is BY-NC-ND: non-commercial and non-derivative. That is incompatible with commercial model training without separate permission. ([TED licensing guidance](https://help.ted.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004233294-How-do-I-license-TED-or-TEDx-content))
  8961	
  8962	### Exact replacement for §3.2’s license language
  8963	
  8964	> **Round #1 licensing rule:** pin the exact source release/revision, download URL, file hashes, and license snapshot before ingestion. A source-level allowlist controls acceptance; a dataset name alone is not proof.  
  8965	>  
  8966	> - **OASST1/OASST2 — GREEN with notice:** Apache-2.0. Carry the license and applicable notices in the training-source notice bundle and model card. Filter quotations, code, PII, and suspected third-party text.  
  8967	> - **AMI — GREEN for covered material only:** use transcription and only annotations explicitly covered by CC BY 4.0. Carry creator/source attribution, license link, and modification notice.  
  8968	> - **VoxPopuli — GREEN with restrictions:** use only VoxPopuli data/transcripts. Do not use its CC BY-NC code, pretrained models, or separately licensed LM data. Carry European Parliament source attribution and the complete source URL.  
  8969	> - **Common Voice CV11–CV16 — GREEN with access conditions:** pin the precise release, accept its repository terms, never attempt speaker identification, strip speaker IDs/demographics, and do not redistribute the raw corpus.  
  8970	> - **FLEURS — LICENSE-GREEN BUT TRAINING-EXCLUDED:** reserve all FLEURS rows for the public-speech evaluation lane so the benchmark remains disjoint.  
  8971	> - **GovInfo — PER-DOCUMENT YELLOW:** accept only material verified as authored by a federal employee within official duties and containing no third-party, contractor, transferred-copyright, covered-faculty, state/local-government, or separately licensed material. Record the originating agency and verification basis per document.  
  8972	>  
  8973	> **Deferred/excluded:** AESLC/Enron requires actual rights clearance; founder approval alone is insufficient. Stack Exchange remains excluded because CC BY-SA attribution/share-alike duties and current automated-ML access restrictions create unnecessary risk; there is no July-2024 content-license cutoff. WikiHow and TED-LIUM remain excluded for non-commercial/no-derivatives restrictions.

    56	## 0. TL;DR
    57	Fix EG-1's three measured English weaknesses — under-activation of genuine lists (esp. two-item/scoped), leftover spoken-command residue, without breaking its currently-strong restraint — by adding ~1,000 public-source-grounded, balanced English training pairs to the existing set and retraining the SAME base (Qwen3-4B) on the SAME shipped prompt via the documented QLoRA recipe. Grade the quantized artifact on the frozen English sets. Ship as a weights-only EG-1 update if it clears the predeclared bar.
    58	
    59	## 1. Problem
    60	Users report EG-1 is weak at exactly what makes cloud polishers popular: turning spoken lists into clean bullets and formatting email/notes structure. Codex's overnight scan makes training-data starvation the leading testable hypothesis: list examples are scarce, two-item lists are nearly absent, and prompt-only tuning caused regressions. Retrain #1 tests that hypothesis. It does not yet prove that the Qwen3-4B base has no relevant ceiling.
    61	
    62	## 2. Goals & non-goals
    63	### 2.1 Goals
    64	- Raise genuine-list activation (esp. two-item + scoped-implicit) measurably (defined in §11).
    65	- Remove leftover spoken formatting commands.
    66	- Hold restraint (do not convert ordinary prose to lists) — currently ~100%.
    67	- Keep core English polish non-inferior (lower bound > -2pp).
    68	- Keep the same base + same shipped prompt + same download size (~2.7GB) → clean weights-only hot-swap.
    69	
    70	### 2.2 Non-goals
    71	- Multilingual (retrain #2, on top of this).
    72	- Base-model switch (Gemma etc. benched unless this plateaus).
    73	- Prompt-contract change (behavior in weights; promptTemplateID unchanged).
    74	- Building the full public-speech benchmark lab (rejected over-engineering).
    75	
    76	## 2.5 Grounding brief (evidence, read not re-derived)
    77	**Weakness diagnosis (Codex overnight, OVERNIGHT-LOG DATA-004 / EVAL-005/006/007):**
    78	- 259/5,656 training outputs are lists; item skew: 2-item=**3**, 3=179, 4=25, 5=30, 6=2, 7=19, 8=1.
    79	- 80 `LF-*` + 80 `LFT-*` rows leaked from the old benchmark into training → old 94-95% headline is contaminated (82% family overlap), NOT held-out quality.
    80	- Current EG-1 + shipped prompt: positive-list activation 72/100, 71/100 strict; two-item activation 11/20. UNDER-activates.
    81	- Restraint currently strong: 100/100 restraint, 98/100 strict on the 100-trap set.
    82	- Prompt-only "list-v2" boosts activation (86/100) but damages meaning, loses scope, leaves command headers, REGRESSES restraint → behavior must be trained into weights at prompt parity.
    83	
    84	**Training pipeline (eg1-model-provenance, #1265):** Base Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507; QLoRA (Unsloth, r16/a32, lr 5e-5, 2 epochs, response-only loss) on the RTX 4090 ($0); merge → GGUF → Q5_K_M → judge the QUANTIZED artifact. Training prompt MUST equal shipped prompt (drift = ±18pp). Weights-only update keeps promptTemplateID → hot-swap.
    85	
    86	**Ceiling context (Fluid-1 teardown):** competitor ~100k real dictations; realistic internal target 20-50k; per-behavior we are near-zero on lists → high buffer, cheap first win.
    87	
    88	**Single-authority / negative claims:** eval harness `scripts/eval/` is the ONLY polish eval harness (never fork); new data + scorers extend in place. All new training pairs must be family-disjoint from the frozen eval sets (exact + token + char-ngram + embedding screen) — reuse the existing scanner.
    89	
    90	## 3. Design
    91	### 3.1 Approach
    92	Add ~1,000 balanced English pairs (dropping the ~160 leaked `LF-*`/`LFT-*` rows so we don't re-contaminate the eval), retrain per the documented recipe under the CURRENT shipped prompt, quantize, grade on frozen sets.
    93	
    94	New English 1,000 stratification (TRAINING-DATA-DESIGN-V2, adopted):
    95	- 400 positive lists — item counts 2/3/5/7 balanced; list types (explicit bullets, explicit numbering, scoped-implicit, bare-label, correction/format-command) balanced; domains (work, personal, technical, medical, legal) balanced; lengths balanced.
    96	- 400 matched prose-restraint — each paired to a positive family, same domain/length/difficulty; types: incidental enumerations, narrative sequences, compound nouns ("laptop charger"), quoted content, alternatives/contrasts, shared modifiers, two-item policy-boundary prose.
    97	- 200 core polish — filler removal, self-correction, punctuation, entity/number/date preservation, minimal edit.
    98	Persona slice (Finding 3): ≥100 of the 1,000 must be email-shaped and ≥100 note-shaped, under the same list/restraint balance and preservation rules.
    99	
   100	### 3.2 Data sourcing — license rule (Codex web-verified r1; round #1 GREEN-with-conditions only)
   101	Pin the exact source release/revision, download URL, file hashes, and license snapshot before ingestion. A source-level allowlist controls acceptance; a dataset name alone is not proof. Two paradigms: **(A) Degrade** real structured GOLD → synthesize messy spoken input; **(B) Minimal-clean** real spoken transcript INPUT → minimally-edited output that STAYS prose.
   102	
   103	- **OASST1/OASST2 — GREEN with notice:** Apache-2.0. Carry license + applicable NOTICE attribution in the training-source notice bundle and model card. Filter quotations, code, PII, suspected third-party text. (GOLD — lists/emails/steps + prose negatives.)
   104	- **AMI — GREEN for covered material only:** use transcription + only annotations explicitly CC-BY-4.0. Carry creator/source attribution, license link, modification notice. (INPUT — restraint pillar: narrative/incidental/compound.)
   105	- **VoxPopuli — GREEN with restrictions:** use only VoxPopuli DATA/transcripts; NOT its CC-BY-NC code/pretrained models/separately-licensed LM data. Carry European Parliament source attribution + complete source URL (obligation, not request). (INPUT — spoken lists, cleanup.)
   106	- **Common Voice CV11–CV16 — GREEN with access conditions:** pin the precise release, accept its terms, never attempt speaker identification, strip speaker IDs/demographics, do not redistribute the raw corpus. (INPUT — single-sentence prose negatives.)
   107	- **FLEURS — LICENSE-GREEN BUT TRAINING-EXCLUDED:** reserve ALL FLEURS rows for the future public-speech EVAL lane so that benchmark stays disjoint. Not a training source.
   108	- **GovInfo — PER-DOCUMENT YELLOW:** accept only material verified as authored by a federal employee within official duties, containing no third-party/contractor/transferred-copyright/covered-faculty/state-local/separately-licensed material. Record originating agency + verification basis per document. (GOLD — agendas/checklists, used sparingly with per-doc clearance.)
   109	
   110	**Deferred/excluded:** AESLC/Enron requires actual rights clearance (founder approval alone insufficient — third-party email copyright + privacy). Stack Exchange excluded (CC-BY-SA attribution/share-alike + current AUP bars automated ML collection; note: license is by contribution date, there is no July-2024 cutoff). WikiHow excluded (CC-BY-NC-SA, non-commercial). TED-LIUM excluded (BY-NC-ND).
   111	
   112	**Slice → source map (round #1, ~1,000 pairs):**
   113	| Slice | Count | Paradigm | Input | Gold |
   114	|---|---:|---|---|---|
   115	| "Make a list" | 400 | A degrade | synthesized spoken | OASST bullet/numbered answers + per-doc-cleared GovInfo |
   116	| "Keep as prose" (matched restraint) | 400 | B + some A | AMI + VoxPopuli transcripts + OASST prose answers | minimally-cleaned prose |
   117	| General cleanup | 200 | B | Common Voice / VoxPopuli | punctuation + caps normalized |
   118	
   119	**W4 design guard:** the 400 restraint cases must be *matched* to the 400 list cases on surface trigger words ("and","then",commas,"first/second") so the model learns the boundary, not a keyword. AMI is the highest-value negative source.
   120	
   121	### 3.3 Generation + acceptance
   122	**Source realism rule:** call this corpus "public-source-grounded," not "real-dictation-grounded." OASST = chat-style clean text; AMI = mostly scenario-based meeting speech; Common Voice/VoxPopuli = read/formal speech. Before acceptance, manually audit a stratified sample of ≥100 generated pairs for ASR-reachable input, realistic dictation phrasing, minimal edits, semantic fidelity, source-style artifacts. Reject + regenerate any stratum with >5% material failures.
   123	
   124	**Pair acceptance contract:** every accepted row records source name, exact release/revision, source document ID, source URL, source-text hash, license snapshot hash, generation-model ID, generation-prompt hash, and stratum. Acceptance requires: source-document dedup; PII/secret screening; removal of quotations, code, lyrics, embedded third-party material unless separately cleared; exact preservation of entities, numbers, dates, negation, scope, attribution, obligations; no newly generated medical/legal advice; no teacher commentary or formatting-command residue in the gold output. Both input and output sides screened. English needs NO native-human roster (multilingual concern; overnight custody machinery out of scope).
