   210	- **~/Documents/** and **~/Desktop/** — local personal files (iCloud Desktop/Documents sync is OFF)
   211	
   212	## Rules
   213	
   214	Global. Every project. Project CLAUDE.md must not restate — extend or scope only.
   215	
   216	1. **Validate, don't guess.** Run the command, read the file, test the path. No assumptions stated as facts. Production-grade from day one.
   217	2. **Empirical debugging.** Hypothesis → falsifiable test → run → fix. No sweeping changes based on theory.
   218	3. **chrome-devtools-mcp first.** Default driver for any browser work. → [browser-automation.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/browser/browser-automation.md)
   219	4. **DRY.** Every fact lives in one place. Reference, don't restate.
   220	5. **Council when unsure.** Canonical invocation → [llm-council.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/llm-council.md).
   221	6. **No em-dashes or en-dashes in human-facing content.** Marketing, in-app strings, email, Discord, release notes. Use periods, commas, colons, semicolons, parens, or restructure.
   222	7. **Edit in place, never delete-and-recreate.** File ID is a primary key. Deleting breaks share links, permissions, comments, history.
   223	8. **Never ask if done.** Keep working. Saurabh decides when to stop.
   224	9. **Session wind-down.** Local session-log + Discord post via canonical script. Promote persistent infra to CLAUDE.md/knowledge before logging. → [session-wind-down.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/session/session-wind-down.md)
   225	10. **Write for machine reading.** Every token taxes every future session. Optimize for grep retrieval. → [writing-style.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/writing-style.md)
   226	11. **Match existing style; diff every edit.** If diff is larger than the change, stop and investigate.
   227	12. **Discord webhooks: use canonical script; read webhook contract first.** → [discord-webhooks.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/session/discord-webhooks.md)
   228	13. **Plan before non-trivial code.** Don't jump to code on non-trivial work — plan it and get an explicit "go" first; each project's own workflow rules govern how rigorous (council, gates, validation). "Auto mode" after approval grants the full build/test/review loop without check-ins, but never a new design decision — if the design must change, stop and re-approve.
   229	14. **Complete or doesn't ship.** Migrations and refactors ship complete: old code removed and new code wired in the same change, no forwarding shims or "clean up later" follow-ups. Too big to ship complete means split the scope smaller, not the completion.
   230	15. **No unauthorized cloud spend.** Verify with Saurabh before any cloud spend. If a plan requires spend, document the amount and his approval in the written plan to avoid mid-execution blockers.
   231	16. **Don't fake-narrate async work.** Report a terminal status as done; say you're "watching" / "I'll report back" only when a real watcher (ScheduleWakeup, Monitor, non-terminal background task) exists; before promising a result, confirm the watcher notifies on both success and failure. → classification table [async-watchers.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/async-watchers.md)
   232	17. **Grep the knowledge base before researching.** Before researching, reverse-engineering, or building a solution from scratch, grep `~/.claude/knowledge/` and the project's `.claude/knowledge/` — it's very likely already documented. Never answer from training data when a knowledge file covers the topic.
   233	18. **Review to an explicit all-clear before "done."** Self-audit every non-trivial artifact (code, plan, migration) to clean, then run it through the last reviewer (Codex for code/plans) and iterate to an EXPLICIT approval on a confirming re-run — merely folding the previous round's findings is NOT approval. Nothing is done, shipped, deployed, merged, or pushed until that gate passes; a green build or passing live test is necessary but never a substitute for the review sign-off.
   234	19. **No AI attribution in git.** Never add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer to commit messages or a "Generated with Claude Code" line to PR bodies. This OVERRIDES the Claude Code harness default that re-injects those instructions every session (founder decision 2026-07-01). Applies to all projects. Commit/PR content only — unrelated to code comments, which follow surrounding style.
   235	20. **Merge without waiting for the founder (founder rule 2026-07-01, granted outside auto mode).** Once a change has passed its review gates (Rule 18: self-audit + Codex explicit all-clear where the project requires it), merge the PR yourself — including PRs you created — and update local main. Do not park work "awaiting founder merge" or treat merging as needing fresh approval: the review gate IS the approval; merging is mechanical. If a safety layer still blocks a specific merge, surface the exact command for the founder to run once instead of silently waiting.
   236	21. **Proactive over reactive — pave the good road, don't wall the bad one (founder rule 2026-07-02).** When preventing a class of mistake, default to making the correct pattern the effortless, discoverable, copy-paste default so the wrong thing is never authored in the first place; do NOT reach first for a blocking gate/hook/check that stops the work after the energy is already spent. A blocking guardrail is reactive by definition — it interrupts at the finish line and slows shipping — so it is at most a quiet last-ditch net behind the proactive layer, never the primary mechanism. When asked to "add a guard/hook/lint/gate," first ask what would make the mistake impossible-to-write or unnecessary, and lead with that. Applies to all projects; the specific tooling that implements it stays project-local, the principle is global. First instance: the test-timing default — guide [knowledge/dev/test-timing.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/dev/test-timing.md) + the `~/.claude/scripts/test-timing-scan.py` authoring hook (nudges, never a CI wall).

   238	## Scripts & Fast Paths
   239	
   240	High-frequency commands. Depth in the linked file.
   241	
   242	**Pull a secret / API key — GCP Secret Manager.** Prereq: `gcloud --configuration=business auth login --update-adc` (as hello@enviouslabs.co). Inside Claude (`$CLAUDECODE=1`) bare `get-key NAME` is REFUSED — use:
   243	- `~/.claude/bin/get-key --list` — available keys
   244	- `~/.claude/bin/get-key --check NAME` — verify access, exit 0/1, no print
   245	- `~/.claude/bin/get-key fingerprint NAME` — SHA-256, safe to log
   246	- `~/.claude/bin/get-key launch NAME ENV_VAR -- cmd…` — bridge value to a process, no stdout leak
   247	→ [secrets-management.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/secrets-management.md)
   248	
   249	**Cloud credits — AWS Bedrock ($1,120, exp 2028-04) / Azure OpenAI ($5K, exp 2027-01).** Route here before direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Keys via `get-key launch`:
   250	- AWS: `aws-bedrock-access-key-id` + `aws-bedrock-secret-access-key`, region `us-east-1`, model IDs `us.anthropic.*`
   251	- Azure: `azure-openai-endpoint` + `azure-openai-key`; `az` CLI needs `--tenant dcf062e4-4887-4190-b873-579cea214f6c`
   252	→ [cloud-llm-credits.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/cloud-llm-credits.md)
   253	
   254	**Council — GPT + Gemini second opinion.** Always background; one call fires both providers; reuse the `--session` name across rounds (never `-v2`). Absolute paths required. Use for **strategic questions only (1-2 rounds)** — pure reasoning, no repo access. Then ground the strategy against real code with Codex.
   255	- `Bash run_in_background:true ~/.claude/bin/get-key launch gemini-api-key GEMINI_API_KEY -- ~/.claude/bin/get-key launch openai-api-key OPENAI_API_KEY -- ~/.local/bin/council ask --reasoning medium --session <kebab-topic-YYYY-MM-DD> "PROMPT"`
   256	→ [llm-council.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/llm-council.md)
   257	
   258	**Codex — GPT-5.x grounding against real code.** Unlike council (pure reasoning), Codex reads the actual codebase, runs commands, and validates strategy against what's really there. Read [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md) before the first Codex call in a task, including a resume. Flow: council converges on a strategy → hand Codex the plan → it checks feasibility against real files (require file:line citations) → implement. **Default path: run `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec` directly via `Bash run_in_background:true`** (fallback `codex-5.3-spark` if usage-capped — never bare `codex`, never hand-edit `~/.codex/config.toml`'s model default: [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md) RULE: two-named-scripts-not-one-mutable-default) — leaner than the subagent, the output file is yours to read for live progress, and the harness re-invokes you on exit either way (same notification). Reserve the `codex:rescue` subagent for interactive multi-round rescue where you want an agent to iterate with Codex for you. EnviousWispr uses the shell path exclusively. Effort is pinned by the script (sol → medium), prompt via stdin:
   259	- `Bash run_in_background:true` → `cat <prompt-file> | ~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check > <out> 2>&1`
   260	- Multi-round: capture `thread_id` from line 1, then `~/.claude/bin/codex-5.6-sol exec resume <UUID> "delta"` (never fresh `exec` for round 2+). If overriding sandbox, the exec-level flag goes before the subcommand: `exec --sandbox read-only resume <UUID> "delta"`. NEVER shell `&` / `</dev/null`.
   261	→ [codex-cli.md](/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/ai/codex-cli.md)

   384	   192	## Failures and how to do differently
   385	   193	
   386	   194	- Symptom: a review loop drifts toward abstract council opinions and away from the real defect set. Cause: non-grounded review is treated like evidence. Fix: reopen the real files and let file/line grounded review drive plan changes. [Task 3]
   387	   195	- Symptom: the 5b fix starts growing into message, analytics, or dead-mic-versus-quiet-room inference work. Cause: the plan stops being about the concrete zero-sound receipt. Fix: keep the scope on the plain silence fact, the existing capture-session identity, and zero-signal-source retirement only. [Task 2]
   388	   196	- Symptom: multilingual confidence gets overstated from one headline score or a geography proxy. Cause: the harness is English-heavy and production language fields are blank. Fix: build per-language baselines and exact-runtime tests before retraining or shipping claims. [Task 4]
   389	   197	- Symptom: a privacy scrub or corpus refresh makes the EG-1 branch look wildly different from what actually changed. Cause: private-bundle history or renamed provenance paths contaminate the audit. Fix: compare semantic fields before assuming corpus drift, keep private snapshots ignored, and rebuild the public branch cleanly on current `origin/main` when scrub history damages ancestry. [Task 4]
   390	   198	- Symptom: overnight/autopilot research loses experiment history after compaction. Cause: tests and numbers live only in chat. Fix: keep docs/scripts/log artifacts with the exact metrics and commands tried. [Task 4]
   391	   199	- Symptom: a large overnight EG-1 push burns usage/time but still feels like "little visible product progress." Cause: the lane spread across benchmark invalidation, safety proofs, model scouting, and infrastructure before producing a ranked shipping candidate. Fix: present the chronology plainly, separate trust-building work from actual model-improvement work, and stop pretending the artifact volume equals product progress. [Task 4]

   452	/Users/m4pro_sv/.claude/knowledge/infra/aliensv-pc.md:106:- **CRITICAL stability fix #2 — long prompts crash without a seq-len cap (2026-06-24):** training under the full production v38 prompt (~500 tokens/sample) recurrently died mid-run with `RuntimeError: CUDA driver error: device not ready` (no clean OOM, dies at a different step each time — a WSL/CUDA instability under sustained long-sequence load). Fixes that landed a clean 3-epoch run on the FIRST try: `--batch-size 1 --gradient-accumulation-steps 4 --activation-checkpointing --max-sequence-length 1536` (+ `--precision bf16`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`). Short-prompt runs (run3, custom framing) never hit this; only the long v38 prompt did.

   736	    10	## FACT: eg1-headline-what-it-is
   737	    11	| Question | Answer |
   738	    12	|---|---|
   739	    13	| Full fine-tune or LoRA? | **QLoRA** (LoRA on the 4-bit-quantized base) — NOT a full-parameter retrain. |
   740	    14	| Adapter shipped separately? | **No.** The LoRA adapter is **merged back into the base weights**, then converted and quantized; there is no runtime "base + adapter." Physical packaging + the current shard identity are owned by [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity (EG-1 ships as 8 componentSet GGUF shards, #1417 — not one file). |
   741	    15	| Base model | **Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507** (Alibaba, Apache-2.0, the non-thinking variant). |
   742	    16	| Built from scratch? | No. It is a fine-tuned **derivative** of Qwen3-4B — this is why the README says "fine-tuned derivative of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0)" and the EG-1 license applies to the *fine-tuned weights*, not the base. |
   743	    17	| Plain-English framing for Saurabh | "We took Alibaba's Qwen 4B, taught it our dictation-cleanup behavior with a QLoRA fine-tune, and baked the result into one custom model. It's ours, but it stands on an open base." |
   744	    18	
   745	    19	The one-line honest positioning: **"a QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-4B, merged and quantized."** Do NOT claim "full fine-tune" (false — it's LoRA) and do NOT claim "trained our own model from scratch" (false — Qwen3-4B is the base).

   748	    22	Settled by council + Codex (#1265), trained on the RTX 4090:
   749	    23	| Knob | Value |
   750	    24	|---|---|
   751	    25	| Method | QLoRA via **Unsloth** (CUDA-only; does not run on Apple Silicon) |
   752	    26	| LoRA rank / alpha | **r16 / a32** |
   753	    27	| Learning rate | **5e-5** (dropped from the research doc's 2e-4 starting point) |
   754	    28	| Epochs | **2** |
   755	    29	| Loss | **response-only** (loss on the cleaned output, not the transcript/prompt) |
   756	    30	| Target modules | all attention + MLP projections |
   757	    31	| Precision | bf16, adamw_8bit, gradient checkpointing |
   758	    32	| Rig | **AlienSV RTX 4090** (24 GB, WSL2 Ubuntu), always-on via Tailscale. **$0 spend** — owned hardware, no cloud GPU. |
   759	    33	| Division of labor | TRAIN on the PC, EVAL on the Mac (llama.cpp/Ollama + judge harness), ship the merged GGUF back over Tailscale. |

   763	    37	## FACT: eg1-build-pipeline
   764	    38	The end-to-end pipeline (mirror of Fluid-1's exact approach — competitor-proven):
   765	    39	```
   766	    40	QLoRA train (4090)  →  merge adapter into base  →  GGUF convert  →  Q5_K_M quantize  →  judge the QUANTIZED artifact
   767	    41	```
   768	    42	- **Judge the quantized artifact, never the fp16 checkpoint.** The shipped quality number must be measured on exactly the GGUF users run. (Q5_K_M was chosen over Q4_K_M: Q4 scored 86.5% vs Q5 88.8% on the hard-340 at bake-off; the feared Qwen-Q4 collapse did not materialize, but Q5's ~2pp edge + fewer criticals won.)
   769	    43	- Shipped quant: **Q5_K_M, ~2.7–2.9 GB total**. Current sharded artifact identity + exact per-shard SHAs: [`eg1-operations.md`](eg1-operations.md) FACT: eg1-artifact-identity.
   770	    44	
   771	    45	## FACT: eg1-training-data
   772	    46	Two data generations; **v2 is what shipped** (`train_sft_v2.jsonl`, **5,656 pairs**). Format is flat `{id, source, input(raw) → output(cleaned)}` JSONL.
   773	    47	- **v1 (3,036 pairs):** SFT built from 1,549 Type-B-approved rows after excluding the hard-340 IDs/texts, plus founder dictations. The exclusion protected the hard-340 exact cases, not the full 1,890 working set. The 900-case overflow set stayed exact-text sealed but was derived from the same provenance families.
   774	    48	- **v2 = v1 + 1,924 teacher-distilled real dictations** (teacher = gemini-2.5-flash + the v6 cloud prompt; hallucination-filtered, noop-capped) **+ 696 targeted convention drills.**
   775	    49	- **Leakage correction (2026-07-15):** shipping v2 has exact ID and normalized-input overlap with **1,549/1,890** full Type B rows; conservative normalization finds 1,551. Provenance-family components expose 1,866/1,890 approved rows and 899/900 overflow rows. The old zero-overlap statement conflated the protected hard-340/exact-overflow checks with the broader working set. The old 1,890 and overflow scores are historical development/robustness evidence, not held-out quality estimates. Owner receipt: `docs/experiments/eg1-multilingual/OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md` TYPE-B-001.
   776	    50	- **Prompt = training contract:** the model was trained AND ships with ONE fixed short system prompt + `<TRANSCRIPT>…</TRANSCRIPT>` wrapper (`scripts/eval/prompts/eg1-polish-prompt-v1.txt`, pinned by a golden-string test in `EGOnePromptBuilder`). Training prompt MUST equal inference prompt — prompt-shape drift cost ±18pp on the untuned base. This is why EG-1 gets its own `.egOneFixed` prompt family and ignores per-mode prompt rules (behavior is in the weights).
   777	    51	
   778	    52	## FACT: eg1-quality-and-bias-gate
   779	    53	Judge: sonnet-5 `behavior_judge.py --system new`. (Numbers here are the #1265 acceptance run; note the separate marketing-vs-settings discrepancy tracked in `eg1-operations.md` FACT: eg1-quality-perf-baselines — 94.4/94.7 internal vs 93.7 public, same model, different run.)
   780	    54	- **Hard-340 subset:** 94.7%, **0 critical fails** (beat the gpt-4o + v6 cloud champion same-batch: 93.5%, 2 crit).
   781	    55	- **Full 1,890:** 94.4% (traps 97.3%, false-positive 2.4%).
   782	    56	- **Historical one-time bias gate:** exact-text-sealed 900-overflow scored 88.0% vs untuned-base anchor 61.2%; Type-C mixed slice 94.5%; 100 train-excluded real dictations ~95%. This does not prove held-out generalization because the 2026-07-15 provenance audit found 899/900 overflow rows in training-exposed Type B families.
   783	    57	
   784	    58	## FACT: eg1-language-coverage-provenance
   785	    59	- **Trained overwhelmingly on English.** The v2 corpus is English-oriented `raw → cleaned` dictation data, but it is not literally ASCII-only. The historical quality numbers above are English.
   786	    60	- **Base is multilingual** (Qwen3-4B handles ~100+ languages) and the fixed prompt says "keep the same language … never translate," so EG-1 will *accept* and attempt to polish non-English — but that rides on base-model ability, un-benchmarked per-language. Lower-resourced languages will be rougher.
   787	    61	- **Multilingual training pairs are an explicit v3 lever** (epic #1190 follow-ups), not shipped in EG-1 v1/v2.
   788	    62	- Do not conflate with transcription: the ASR engines (Parakeet = English + 24 European; WhisperKit = 99) are a separate stage feeding EG-1 (`architecture.md`).
   789	    63	
   790	    64	## RULE: eg1-retrain-recipe-for-eg2
   791	    65	Rule: To build EG-2 (or EG-1 v3), reuse this exact pipeline — QLoRA (Unsloth, 4090) → merge → GGUF → quantize → judge the quantized artifact against the SEALED holdout — and keep the training prompt byte-identical to the shipped prompt. A PROMPT change means a new `promptTemplateID` + new `PromptFamily` case (see `eg1-operations.md` RULE: eg1-hot-swap-contract); a weights-only update keeps the template id.
   792	    66	Why: prompt-shape drift alone swings quality ±18pp; judging fp16 instead of the quantized GGUF ships a number users never see.
   793	    67	How to apply: expand data on the v2 recipe (synthetic + teacher-distilled real dictations + targeted drills), preserve zero-overlap with the eval, re-run the one-time bias gate on any new data generation, and route any prompt-family change through a code-lane PR. Distribution (R2 upload, manifest bump) is `eg1-operations.md`.
   794	    68	Ref: #1265 method-of-record; #1190 epic.

__DESIGN__
     1	# EG-1 Universal Multilingual Training Data Design V2
     2	
     3	Status: proposed next training lane. Do not launch until the model-blind development corpus is audited and the founder/CTO approves the data budget.
     4	
     5	## Product boundary
     6	
     7	The preferred result is one universal offline model for English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian. One byte-identical shared base plus delta-only LoRA adapters is a fallback only if the universal learning curve plateaus below the per-language gates. An adapter cannot duplicate the base tensors or run independently as a complete model. Requiring one user to install more than one complete base-weight set to enable any two claimed languages is disqualified, regardless of whether a package is called compact, regional, optional, or language-specific.
     8	
     9	## Why the current distribution is insufficient
    10	
    11	The original 5,656-row training set has 259 outputs with at least two list lines. The item-count distribution is badly skewed:
    12	
    13	| List lines | Rows |
    14	|---:|---:|
    15	| 2 | 3 |
    16	| 3 | 179 |
    17	| 4 | 25 |
    18	| 5 | 30 |
    19	| 6 | 2 |
    20	| 7 | 19 |
    21	| 8 | 1 |
    22	
    23	It also contains 80 `LF-*` and 80 `LFT-*` rows copied directly from the old benchmark. The old 94-95% style headline therefore mixes real learning with train/test leakage and does not estimate family-level generalization.
    24	
    25	The first multilingual smoke added only 160 non-English rows, 2.74% of the 5,836-row mixture: 40 synthetic rows each for German, French, Spanish, and Russian, plus 20 synthetic English list rows. Every added row was marked `native_reviewed: false`, and the schema had no domain or high-risk safety stratum. It was a direction screen, not a serious test of universal multilingual capacity. The prompt-aligned Gemma experiment improved Russian but regressed English lists and introduced medical timing damage. That result rejects the exact low-dose recipe, not universal multilingual tuning.
    26	
    27	## Data contract
    28	
    29	Every row must have:
    30	
    31	- a stable semantic-family ID assigned before writing or localization;
    32	- language, domain, behavior, difficulty, and safety-risk labels;
    33	- source and author provenance;
    34	- `native_reviewed` and validator identity/status fields;
    35	- an ASR-style input and one minimally edited gold output;
    36	- explicit required meaning, entity, number, timing, attribution, and formatting checks;
    37	- no semantic/template-family overlap with development or frozen data.
    38	
    39	Training and inference use the same exact prompt hash. If list-v2 is the intended contract, all examples—including replay—must be rendered against list-v2. Do not change prompt text, weights, decoding, and data mixture in the same comparison.
    40	
    41	## Pilot mixture
    42	
    43	Build a 14,656-row first serious pilot before any quarantines/replacements:
    44	
    45	- a 5,656-row English replay pool derived from the original set after removing leaked/unsafe benchmark rows and replacing them with independently authored, family-disjoint rows;
    46	- 1,000 new English rows;
    47	- 2,000 new native-language rows each for German, French, Spanish, and Russian.
    48	
    49	This yields about 45% English and 13.6% for each other language without repeating a tiny non-English set. Exact counts may move after quarantine, but every replacement must preserve the predeclared strata.
    50	
    51	### New English 1,000
    52	
    53	| Stratum | Rows |
    54	|---|---:|
    55	| Core polish and preservation | 200 |
    56	| Positive lists | 400 |
    57	| Matched prose restraint | 400 |
    58	
    59	### Each non-English language 2,000
    60	
    61	| Stratum | Rows |
    62	|---|---:|
    63	| Core polish and preservation | 800 |
    64	| Positive lists | 600 |
    65	| Matched prose restraint | 600 |
    66	
    67	Core polish is balanced across filler removal, self-correction, native morphology, punctuation, entity/number/date preservation, names/code-switching, topic shifts, minimal edit, and mixed behaviors. High-risk medical, legal, and financial rows are present in every behavior family rather than isolated in one small bucket.
    68	
    69	## List and restraint balance
    70	
    71	Within every language's positive-list rows:
    72	
    73	- item counts 2, 3, 5, and 7 are exactly balanced;
    74	- explicit bullets, explicit numbering, scoped implicit tasks, bare-label lists, and correction/format-command cases are exactly balanced;
    75	- work/admin, personal/home, technical/product, medical, and legal/financial domains are exactly balanced;
    76	- short, medium, long, and surrounding-context length buckets are exactly balanced.
    77	
    78	Every positive semantic family has a separately authored restraint family in the same domain and length range. Restraint types cover incidental enumerations, narrative action sequences, compound objects, quoted content, alternatives/contrasts, shared modifiers, and policy-boundary two-item prose. Positive and restraint pairs must share difficulty, not wording or templates.
    79	
    80	Compound nouns and source-wide modifiers are marked explicitly so gold labels cannot split `laptop charger`, `billing copy`, or `evaluation benchmarks`, or attach a shared deadline only to the final bullet. Medical/legal timing, attribution, obligation, identifier, and destination checks are hard gates.
    81	
    82	## Provenance and native review
    83	
    84	- Native-original target: at least 80% per non-English language.
    85	- Cross-language shared concepts: at most 20%, independently rewritten rather than translated templates.
    86	- Native validation: 100% of medical/legal/financial and morphology rows; at least 20% stratified sample of all other rows before smoke training.
    87	- Before release training, every retained row receives native validation or is excluded from release provenance.
    88	- Synthetic author and critic models cannot be the same model/configuration.
    89	- Reviewer disagreements are adjudicated without seeing model outputs.
    90	
    91	## Family separation and leakage controls
    92	
    93	1. Assign family IDs before localization or paraphrasing.
    94	2. Allocate whole families to training, development, or frozen splits.
    95	3. Reject exact normalized input/output duplicates.
    96	4. Reject high token, character n-gram, and embedding similarity across splits.
    97	5. Maintain a blocked-family registry containing the old `LF-*`, `LFT-*`, overflow origins, Russian development/frozen families, multilingual probes, and new benchmark families.
    98	6. Re-run the full leakage audit from raw sources after every corpus merge.
    99	7. Hash and seal frozen corpora before candidate training; never inspect frozen outputs during recipe selection.
   100	
   101	No row can become safe for training merely by paraphrasing a development/frozen family.
   102	
   103	## Staged data-dose experiment
   104	
   105	Do not jump directly to 100,000 rows. Measure a learning curve with nested, family-disjoint additions:
   106	
   107	| Stage | New multilingual rows | Purpose |
   108	|---|---:|---|
   109	| D1 | 2,000 | Detect whether corrected balance moves list and language gates safely |
   110	| D2 | 9,000 | Run the full pilot mixture above |
   111	| D3 | 25,000 | Test whether quality continues improving after the pilot |
   112	| D4 | 50,000 | Scale only when D3 has a positive marginal gain |
   113	| D5 | 100,000+ | Justified only by an unsaturated learning curve and data-quality capacity |
   114	
   115	The row counts are additions before English replay. Each stage is nested by randomly selected semantic families using a recorded seed. Keep optimizer, rank, epochs/tokens, prompt, base, quantization lane, and evaluation constant within the dose comparison. Report both examples and total labeled tokens so longer languages do not silently receive more weight.
   116	
   117	## Ablations
   118	
   119	Run one bounded smoke and one full development benchmark for each predeclared arm:
   120	
   121	1. Core multilingual control with no new list families.
   122	2. Core plus balanced positive lists and matched restraint families.
   123	3. Arm 2 plus the higher data dose only if Arm 2 improves target metrics without English or safety regression.
   124	
   125	Do not run a positive-list-only release candidate; it is an intentionally unsafe distribution. The matched-restraint arm tests whether activation can improve without false lists.
   126	
   127	The initial base comparison is Gemma 4 E4B as the safety-first finalist versus Qwen3.5 as the reserve challenger. Untouched Qwen3 is dropped from this lane after the broader 56-case semantic audit found the most meaning damage. Use the same training families across bases so data and base effects are separable.
   128	
   129	## Reproducibility and statistics
   130	
   131	- Training seed for screening: 1265.
   132	- A development finalist must repeat with three seeds before frozen evaluation.
   133	- Report each seed plus the mean/range; do not average away a damaging run.
   134	- Primary comparisons use per-case paired strict outcomes, exact McNemar tests, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
   135	- Use Holm correction across English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian primary tests.
   136	- English non-inferiority lower bound must remain above -2 percentage points.
   137	- Report core polish, positive-list activation, false-list restraint, and S0-S4 damage separately.
   138	- The exact quantized GGUF through the bundled Mac runtime is the release authority.
   139	
   140	## Promotion and stop rules
   141	
   142	A data stage advances only when:
   143	
   144	- no new S4 meaning/entity/number/timing damage appears on development;
   145	- English meets the predeclared non-inferiority gate;
   146	- positive lists improve without exceeding the false-list gate;
   147	- at least two target non-English languages improve directionally;
   148	- the improvement survives independent semantic review and is not driven by leaked families.
   149	
   150	Stop the lane after one smoke and one full development run when the target metric does not improve or safety regresses. A failed D1 rejects that mixture. It does not prove that a better universal base or higher-quality multilingual corpus cannot work.
   151	
   152	Only one predeclared finalist reaches the sealed frozen benchmark and exact Mac release path.

    29	## FOUNDER CONSTRAINTS
    30	
    31	These are pass/fail requirements, not scoring preferences:
    32	
    33	1. EnviousWispr must work fully offline after the initial model download.
    34	2. Preferred architecture: one multilingual model for all supported languages.
    35	3. Allowed fallback: one shared full base plus small, optional language LoRA adapters.
    36	4. Disqualified: making a user download multiple full-size language models.
    37	5. A larger single universal model is allowed; size is weighted after quality and architecture gates.
    38	6. English remains primary. Initial multilingual priority is English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian.
    39	7. Do not build product packaging or model-selection UI until a candidate beats the benchmark.
    40	8. The larger leakage-clean Type B replacement remains the real gate; a quick pilot must not replace it.
    41	
    42	## WHAT THE 24-HOUR RUN ACTUALLY DELIVERED
    43	
    44	The run built a reproducible research lab and invalidated several bad assumptions. It did not produce a better downloadable model.
    45	
    46	At pause, draft PR #1562 contained 70 commits, 441 changed files, and 86,003 additions. Most of that volume is prompts, manifests, hashes, row-level outputs, scorers, contracts, fixtures, and test receipts. Do not confuse repository volume with product progress.
    47	
    48	## USE AS-IS
    49	
    50	These conclusions are sufficiently supported for future work.
    51	
    52	### 1. The old quality headline is not a held-out real-world score
    53	
    54	- Shipping v2 training overlaps exactly with 1,549/1,890 old Type B rows.
    55	- Conservative normalized overlap is 1,551/1,890.
    56	- Provenance-family exposure is 1,866/1,890; normalized-family exposure is 1,868/1,890.
    57	- The overflow set is also exposed by family on 899/900 rows.
    58	
    59	Decision: never use 93.7%, 94.4%, or the old overflow result as proof of generalization or multilingual quality. They remain historical development results only.
    60	
    61	### 2. Current EG-1's training mixture explains the observed gaps
    62	
    63	- Base: `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`.
    64	- Tune: rank-16 QLoRA, two epochs, 5,656 mostly English examples.
    65	- Only 259 training outputs are lists.
    66	- Only three training outputs are two-item lists.
    67	- The earlier multilingual smoke added only 40 synthetic, non-native-reviewed rows per non-English language. All 160 non-English rows were 2.74% of that mixture.
    68	
    69	Decision: reliable short-list and multilingual behavior cannot be inferred from the current data dose.
    70	
    71	### 3. Prompt-only list tuning is rejected
    72	
    73	Exact Mac shipping-path A/B on 75 new positive-list plus 75 restraint cases:
    74	
    75	| Metric | Shipping prompt | List prompt |
    76	|---|---:|---:|
    77	| List activation | 52/75 | 68/75 |
    78	| Strict positive success | 11/75 | 15/75 |
    79	| False lists | 25/75 | 32/75 |
    80	| Positive scope loss | 15/75 | 23/75 |
    81	| Meaning-damaging outputs | 8/150 | 12/150 |
    82	
    83	- Paired strict gain was four cases, exact McNemar `p=0.125`.
    84	- The sealed gate required at least eight net strict gains and `p<0.05`.
    85	- Six meaning-damaging cases occurred only under the candidate prompt.
    86	
    87	Decision: do not retune or ship the list-v2 prompt. Prompt changes may remain an experiment arm, but targeted training data is required.
    88	
    89	### 4. Several base-model lanes are closed
    90	
    91	| Model | Technical result | Decision |
    92	|---|---|---|
    93	| Qwen3.5-9B | 40/92 strict, 15 damaging, 7/16 Russian, 2/20 two-item, 0/100 broad list activation | Reject |
    94	| Phi-4-mini | 18/56 multilingual; 26/92 damaging, including translations and identifier corruption | Reject |
    95	| Ministral 3 3B | 30/92 strict, 24/56 multilingual, 5/16 Russian, 1/20 two-item | Reject |
    96	| EuroLLM-9B | Internal wrappers leaked in 2/5 smoke outputs | Reject at smoke |
    97	
    98	Decision: do not spend more training or Mac-runtime time on these exact model lanes without new contrary evidence.
    99	
   100	### 5. Adapter storage and runtime are viable as a fallback
   101	
   102	- Current PEFT adapter: 126.1 MiB.
   103	- Converted F16 LoRA GGUF: 63.0 MiB.
   104	- Merged Q5 model: 2.69 GiB.
   105	- One base plus five current-size F16 adapters: about 3.00 GiB.
   106	- Five full models: about 13.45 GiB.
   107	- One selected adapter loaded cleanly with about 79 MiB additional idle memory and sub-second readiness.
   108	- Simultaneously preloading two adapters failed output isolation.
   109	
   110	Decision: if a universal tune fails, the technically viable fallback is one shared base plus exactly one selected adapter loaded at server start, with a local restart when switching. Do not preload multiple active adapters.
   111	
   112	### 6. The exact Mac and evaluation safety gates work
   113	
   114	- Final integrated suite: 587 passed, 2 expected private-data skips, 118 subtests in 126.54 seconds.
   115	- Exact private Mac/MPS fail-closed lifecycle: 1,061.131 seconds, exit 0.
   116	- Production evidence correctly stopped as noncertifying; synthetic evidence correctly stopped as not quality evidence; neither published an evaluation bundle.
   117	- The fresh 75+75 prompt pilot recomputed 5,028,900 leakage comparisons with no exact or high-similarity violations.
   118	
   119	Decision: preserve the exact request path, artifact identity, leakage checks, failure handling, paired scoring, and immutable receipts when simplifying the branch.
   120	
   121	## USE WITH CAVEATS
   122	
   123	These are useful leads or tools, not final conclusions.
   124	
   125	### Gemma 4 E4B
   126	
   127	- Lowest observed meaning damage in the small blind multilingual audit: 1/56.
   128	- Current EG-1 was 8/56; Qwen3.5-4B was 5/56.
   129	- Two trained Gemma recipes were rejected because they introduced scope or medical-timing damage.
   130	- Gemma GGUF experiments were much larger: approximately 5.37-7.48 GiB depending on quantization.
   131	
   132	Use: primary serious balanced-data experiment.
   133	
   134	Caveat: call it the discovery leader, never a winner. Small development samples do not establish release quality.
   135	
   136	### Qwen3.5-4B
   137	
   138	- Small development signal was 5/56 damaging outputs with useful German/grammar behavior but weak lists.
   139	- AlienSV compatibility was proven: 248/248 text modules, all 120 GDN placements, 32,464,896 trainable parameters, one optimizer step in 20.347 seconds, and a 129,927,008-byte adapter.
   140	
   141	Use: reserve universal challenger because it is compact and trainable.
   142	
   143	Caveat: the one-step adapter proves compatibility only. It is not a quality candidate.
   144	
   145	### Language ordering evidence
   146	
   147	- Tiny current-EG-1 diagnostic: German 8/8, French 6/8, Spanish 2/8.
   148	- Russian moved from 3/16 to 7/16 on the same cases when the prompt changed.
   149	
   150	Use: prioritize German after English and keep French, Spanish, and Russian in the first balanced comparison.
   151	
   152	Caveat: no statistically valid five-language ranking exists. The observed order is small-sample and prompt-sensitive.
   153	
   154	### Type B V2 structure
   155	
   156	- The 1,890-slot category/length/tier/trap matrix is preserved.
   157	- It has 23 replacement reserves, 126 packets of 15, and 1,913 custody records.
   158	- The blocked registry contains 11,236 source rows, 7,198 families, and 13,733 normalized text hashes.
   159	
   160	Use: retain the allocation and contamination registry.
   161	
   162	Caveat: the content, public-speech source selection, Type B-specific scorer, and final freeze do not exist.
   163	
   164	### Authoring/calibration machinery
   165	
   166	The 800-row human-authoring, four-role custody, leakage, ratings, power, and calibration paths are technically hardened.
   167	
   168	Use: salvage its immutable-input, family-isolation, rating, and fail-closed patterns.
   169	
   170	Caveat: the founder removed human authors/reviewers as an operational dependency. Do not restart the large human-roster workflow. Adapt the useful controls to licensed public speech.
   171	
   172	## DO NOT USE
   173	
   174	Do not carry these claims or approaches forward:
   175	
   176	- The old 93.7%/94.4% result as held-out accuracy.
   177	- The old Type B or overflow corpora as sealed release benchmarks.
   178	- The list-v2 prompt as a production fix.
   179	- Multiple complete language-specific model downloads.
   180	- Simultaneous multi-adapter preloading in the current llama-server path.
   181	- The human four-role authoring workflow as the current benchmark plan.
   182	- Synthetic or model-judged calibration thresholds as production certification.
   183	- The Qwen3.5 one-step adapter as a trained candidate.
   184	- The 40-rows-per-language smoke as evidence that universal multilingual tuning works or fails.
   185	- Any claim that Gemma has won, German support is proven, or the five languages have a stable quality ranking.
   186	- Any rejected Gemma checkpoint; both failed meaning/scope safety.
   187	- Any repeated prompt hand-tuning on the sealed 75+75 cases.
   188	
   189	## PUBLIC HUMAN-SPEECH BENCHMARK DECISION
   190	
   191	Because native human authors/reviewers are unavailable, use licensed public speech as the next-best reproducible proxy.
   192	
   193	### Common five-language benchmark
   194	
   195	- Backbone: FLEURS plus MINDS-14.
   196	- Languages: EN, DE, FR, ES, RU.
   197	- FLEURS provides broad topics and reference transcripts but is read speech.
   198	- MINDS-14 provides genuinely spoken queries but is banking-only and has no public speaker IDs.
   199	- Run public audio through EnviousWispr's real ASR. The ASR output is the polish input; the public transcript anchors content truth.
   200	
   201	### English Type B replacement
   202	
   203	- Recommended source split: 630 held-out FLEURS units, 630 VoxPopuli units, 630 AMI IHM meeting-speech units.
   204	- Preserve the existing 1,890-case Type B matrix.
   205	- List cases may combine 2-5 held-out speech fragments under predeclared list-cue templates, while keeping every component source family attached for leakage control.
   206	
   207	### Required caveat
   208	
   209	We can prove separation from Envious-held training and evaluation data. We cannot prove that public transcripts were absent from the unknown pretraining corpus of a base model such as Qwen. State this limitation in every release claim.
   210	
   211	## MISSING WORK
   212	
   213	The following deliverables do not exist yet:
   214	
   215	1. Final pinned source/revision/license contract for the web-speech datasets.
   216	2. Tested metadata verifier and ignored audio downloader.
   217	3. Materialized 800-row multilingual development proxy.
   218	4. Sealed minimum 1,600-row multilingual frozen proxy.
   219	5. Public-speech content and dedicated scoring for Type B V2.
   220	6. Comparable vanilla Qwen3, current EG-1, prompt, Gemma, and Qwen3.5 runs on one common development set.
   221	7. A serious balanced training-only corpus.
   222	8. A promoted model candidate.
   223	9. One-time frozen, Type B V2, and exact shipped-Mac finalist results.
   224	10. Production packaging or language-selection UI.
   225	
   226	## SHORTEST SALVAGE PATH
   227	
   228	Do this in order. Do not add more research lanes until this produces comparable model numbers.
   229	
   230	1. Finalize FLEURS + MINDS-14 source revisions, licenses, selection rules, family keys, and source hashes.
   231	2. Materialize development only: 160 cases per language, 800 total. Keep frozen selections committed only by private seed/hash and do not generate candidate outputs for them.
   232	3. Run the 800 public audio cases through the real EnviousWispr ASR path.
   233	4. Compare, on identical inputs and scoring, only these initial arms: vanilla Qwen3, shipping EG-1, the already-rejected prompt as a control, untouched Gemma, and untouched Qwen3.5-4B.
   234	5. Use the result to create one balanced training-only dose covering language, list length, restraint, corrections, identifiers, numbers, medical timing, and no-op preservation.
   235	6. Train exactly two candidates in parallel on AlienSV: Gemma primary and Qwen3.5-4B reserve.
   236	7. For each recipe, run one smoke and one full development benchmark. Stop any recipe that does not improve the target without meaningful safety regressions.
   237	8. Lock one finalist. Only then materialize/open frozen outputs and run the new 1,890-case Type B once.
   238	9. Run the survivor through the quantized exact shipped Mac path.
   239	10. Only after a benchmark win, design packaging or adapter-selection UX.
   240	
   241	## STOP RULES
   242	
   243	- One smoke plus one full development run per exact recipe.
   244	- No repeated tuning against frozen, Type B, or the sealed 75+75 prompt pilot.
   245	- No aggregate headline may hide a failing language or safety slice.
   246	- Meaning, scope, names, identifiers, numbers, negation, corrections, and timing are hard safety gates.
   247	- If neither serious universal tune wins, then test one shared-base-plus-selected-adapter fallback. Do not jump to multiple full models.
   248	
   249	## DEFINITION OF THE NEXT MEANINGFUL RESULT
   250	
   251	The next update should not be another infrastructure count. It should be one comparison table showing the same 800 public-speech development cases run through the five initial arms, with per-language list success, restraint/false-list rate, meaning/scope damage, inference failures, paired uncertainty, exact prompt/artifact identity, and raw-output receipts.
   252	
   253	That table is the decision point for whether to train Gemma, Qwen3.5-4B, both, or neither.

Read this before the 2,049-line chronological log. The purpose is to separate proven evidence from promising hypotheses, infrastructure that can be reused, work that should be discarded, and the shortest path to a measurable model improvement.\n\nRelated records:\n\n- Running tracker: GitHub issue #1364\n- Draft research PR: GitHub PR #1562\n- Branch: `codex/eg1-multilingual-overnight`\n- Full work index: `WORK-INDEX-2026-07-15.md`\n- Full chronological log: `OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md`\n\n## STATUS\n\n- The overnight automation is paused.\n- No training, ASR, benchmark-generation, or model-evaluation process is running.\n- Current EG-1 remains the shipping baseline.\n- There is no release winner.\n- No public-speech audio was downloaded and no web-speech benchmark rows were selected.\n- No frozen benchmark output was opened.\n- The branch was clean and pushed at `e981909a` before this handoff update.\n- PR #1562 is a draft and must not be merged as a product improvement. It is an evidence-heavy research branch.\n\n## FOUNDER CONSTRAINTS\n\nThese are pass/fail requirements, not scoring preferences:\n\n1. EnviousWispr must work fully offline after the initial model download.\n2. Preferred architecture: one multilingual model for all supported languages.\n3. Allowed fallback: one shared full base plus small, optional language LoRA adapters.\n4. Disqualified: making a user download multiple full-size language models.\n5. A larger single universal model is allowed; size is weighted after quality and architecture gates.\n6. English remains primary. Initial multilingual priority is English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian.\n7. Do not build product packaging or model-selection UI until a candidate beats the benchmark.\n8. The larger leakage-clean Type B replacement remains the real gate; a quick pilot must not replace it.\n\n## WHAT THE 24-HOUR RUN ACTUALLY DELIVERED\n\nThe run built a reproducible research lab and invalidated several bad assumptions. It did not produce a better downloadable model.\n\nAt pause, draft PR #1562 contained 70 commits, 441 changed files, and 86,003 additions. Most of that volume is prompts, manifests, hashes, row-level outputs, scorers, contracts, fixtures, and test receipts. Do not confuse repository volume with product progress.\n\n## USE AS-IS\n\nThese conclusions are sufficiently supported for future work.\n\n### 1. The old quality headline is not a held-out real-world score\n\n- Shipping v2 training overlaps exactly with 1,549/1,890 old Type B rows.\n- Conservative normalized overlap is 1,551/1,890.\n- Provenance-family exposure is 1,866/1,890; normalized-family exposure is 1,868/1,890.\n- The overflow set is also exposed by family on 899/900 rows.\n\nDecision: never use 93.7%, 94.4%, or the old overflow result as proof of generalization or multilingual quality. They remain historical development results only.\n\n### 2. Current EG-1's training mixture explains the observed gaps\n\n- Base: `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`.\n- Tune: rank-16 QLoRA, two epochs, 5,656 mostly English examples.\n- Only 259 training outputs are lists.\n- Only three training outputs are two-item lists.\n- The earlier multilingual smoke added only 40 synthetic, non-native-reviewed rows per non-English language. All 160 non-English rows were 2.74% of that mixture.\n\nDecision: reliable short-list and multilingual behavior cannot be inferred from the current data dose.\n\n### 3. Prompt-only list tuning is rejected\n\nExact Mac shipping-path A/B on 75 new positive-list plus 75 restraint cases:\n\n| Metric | Shipping prompt | List prompt |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| List activation | 52/75 | 68/75 |\n| Strict positive success | 11/75 | 15/75 |\n| False lists | 25/75 | 32/75 |\n| Positive scope loss | 15/75 | 23/75 |\n| Meaning-damaging outputs | 8/150 | 12/150 |\n\n- Paired strict gain was four cases, exact McNemar `p=0.125`.\n- The sealed gate required at least eight net strict gains and `p<0.05`.\n- Six meaning-damaging cases occurred only under the candidate prompt.\n\nDecision: do not retune or ship the list-v2 prompt. Prompt changes may remain an experiment arm, but targeted training data is required.\n\n### 4. Several base-model lanes are closed\n\n| Model | Technical result | Decision |\n|---|---|---|\n| Qwen3.5-9B | 40/92 strict, 15 damaging, 7/16 Russian, 2/20 two-item, 0/100 broad list activation | Reject |\n| Phi-4-mini | 18/56 multilingual; 26/92 damaging, including translations and identifier corruption | Reject |\n| Ministral 3 3B | 30/92 strict, 24/56 multilingual, 5/16 Russian, 1/20 two-item | Reject |\n| EuroLLM-9B | Internal wrappers leaked in 2/5 smoke outputs | Reject at smoke |\n\nDecision: do not spend more training or Mac-runtime time on these exact model lanes without new contrary evidence.\n\n### 5. Adapter storage and runtime are viable as a fallback\n\n- Current PEFT adapter: 126.1 MiB.\n- Converted F16 LoRA GGUF: 63.0 MiB.\n- Merged Q5 model: 2.69 GiB.\n- One base plus five current-size F16 adapters: about 3.00 GiB.\n- Five full models: about 13.45 GiB.\n- One selected adapter loaded cleanly with about 79 MiB additional idle memory and sub-second readiness.\n- Simultaneously preloading two adapters failed output isolation.\n\nDecision: if a universal tune fails, the technically viable fallback is one shared base plus exactly one selected adapter loaded at server start, with a local restart when switching. Do not preload multiple active adapters.\n\n### 6. The exact Mac and evaluation safety gates work\n\n- Final integrated suite: 587 passed, 2 expected private-data skips, 118 subtests in 126.54 seconds.\n- Exact private Mac/MPS fail-closed lifecycle: 1,061.131 seconds, exit 0.\n- Production evidence correctly stopped as noncertifying; synthetic evidence correctly stopped as not quality evidence; neither published an evaluation bundle.\n- The fresh 75+75 prompt pilot recomputed 5,028,900 leakage comparisons with no exact or high-similarity violations.\n\nDecision: preserve the exact request path, artifact identity, leakage checks, failure handling, paired scoring, and immutable receipts when simplifying the branch.\n\n## USE WITH CAVEATS\n\nThese are useful leads or tools, not final conclusions.\n\n### Gemma 4 E4B\n\n- Lowest observed meaning damage in the small blind multilingual audit: 1/56.\n- Current EG-1 was 8/56; Qwen3.5-4B was 5/56.\n- Two trained Gemma recipes were rejected because they introduced scope or medical-timing damage.\n- Gemma GGUF experiments were much larger: approximately 5.37-7.48 GiB depending on quantization.\n\nUse: primary serious balanced-data experiment.\n\nCaveat: call it the discovery leader, never a winner. Small development samples do not establish release quality.\n\n### Qwen3.5-4B\n\n- Small development signal was 5/56 damaging outputs with useful German/grammar behavior but weak lists.\n- AlienSV compatibility was proven: 248/248 text modules, all 120 GDN placements, 32,464,896 trainable parameters, one optimizer step in 20.347 seconds, and a 129,927,008-byte adapter.\n\nUse: reserve universal challenger because it is compact and trainable.\n\nCaveat: the one-step adapter proves compatibility only. It is not a quality candidate.\n\n### Language ordering evidence\n\n- Tiny current-EG-1 diagnostic: German 8/8, French 6/8, Spanish 2/8.\n- Russian moved from 3/16 to 7/16 on the same cases when the prompt changed.\n\nUse: prioritize German after English and keep French, Spanish, and Russian in the first balanced comparison.\n\nCaveat: no statistically valid five-language ranking exists. The observed order is small-sample and prompt-sensitive.\n\n### Type B V2 structure\n\n- The 1,890-slot category/length/tier/trap matrix is preserved.\n- It has 23 replacement reserves, 126 packets of 15, and 1,913 custody records.\n- The blocked registry contains 11,236 source rows, 7,198 families, and 13,733 normalized text hashes.\n\nUse: retain the allocation and contamination registry.\n\nCaveat: the content, public-speech source selection, Type B-specific scorer, and final freeze do not exist.\n\n### Authoring/calibration machinery\n\nThe 800-row human-authoring, four-role custody, leakage, ratings, power, and calibration paths are technically hardened.\n\nUse: salvage its immutable-input, family-isolation, rating, and fail-closed patterns.\n\nCaveat: the founder removed human authors/reviewers as an operational dependency. Do not restart the large human-roster workflow. Adapt the useful controls to licensed public speech.\n\n## DO NOT USE\n\nDo not carry these claims or approaches forward:\n\n- The old 93.7%/94.4% result as held-out accuracy.\n- The old Type B or overflow corpora as sealed release benchmarks.\n- The list-v2 prompt as a production fix.\n- Multiple complete language-specific model downloads.\n- Simultaneous multi-adapter preloading in the current llama-server path.\n- The human four-role authoring workflow as the current benchmark plan.\n- Synthetic or model-judged calibration thresholds as production certification.\n- The Qwen3.5 one-step adapter as a trained candidate.\n- The 40-rows-per-language smoke as evidence that universal multilingual tuning works or fails.\n- Any claim that Gemma has won, German support is proven, or the five languages have a stable quality ranking.\n- Any rejected Gemma checkpoint; both failed meaning/scope safety.\n- Any repeated prompt hand-tuning on the sealed 75+75 cases.\n\n## PUBLIC HUMAN-SPEECH BENCHMARK DECISION\n\nBecause native human authors/reviewers are unavailable, use licensed public speech as the next-best reproducible proxy.\n\n### Common five-language benchmark\n\n- Backbone: FLEURS plus MINDS-14.\n- Languages: EN, DE, FR, ES, RU.\n- FLEURS provides broad topics and reference transcripts but is read speech.\n- MINDS-14 provides genuinely spoken queries but is banking-only and has no public speaker IDs.\n- Run public audio through EnviousWispr's real ASR. The ASR output is the polish input; the public transcript anchors content truth.\n\n### English Type B replacement\n\n- Recommended source split: 630 held-out FLEURS units, 630 VoxPopuli units, 630 AMI IHM meeting-speech units.\n- Preserve the existing 1,890-case Type B matrix.\n- List cases may combine 2-5 held-out speech fragments under predeclared list-cue templates, while keeping every component source family attached for leakage control.\n\n### Required caveat\n\nWe can prove separation from Envious-held training and evaluation data. We cannot prove that public transcripts were absent from the unknown pretraining corpus of a base model such as Qwen. State this limitation in every release claim.\n\n## MISSING WORK\n\nThe following deliverables do not exist yet:\n\n1. Final pinned source/revision/license contract for the web-speech datasets.\n2. Tested metadata verifier and ignored audio downloader.\n3. Materialized 800-row multilingual development proxy.\n4. Sealed minimum 1,600-row multilingual frozen proxy.\n5. Public-speech content and dedicated scoring for Type B V2.\n6. Comparable vanilla Qwen3, current EG-1, prompt, Gemma, and Qwen3.5 runs on one common development set.\n7. A serious balanced training-only corpus.\n8. A promoted model candidate.\n9. One-time frozen, Type B V2, and exact shipped-Mac finalist results.\n10. Production packaging or language-selection UI.\n\n## SHORTEST SALVAGE PATH\n\nDo this in order. Do not add more research lanes until this produces comparable model numbers.\n\n1. Finalize FLEURS + MINDS-14 source revisions, licenses, selection rules, family keys, and source hashes.\n2. Materialize development only: 160 cases per language, 800 total. Keep frozen selections committed only by private seed/hash and do not generate candidate outputs for them.\n3. Run the 800 public audio cases through the real EnviousWispr ASR path.\n4. Compare, on identical inputs and scoring, only these initial arms: vanilla Qwen3, shipping EG-1, the already-rejected prompt as a control, untouched Gemma, and untouched Qwen3.5-4B.\n5. Use the result to create one balanced training-only dose covering language, list length, restraint, corrections, identifiers, numbers, medical timing, and no-op preservation.\n6. Train exactly two candidates in parallel on AlienSV: Gemma primary and Qwen3.5-4B reserve.\n7. For each recipe, run one smoke and one full development benchmark. Stop any recipe that does not improve the target without meaningful safety regressions.\n8. Lock one finalist. Only then materialize/open frozen outputs and run the new 1,890-case Type B once.\n9. Run the survivor through the quantized exact shipped Mac path.\n10. Only after a benchmark win, design packaging or adapter-selection UX.\n\n## STOP RULES\n\n- One smoke plus one full development run per exact recipe.\n- No repeated tuning against frozen, Type B, or the sealed 75+75 prompt pilot.\n- No aggregate headline may hide a failing language or safety slice.\n- Meaning, scope, names, identifiers, numbers, negation, corrections, and timing are hard safety gates.\n- If neither serious universal tune wins, then test one shared-base-plus-selected-adapter fallback. Do not jump to multiple full models.\n\n## DEFINITION OF THE NEXT MEANINGFUL RESULT\n\nThe next update should not be another infrastructure count. It should be one comparison table showing the same 800 public-speech development cases run through the five initial arms, with per-language list success, restraint/false-list rate, meaning/scope damage, inference failures, paired uncertainty, exact prompt/artifact identity, and raw-output receipts.\n\nThat table is the decision point for whether to train Gemma, Qwen3.5-4B, both, or neither.\n\n## FILE MAP\n\n| Need | File |\n|---|---|\n| Concise full-run index | `WORK-INDEX-2026-07-15.md` |\n| Founder-readable summary | `FOUNDER-READOUT-2026-07-15.md` |\n| Every chronological experiment receipt | `OVERNIGHT-LOG-2026-07-15.md` |\n| Web-speech benchmark design | `WEB-SPEECH-PROXY-BENCHMARK-V1.md` |\n| Five-language benchmark contract | `MULTILINGUAL-BENCHMARK-V2-SPEC.md` |\n| Training data design | `TRAINING-DATA-DESIGN-V2.md` |\n| Model comparison | `MODEL-SCORECARD-V1.md` |\n| Qwen language evidence | `QWEN3-LANGUAGE-EVIDENCE-AUDIT-2026-07-15.md` |\n| Qwen3.5 LoRA compatibility | `QWEN35-RESERVE-BF16-LORA-PREFLIGHT-2026-07-15.md` |\n\n## BRANCH HANDLING\n\nPR #1562 is too broad to treat as a product PR. Keep it excluded unless an archived official terms snapshot is obtained. ([current licensing record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiHow), [CC BY-NC-SA legal code](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/legalcode.en))
8764:- **Stack Exchange: exclusion is reasonable, but the date claim is wrong.** Public contributions remain CC BY-SA according to contribution date: 2.5 before April 2011, 3.0 through May 1, 2018, and 4.0 afterward. There is no “July 2024 content license” cutoff. Its current AUP separately prohibits automated collection for ML training without written consent. Commercial reuse is possible under CC BY-SA, but attribution/share-alike and access-method risk make exclusion sensible. ([licensing help](https://stackoverflow.com/help/licensing), [AUP](https://stackoverflow.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy))
8766:- **TED-LIUM: RED is correct.** TED says its content is BY-NC-ND: non-commercial and non-derivative. That is incompatible with commercial model training without separate permission. ([TED licensing guidance](https://help.ted.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004233294-How-do-I-license-TED-or-TEDx-content))
8768:### Exact replacement for §3.2’s license language
8770:> **Round #1 licensing rule:** pin the exact source release/revision, download URL, file hashes, and license snapshot before ingestion. A source-level allowlist controls acceptance; a dataset name alone is not proof.  
8772:> - **OASST1/OASST2 — GREEN with notice:** Apache-2.0. Carry the license and applicable notices in the training-source notice bundle and model card. Filter quotations, code, PII, and suspected third-party text.  
8773:> - **AMI — GREEN for covered material only:** use transcription and only annotations explicitly covered by CC BY 4.0. Carry creator/source attribution, license link, and modification notice.  
8774:> - **VoxPopuli — GREEN with restrictions:** use only VoxPopuli data/transcripts. Do not use its CC BY-NC code, pretrained models, or separately licensed LM data. Carry European Parliament source attribution and the complete source URL.  
8777:> - **GovInfo — PER-DOCUMENT YELLOW:** accept only material verified as authored by a federal employee within official duties and containing no third-party, contractor, transferred-copyright, covered-faculty, state/local-government, or separately licensed material. Record the originating agency and verification basis per document.  
8779:> **Deferred/excluded:** AESLC/Enron requires actual rights clearance; founder approval alone is insufficient. Stack Exchange remains excluded because CC BY-SA attribution/share-alike duties and current automated-ML access restrictions create unnecessary risk; there is no July-2024 content-license cutoff. WikiHow and TED-LIUM remain excluded for non-commercial/no-derivatives restrictions.

   100	### 5. Adapter storage and runtime are viable as a fallback
   101	
   102	- Current PEFT adapter: 126.1 MiB.
   103	- Converted F16 LoRA GGUF: 63.0 MiB.
   104	- Merged Q5 model: 2.69 GiB.
   105	- One base plus five current-size F16 adapters: about 3.00 GiB.
   106	- Five full models: about 13.45 GiB.
   107	- One selected adapter loaded cleanly with about 79 MiB additional idle memory and sub-second readiness.
   108	- Simultaneously preloading two adapters failed output isolation.
   109	
   110	Decision: if a universal tune fails, the technically viable fallback is one shared base plus exactly one selected adapter loaded at server start, with a local restart when switching. Do not preload multiple active adapters.
   111	
   112	### 6. The exact Mac and evaluation safety gates work
   113	
   114	- Final integrated suite: 587 passed, 2 expected private-data skips, 118 subtests in 126.54 seconds.
   115	- Exact private Mac/MPS fail-closed lifecycle: 1,061.131 seconds, exit 0.
   116	- Production evidence correctly stopped as noncertifying; synthetic evidence correctly stopped as not quality evidence; neither published an evaluation bundle.
   117	- The fresh 75+75 prompt pilot recomputed 5,028,900 leakage comparisons with no exact or high-similarity violations.
   118	
   119	Decision: preserve the exact request path, artifact identity, leakage checks, failure handling, paired scoring, and immutable receipts when simplifying the branch.

   121	## USE WITH CAVEATS
   122	
   123	These are useful leads or tools, not final conclusions.
   124	
   125	### Gemma 4 E4B
   126	
   127	- Lowest observed meaning damage in the small blind multilingual audit: 1/56.
   128	- Current EG-1 was 8/56; Qwen3.5-4B was 5/56.
   129	- Two trained Gemma recipes were rejected because they introduced scope or medical-timing damage.
   130	- Gemma GGUF experiments were much larger: approximately 5.37-7.48 GiB depending on quantization.
   131	
   132	Use: primary serious balanced-data experiment.
   133	
   134	Caveat: call it the discovery leader, never a winner. Small development samples do not establish release quality.
   135	
   136	### Qwen3.5-4B
   137	
   138	- Small development signal was 5/56 damaging outputs with useful German/grammar behavior but weak lists.
   139	- AlienSV compatibility was proven: 248/248 text modules, all 120 GDN placements, 32,464,896 trainable parameters, one optimizer step in 20.347 seconds, and a 129,927,008-byte adapter.
   140	
   141	Use: reserve universal challenger because it is compact and trainable.
   142	
   143	Caveat: the one-step adapter proves compatibility only. It is not a quality candidate.
   144	
   145	### Language ordering evidence
   146	
   147	- Tiny current-EG-1 diagnostic: German 8/8, French 6/8, Spanish 2/8.
   148	- Russian moved from 3/16 to 7/16 on the same cases when the prompt changed.
   149	
   150	Use: prioritize German after English and keep French, Spanish, and Russian in the first balanced comparison.
   151	
   152	Caveat: no statistically valid five-language ranking exists. The observed order is small-sample and prompt-sensitive.

   155

   190	
   191	Because native human authors/reviewers are unavailable, use licensed public speech as the next-best reproducible proxy.
   192	
   193	### Common five-language benchmark
   194	
   195	- Backbone: FLEURS plus MINDS-14.
   196	- Languages: EN, DE, FR, ES, RU.
   197	- FLEURS provides broad topics and reference transcripts but is read speech.
   198	- MINDS-14 provides genuinely spoken queries but is banking-only and has no public speaker IDs.
   199	- Run public audio through EnviousWispr's real ASR. The ASR output is the polish input; the public transcript anchors content truth.
   200

   202	
   203	- Recommended source split: 630 held-out FLEURS units, 630 VoxPopuli units, 630 AMI IHM meeting-speech units.
   204	- Preserve the existing 1,890-case Type B matrix.
   205	- List cases may combine 2-5 held-out speech fragments under predeclared list-cue templates, while keeping every component source family attached for leakage control.
   206

   208	
   209	We can prove separation from Envious-held training and evaluation data. We cannot prove that public transcripts were absent from the unknown pretraining corpus of a base model such as Qwen. State this limitation in every release claim.

    39	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    40	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    41	    parser.add_argument("--positive-corpus", required=True, type=Path)
    42	    parser.add_argument("--restraint-corpus", required=True, type=Path)
    43	    parser.add_argument("--ab-bundle", required=True, type=Path)
    44	    parser.add_argument("--expected-ab-receipt-sha256", required=True)
    45	    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
    46	    return parser.parse_args()

    49	def sha256_bytes(value: bytes) -> str:
    50	    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()
    51	
    52	
    53	def read_once(path: Path, label: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
    54	    try:
    55	        value = path.read_bytes()
    56	    except OSError as error:
    57	        raise ValueError(f"cannot read {label}") from error
    58	    return value, sha256_bytes(value)
    59	
    60	
    61	def parse_json(value: bytes, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    62	    try:
    63	        parsed = json.loads(value)
    64	    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
    65	        raise ValueError(f"{label} is invalid JSON") from error
    66	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
    67	        raise ValueError(f"{label} is not an object")
    68	    return parsed
    69	
    70	
    71	def require_sha(actual: str, expected: Any, label: str) -> None:
    72	    if not isinstance(expected, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", expected):
    73	        raise ValueError(f"expected {label} SHA-256 is invalid")
    74	    if actual != expected:
    75	        raise ValueError(f"{label} differs from its bound SHA-256")
    76	
    77	
    78	def resolve_recorded_path(value: Any, label: str) -> Path:
    79	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
    80	        raise ValueError(f"{label} path is invalid")
    81	    path = Path(value)
    82	    if path.is_absolute():
    83	        return path
    84	    if ".." in path.parts:
    85	        raise ValueError(f"{label} path escapes the repository")
    86	    return REPO_ROOT / path
    87	
    88	
    89	def direct_child(bundle: Path, value: Any, label: str) -> Path:
    90	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
    91	        raise ValueError(f"{label} path is invalid")
    92	    relative = Path(value)
    93	    if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts or len(relative.parts) != 1:
    94	        raise ValueError(f"{label} path is not a direct bundle child")
    95	    path = bundle / relative
    96	    if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
    97	        raise ValueError(f"{label} is unavailable")
    98	    return path
    99	
   100	
   101	def publish_exclusive(
   102	    path: Path, value: bytes, before_link: Callable[[], None] | None = None
   103	) -> None:
   104	    fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{path.name}.", dir=path.parent)
   105	    temp = Path(temp_name)
   106	    try:
   107	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
   108	            handle.write(value)
   109	            handle.flush()
   110	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   111	        if before_link is not None:
   112	            before_link()
   113	        os.link(temp, path)
   114	    finally:
   115	        temp.unlink(missing_ok=True)

   118	def load_bound_inputs(
   119	    positive: Path,
   120	    restraint: Path,
   121	    bundle: Path,
   122	    expected_ab_receipt_sha: str,
   123	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path, Path, Path, str]:
   124	    ab_receipt_path = bundle / "receipt.json"
   125	    ab_bytes, ab_sha = read_once(ab_receipt_path, "A/B receipt")
   126	    require_sha(ab_sha, expected_ab_receipt_sha, "A/B receipt")
   127	    ab = parse_json(ab_bytes, "A/B receipt")
   128	    validate_noncertifying_ab_runtime_receipt(ab)
   129	
   130	    try:
   131	        provenance = ab["provenance"]
   132	        source_records = provenance["sources"]
   133	        contract_record = source_records["decision_contract"]
   134	    except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:
   135	        raise ValueError("A/B receipt does not bind the decision contract") from error
   136	    contract_path = resolve_recorded_path(
   137	        contract_record.get("path"), "decision contract"
   138	    )
   139	    if contract_path.resolve() != CANONICAL_DECISION_CONTRACT.resolve():
   140	        raise ValueError("A/B receipt does not bind the canonical V2 contract")
   141	    contract_bytes, contract_sha = read_once(contract_path, "decision contract")
   142	    require_sha(contract_sha, contract_record.get("sha256"), "decision contract")
   143	    loaded_bytes, loaded_sha, bindings = load_contract(contract_path)
   144	    if loaded_bytes != contract_bytes or loaded_sha != contract_sha:
   145	        raise RuntimeError("decision contract changed while loading")
   146	    if provenance.get("bindings") != bindings:
   147	        raise ValueError("A/B receipt bindings differ from the executable contract")
   148	    for key, path in (
   149	        ("contract_verifier_sha256", CONTRACT_VERIFIER),
   150	        ("deterministic_scorer_sha256", DETERMINISTIC_SCORER),
   151	        ("ab_scorer_sha256", SCRIPT_PATH),
   152	    ):
   153	        _, actual_sha = read_once(path, key)
   154	        require_binding(bindings, key, actual_sha)
   155	    execution_head = validate_binding_commit(
   156	        bindings, contract_path, REPO_ROOT
   157	    )
   158	    if provenance.get("git_head") != execution_head:
   159	        raise ValueError("A/B receipt Git head differs from the contract binding commit")
   160	
   161	    arm_paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
   162	    for arm in EXPECTED_ARMS:
   163	        try:
   164	            record = ab["arms"][arm]
   165	        except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:
   166	            raise ValueError(f"A/B receipt is missing {arm}") from error
   167	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
   168	            raise ValueError(f"A/B receipt {arm} record is invalid")
   169	        if (
   170	            record.get("inference_error_count") != 0
   171	            or record.get("empty_output_count") != 0
   172	            or record.get("runner_returncode") != 0
   173	            or record.get("row_count") != 150
   174	        ):
   175	            raise ValueError(f"A/B receipt {arm} failed inference health")
   176	        path = direct_child(bundle, record.get("path"), f"{arm} output")
   177	        value, actual_sha = read_once(path, f"{arm} output")
   178	        require_sha(actual_sha, record.get("sha256"), f"{arm} output")
   179	        rows = deterministic.read_jsonl(path)
   180	        if any("model_id" in row for row in rows):
   181	            raise ValueError(f"{arm} output may not override receipt-bound arm identity")
   182	        arm_paths[arm] = path
   183	
   184	    try:
   185	        render_record = ab["provenance"]["render_receipt"]
   186	    except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:
   187	        raise ValueError("A/B receipt does not bind the render receipt") from error
   188	    render_path = resolve_recorded_path(render_record.get("path"), "render receipt")
   189	    render_bytes, render_sha = read_once(render_path, "render receipt")
   190	    require_sha(render_sha, render_record.get("sha256"), "render receipt")
   191	    render = parse_json(render_bytes, "render receipt")
   192	    try:
   193	        render_bindings = render["provenance"]["bindings"]
   194	    except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:
   195	        raise ValueError("render receipt does not carry contract bindings") from error
   196	    if render_bindings != bindings:
   197	        raise ValueError("render receipt bindings differ from the executable contract")
   198	    try:
   199	        positive_source = render["sources"]["positive_corpus"]
   200	        restraint_source = render["sources"]["restraint_corpus"]
   201	    except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:
   202	        raise ValueError("render receipt does not bind both corpora") from error
   203	    for supplied, source, label in (
   204	        (positive, positive_source, "positive corpus"),
   205	        (restraint, restraint_source, "restraint corpus"),
   206	    ):
   207	        recorded = resolve_recorded_path(source.get("path"), label)
   208	        if recorded.resolve() != supplied.resolve():
   209	            raise ValueError(f"supplied {label} is not receipt-bound")
   210	        _, actual_sha = read_once(supplied, label)
   211	        require_sha(actual_sha, source.get("sha256"), label)
   212	
   213	    ab["_verified_contract"] = {
   214	        "path": str(contract_path),
   215	        "sha256": contract_sha,
   216	        "bindings": bindings,
   217	        "git_head": execution_head,
   218	    }
   219	    return ab, arm_paths["baseline"], arm_paths["candidate"], render_path, ab_sha

   222	def role_losses(model: dict[str, Any], role: str, key: str) -> int:
   223	    return sum(
   224	        row["inference_ok"] and not row[key]
   225	        for row in model["case_results"]
   226	        if row["role"] == role
   227	    )

   230	def mechanical_gate(report: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   231	    baseline = report["models"]["baseline"]
   232	    candidate = report["models"]["candidate"]
   233	    comparison = next(
   234	        item
   235	        for item in report["paired_comparisons"]
   236	        if item["left_model"] == "baseline" and item["right_model"] == "candidate"
   237	    )
   238	    positive = comparison["positive_strict"]
   239	    net_gain = positive["right_only"] - positive["left_only"]
   240	    baseline_by_id = {row["id"]: row for row in baseline["case_results"]}
   241	    candidate_by_id = {row["id"]: row for row in candidate["case_results"]}
   242	    restraint_ids = [
   243	        case_id
   244	        for case_id, row in baseline_by_id.items()
   245	        if row["role"] == "prose_restraint"
   246	    ]
   247	    candidate_only_false_lists = [
   248	        case_id
   249	        for case_id in restraint_ids
   250	        if candidate_by_id[case_id]["false_list"] and not baseline_by_id[case_id]["false_list"]
   251	    ]
   252	    loss_checks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   253	    for role in ("positive_list", "prose_restraint"):
   254	        for key in ("items_preserved", "scope_preserved"):
   255	            name = f"{role}.{key.replace('_preserved', '_loss')}"
   256	            baseline_loss = role_losses(baseline, role, key)
   257	            candidate_loss = role_losses(candidate, role, key)
   258	            loss_checks[name] = {
   259	                "baseline": baseline_loss,
   260	                "candidate": candidate_loss,
   261	                "pass": candidate_loss <= baseline_loss,
   262	            }
   263	
   264	    conditions = {
   265	        "both_arms_inference_healthy": {
   266	            "pass": baseline["inference_failure_count"] == 0
   267	            and candidate["inference_failure_count"] == 0,
   268	        },
   269	        "positive_net_gain_at_least_8": {"value": net_gain, "pass": net_gain >= 8},
   270	        "positive_mcnemar_p_below_0_05": {
   271	            "value": positive["exact_mcnemar_p_two_sided"],
   272	            "pass": positive["exact_mcnemar_p_two_sided"] < 0.05,
   273	        },
   274	        "zero_candidate_only_restraint_false_lists": {
   275	            "ids": candidate_only_false_lists,
   276	            "pass": not candidate_only_false_lists,
   277	        },
   278	        "candidate_total_false_lists_not_above_baseline": {
   279	            "baseline": baseline["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
   280	            "candidate": candidate["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
   281	            "pass": candidate["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"]
   282	            <= baseline["restraint"]["false_list"]["successes"],
   283	        },
   284	        "item_and_scope_loss_not_increased_per_lane": {
   285	            "details": loss_checks,
